articles.title: A subgroup of the Baer–Specker group with free dual of uncountable rank
articles.statement:
The Baer–Specker
group $\mathbb{Z}^{\mathbb{N}}$ of all integer sequences has a subgroup $H$ whose dual
$\operatorname{Hom}(H, \mathbb{Z})$ is a free abelian group of rank greater than $\aleph_0$; this
answers Kourovka 17.24 positively.

Bergman's subgroup has dual free abelian of rank $2^{\aleph_0}$.

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Archive of Solved Problems, Problem 17.24 (G. M. Bergman); resolution: G. M. Bergman, More Abelian groups with free duals, Portugaliae Math. 69 (2012), 69-84 (arXiv:1104.3827), abstract (a subgroup of ℤ^ω whose dual Hom(G, ℤ) is free abelian of rank 2^ℵ₀); Kourovka Archive, Problem 17.24 (Yes, it does), https://arxiv.org/abs/1104.3827.

articles.title: Bergman's question on subgroups of the Baer–Specker group (Kourovka 17.24)
articles.statement:
The
proposition that the Baer–Specker group $\mathbb{Z}^{\mathbb{N}}$ of all integer sequences has a
subgroup $H$ whose dual $\operatorname{Hom}(H, \mathbb{Z})$ is a free abelian group of rank
greater than $\aleph_0$.

articles.title: The quotient by a cyclic sublattice is cyclic
articles.statement:
Let $L'$ and $L$ be subgroups of an
abelian group $A$. If $L'$ is a cyclic sublattice of $L$, then the quotient group $L/L'$ is
cyclic.

articles.title: Characterization of cyclic sublattices
articles.statement:
Let $L'$ and $L$ be subgroups of an abelian
group $A$. Then $L'$ is a cyclic sublattice of $L$ if and only if $L' \subseteq L$ and the
quotient group $L/(L' \cap L)$, with $L' \cap L$ regarded as a subgroup of $L$, is cyclic.

articles.title: Cyclic sublattice of a subgroup
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be an abelian group and let $L'$ and $L$ be
subgroups of $A$. Then $L'$ is a cyclic sublattice of $L$ when $L' \subseteq L$ and the quotient
group $L/L'$ is cyclic; formally the quotient is taken by $L' \cap L$, regarded as a subgroup
of $L$.

articles.title: A cyclic sublattice is contained in its ambient subgroup
articles.statement:
Let $L'$ and $L$ be subgroups
of an abelian group $A$. If $L'$ is a cyclic sublattice of $L$, then $L' \subseteq L$.

articles.title: Criterion for a cyclic sublattice
articles.statement:
Let $L'$ and $L$ be subgroups of an abelian group $A$.
If $L' \subseteq L$ and the quotient group $L/L'$ is cyclic, then $L'$ is a cyclic sublattice
of $L$.

articles.title: Torsion-free abelian group
articles.statement:
An abelian group $A$, written additively, is torsion-free when
for every natural number $n \ne 0$ and every $a \in A$, $n a = 0$ implies $a = 0$.

articles.title: Failure of direct-summand absorption with isomorphic summands
articles.statement:
There exist torsion-free abelian
groups $A$, $B$, $C$ with $B \cong C$ and $A \cong A \oplus B \oplus C$ but
$A \not\cong A \oplus B$; thus the answer to Kourovka Problem 17.21(b) is negative.

The Kourovka Archive answers 17.21(b) negatively as well ("even in case b)", Corner 1964; Bergman,
letter of 2011).

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Archive of Solved Problems, Problem 17.21 (G. M. Bergman); resolution: A. L. S. Corner, in Proc. Colloq. Abelian Groups (Tihany, 1963), Budapest, 1964, 43-48; G. M. Bergman, letter of 20 February 2011, as recorded in the Kourovka Archive, Kourovka Archive, Problem 17.21 (No, not necessarily, even in case b); see Corner (1964); Bergman also has an example with B and C of rank 1).

articles.title: Bergman's absorption question for isomorphic summands (Kourovka 17.21(b))
articles.statement:
The statement
that for all torsion-free abelian groups $A$, $B$, $C$ with $B \cong C$, if
$A \cong A \oplus B \oplus C$ then $A \cong A \oplus B$.

articles.title: Failure of direct-summand absorption for torsion-free abelian groups
articles.statement:
There exist torsion-free
abelian groups $A$, $B$, $C$ with $A \cong A \oplus B \oplus C$ but $A \not\cong A \oplus B$; thus
the answer to Kourovka Problem 17.21(a) is negative.

The Kourovka Archive answers 17.21 "No, not necessarily, even in case b)", citing Corner (1964)
and Bergman (letter of 2011, an example with $B$ and $C$ of rank 1).

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Archive of Solved Problems, Problem 17.21 (G. M. Bergman); resolution: A. L. S. Corner, in Proc. Colloq. Abelian Groups (Tihany, 1963), Budapest, 1964, 43-48; G. M. Bergman, letter of 20 February 2011, as recorded in the Kourovka Archive, Kourovka Archive, Problem 17.21 (No, not necessarily, even in case b); see Corner (1964); Bergman also has an example with B and C of rank 1).

articles.title: Bergman's absorption question (Kourovka 17.21(a))
articles.statement:
The statement that for all torsion-free
abelian groups $A$, $B$, $C$, if $A \cong A \oplus B \oplus C$ then $A \cong A \oplus B$.

articles.title: Characters of a product of abelian groups
articles.statement:
For all abelian groups $A$ and $B$, the group of
characters of $A \times B$ is isomorphic to the product of the character groups of $A$ and $B$.
Here a character of $A$ is a map $\chi : A \to \mathbb{C}$ with $\chi(0) = 1$ and
$\chi(a + a') = \chi(a)\chi(a')$ for all $a, a' \in A$, and the characters of $A$ form a group
under pointwise multiplication.

Proof: Restrict a character along the two coordinate inclusions, with inverse
$(\chi_1, \chi_2) \mapsto ((x, y) \mapsto \chi_1(x)\chi_2(y))$. Conrad's Lemma 3.12 uses the
same restriction map for finite groups and concludes by counting; the explicit
inverse removes the finiteness assumption.

## Sources

- K. Conrad, Characters of finite abelian groups, https://kconrad.math.uconn.edu/blurbs/grouptheory/charthy.pdf, Lemma 3.12.

articles.title: A finite abelian group is isomorphic to its dual group
articles.statement:
Every finite abelian group $A$ is
isomorphic to its dual group, the group of characters of $A$ under pointwise multiplication,
where a character of $A$ is a map $\chi : A \to \mathbb{C}$ with $\chi(0) = 1$ and
$\chi(a + a') = \chi(a)\chi(a')$ for all $a, a' \in A$.

Proof: Use the structure theorem to write $A$ as a direct sum of finite cyclic groups,
identify each cyclic group $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ with its dual group, and transport
characters along the decomposition. This is the proof of Conrad's Theorem 3.13: the cyclic
case, then products of cyclic groups.

## Sources

- K. Conrad, Characters of finite abelian groups, https://kconrad.math.uconn.edu/blurbs/grouptheory/charthy.pdf, Theorem 3.13.

articles.title: Abelian images of products of finite groups
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be an abelian group. If $A$ is a
homomorphic image of a direct product $\prod_{i \in I} G_i$ of an infinite family $(G_i)_{i \in I}$
of finite (not necessarily abelian) groups, then $A$ is a homomorphic image of the direct product
$\prod_{j \in J} H_j$ of some family $(H_j)_{j \in J}$ of finite abelian groups.

Corson proves more: such an $A$ is a homomorphic image of a direct product of finite cyclic groups.

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Problem 20.13 (G. M. Bergman); resolution: S. M. Corson, On homomorphic images of ultraproducts, preprint, arXiv:2503.09228 (2025), Theorem 17 with Proposition 10: an abelian group is cotorsion iff it is an image of (∏ G_i)/(⊕ G_i) for some sequence of groups, iff an image of a product of finite cyclic groups, iff an image of a product of finite groups, and cotorsion groups are images of nonprincipal ultraproducts of abelian groups; Questions 1 and 2 (Kourovka 20.13(a), (b)) are answered affirmatively, https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.09228.

articles.title: Kourovka Problem 20.13(b) (Bergman)
articles.statement:
The proposition that every abelian group $A$ that is a
homomorphic image of a direct product $\prod_{i \in I} G_i$ of an infinite family $(G_i)_{i \in I}$
of finite (not necessarily abelian) groups is also a homomorphic image of the direct product
$\prod_{j \in J} H_j$ of some family $(H_j)_{j \in J}$ of finite abelian groups.

articles.title: Abelian images of ultraproducts are images of abelian ultraproducts
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be an abelian
group, let $(G_i)_{i \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence of (not necessarily abelian) groups, and let $U$
be a nonprincipal ultrafilter on $\mathbb{N}$, that is, one containing every cofinite set. If there
is a surjective homomorphism from the ultraproduct $\left(\prod_i G_i\right)/U$ onto $A$, then there
are a sequence $(H_i)_{i \in \mathbb{N}}$ of abelian groups and a nonprincipal ultrafilter $V$ on
$\mathbb{N}$ with a surjective homomorphism from $\left(\prod_i H_i\right)/V$ onto $A$.

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Problem 20.13 (G. M. Bergman); resolution: S. M. Corson, On homomorphic images of ultraproducts, preprint, arXiv:2503.09228 (2025), Theorem 17 with Proposition 10: an abelian group is cotorsion iff it is an image of (∏ G_i)/(⊕ G_i) for some sequence of groups, iff an image of a product of finite cyclic groups, iff an image of a product of finite groups, and cotorsion groups are images of nonprincipal ultraproducts of abelian groups; Questions 1 and 2 (Kourovka 20.13(a), (b)) are answered affirmatively, https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.09228.

articles.title: Kourovka Problem 20.13(a) (Bergman)
articles.statement:
The proposition that for every abelian group $A$, every
sequence $(G_i)_{i \in \mathbb{N}}$ of (not necessarily abelian) groups and every nonprincipal
ultrafilter $U$ on $\mathbb{N}$ (one containing every cofinite set), if there is a surjective
homomorphism from the ultraproduct $\left(\prod_i G_i\right)/U$ onto $A$, then there are a sequence
$(H_i)_{i \in \mathbb{N}}$ of abelian groups and a nonprincipal ultrafilter $V$ on $\mathbb{N}$
with a surjective homomorphism from $\left(\prod_i H_i\right)/V$ onto $A$.

articles.title: Groups locally an image of the ultrapower $\mathbb{Z}^{\mathbb{N}}/U$
articles.statement:
Let $U$ be an
ultrafilter on $\mathbb{N}$ and $B$ a group. Then $B$ is locally an image of the ultrapower
$\mathbb{Z}^{\mathbb{N}}/U$ when every element $b \in B$ lies in a subgroup $H$ of $B$ that is a
homomorphic image of $\mathbb{Z}^{\mathbb{N}}/U$: there is a surjective homomorphism $\psi$ from
the additive group $\mathbb{Z}^{\mathbb{N}}$ of integer sequences onto $H$ such that $\psi(f) = 1$
for every sequence $f$ with $f_i = 0$ for $U$-almost every $i$.

articles.title: Bergman's question 21.12 has a negative answer
articles.statement:
For every nonprincipal ultrafilter $U$
on $\mathbb{N}$ there is a group $B$ that is locally an image of the ultrapower
$\mathbb{Z}^{\mathbb{N}}/U$ (every element of $B$ lies in a subgroup of $B$ that is a homomorphic
image of $\mathbb{Z}^{\mathbb{N}}/U$) but is not a homomorphic image of any ultraproduct
$(\prod_{i \in \mathbb{N}} G_i)/U$ of groups: for no groups $G_i$, $i \in \mathbb{N}$, is there a
surjective homomorphism $\varphi \colon \prod_i G_i \to B$ with $\varphi(f) = 1$ for every family
$f$ such that $f_i = 1$ for $U$-almost every $i$.

Corson shows that the abelian group $\bigoplus_n C_n$, with $C_n$ finite cyclic of unbounded
orders, is such a group for every nonprincipal $U$: it is not a homomorphic image of any
nonprincipal countable ultraproduct. The Kourovka Notebook marks 21.12 solved ("No, it need not").

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Problem 21.12 (G. M. Bergman); resolution: S. M. Corson, On homomorphic images of ultraproducts, J. Algebra 681 (2025), 306-317, arXiv:2503.09228, Section 2, proof of the negative answer to Question 3 (Bergman's Question 19): for every nonprincipal ultrafilter U on ω the group ⊕ₙ Cₙ, Cₙ finite cyclic of unbounded orders, has each element in a homomorphic image of (∏ ℤ)/U but is not a homomorphic image of any nonprincipal ultraproduct (∏ Gᵢ)/V; Kourovka Notebook (21st issue), Problem 21.12: No, it need not, https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.09228.

articles.title: Bergman's question on images of countable ultraproducts (Kourovka 21.12)
articles.statement:
There is a
nonprincipal ultrafilter $U$ on $\mathbb{N}$ such that every group $B$ that is locally an image of
the ultrapower $\mathbb{Z}^{\mathbb{N}}/U$ (every element of $B$ lies in a subgroup of $B$ that is
a homomorphic image of $\mathbb{Z}^{\mathbb{N}}/U$) is a homomorphic image of an ultraproduct
$(\prod_{i \in \mathbb{N}} G_i)/U$: there are groups $G_i$, $i \in \mathbb{N}$, and a surjective
homomorphism $\varphi \colon \prod_i G_i \to B$ such that $\varphi(f) = 1$ for every family $f$
with $f_i = 1$ for $U$-almost every $i$.

The question is posed for a fixed nonprincipal $U$; it is stated here for some $U$, so that its
refutation covers every $U$.

articles.title: Ultraproduct kernel
articles.statement:
For an ultrafilter $U$ on $\mathbb{N}$ and a sequence
$(G_i)_{i \in \mathbb{N}}$ of groups, the normal subgroup of $\prod_i G_i$ generated by the
sequences $(g_i)_i$ with $\{i : g_i = 1\} \in U$. These sequences already form a normal subgroup,
so the kernel consists of exactly them.

articles.title: Ultraproduct of a sequence of groups
articles.statement:
For an ultrafilter $U$ on $\mathbb{N}$ and a sequence
$(G_i)_{i \in \mathbb{N}}$ of groups, the ultraproduct $\left(\prod_i G_i\right)/U$ is the quotient
of the direct product $\prod_i G_i$ by the ultraproduct kernel, the normal subgroup of sequences
$(g_i)_i$ with $\{i : g_i = 1\} \in U$.

articles.title: Refutation of Scottish Book Problem 62
articles.statement:
The claim of Scottish Book Problem 62 is false:
there are an abelian group $G$ and subgroups $H_0 \le H_1 \le H_2 \le \cdots$ of $G$ whose
union is $G$, each isomorphic to $H_1$, such that $G$ is not isomorphic to $H_1$.

R. Baer's counterexample is $G = \mathbb{Q}$ with $H_n = \frac{1}{n!}\mathbb{Z}$: each $H_n$
is isomorphic to $\mathbb{Z}$ and their union is $\mathbb{Q}$, but $\mathbb{Q}$ is not
isomorphic to $\mathbb{Z}$.

## Sources

- S. Mazur and S. Ulam, Problem 62 of the Scottish Book; the typescript Ad 62 records R. Baer's remark giving the counterexample, with `G` the group of rational numbers and `G 1` the integers: the rationals are the union of an increasing chain of subgroups each isomorphic to the integers (for example the subgroups `(1 / n !) ℤ`), but the rationals are not isomorphic to the integers.

articles.title: Claim of Scottish Book Problem 62
articles.statement:
The claim that for every abelian group $G$ and
every sequence of subgroups $H_0 \le H_1 \le H_2 \le \cdots$ of $G$ whose union is $G$ and
each of which is isomorphic to $H_1$, the group $G$ is itself isomorphic to $H_1$.

The problem is posed for groups; the claim here is restricted to abelian groups, which loses
nothing for its refutation since Baer's counterexample is abelian.

articles.title: Pure subgroups of abelian groups
articles.statement:
A subgroup $B$ of an abelian group $A$ is pure when
$nA \cap B = nB$ for every integer $n$: for every integer $n$ and every $a \in A$ with
$na \in B$ there is some $b \in B$ with $nb = na$.

articles.title: Cardinality of the $n$-torsion of a vector space modulo a lattice
articles.statement:
The `n`-torsion of the quotient of a vector space by a free finite
lattice has cardinality `n ^ finrank L`.

This counts torsion points: for a lattice `L` of rank `r` in a vector
space, the `n`-torsion subgroup of `V ⧸ L` has `n ^ r` elements. It is
used for torsion in abelian varieties and elliptic curves, for class group
computations, and for lattice index arguments.

articles.title: From elementary divisors to invariant factors
articles.statement:
Let $I$ be a finite set, and for each
$i \in I$ let $p_i$ be a prime and $e_i$ a natural number. Then there are $k \in \mathbb{N}$ and
natural numbers $d_0, \dots, d_{k-1}$ with $d_j > 1$ for every $j$ and $d_j \mid d_l$ whenever
$j \le l$, such that $\bigoplus_{i \in I} \mathbb{Z}/p_i^{e_i}\mathbb{Z}$ is isomorphic to
$\bigoplus_{j < k} \mathbb{Z}/d_j\mathbb{Z}$.

Exponent zero is allowed, giving a trivial summand.

articles.title: Uniqueness of elementary divisors
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime and let $A$ be an abelian group.
If $A \cong \bigoplus_{i=1}^{n} \mathbb{Z}/p^{e_i}\mathbb{Z}$ and
$A \cong \bigoplus_{j=1}^{m} \mathbb{Z}/p^{f_j}\mathbb{Z}$ for positive integers
$e_1, \dots, e_n$ and $f_1, \dots, f_m$, then $n = m$ and the multisets
$\{e_1, \dots, e_n\}$ and $\{f_1, \dots, f_m\}$ are equal.

articles.title: Invariant factor decomposition of finite abelian groups
articles.statement:
Every finite abelian group $A$
is isomorphic to $\bigoplus_{i < k} \mathbb{Z}/d_i\mathbb{Z}$ for some $k \in \mathbb{N}$ and
natural numbers $d_0, \dots, d_{k-1}$ with $d_i > 1$ for every $i$ and $d_i \mid d_j$ whenever
$i \le j$.

articles.title: Fundamental theorem of finitely generated abelian groups, invariant factor form
articles.statement:
Every
finitely generated abelian group $A$ is isomorphic to
$\mathbb{Z}^a \times \bigoplus_{i < k} \mathbb{Z}/d_i\mathbb{Z}$ for some $a, k \in \mathbb{N}$
and natural numbers $d_0, \dots, d_{k-1}$ with $d_i > 1$ for every $i$ and $d_i \mid d_j$
whenever $i \le j$.

articles.title: Torsion subgroup of a finitely generated abelian group is finitely generated
articles.statement:
If $A$ is a
finitely generated abelian group, then its torsion subgroup is finitely generated.

articles.title: Torsion subgroup of a finitely generated abelian group is finite
articles.statement:
If $A$ is a finitely
generated abelian group, then its torsion subgroup is finite.

articles.title: Torsion subgroup of a finitely generated abelian group as a sum of cyclic groups
articles.statement:
If $A$
is a finitely generated abelian group, then there exist a natural number $n$ and positive
integers $d_1, \dots, d_n$ such that the torsion subgroup of $A$ is isomorphic to the direct sum
$\mathbb{Z}/d_1\mathbb{Z} \oplus \cdots \oplus \mathbb{Z}/d_n\mathbb{Z}$ of finite cyclic groups.

articles.title: The $4$-rank of a finite abelian group
articles.statement:
For a finite abelian group $A$, written
additively, the $4$-rank of $A$ is the dimension over $\mathbb{F}_2$ of the quotient $2A / 4A$,
where $2A = \{2a : a \in A\}$ and $4A = \{4a : a \in A\}$; it is the $2^j$-rank of $A$ for
$j = 2$.

articles.title: The two-power layer $2^{j-1}A / 2^jA$
articles.statement:
For an abelian group $A$, written additively, and a
natural number $j$, this is the quotient group $2^{j-1}A / 2^jA$, where $2^kA$ denotes the
subgroup $\{2^k a : a \in A\}$ and $2^jA \subseteq 2^{j-1}A$. For $j = 0$, where $j - 1$ is
read as $0$, it is the trivial quotient $A / A$.

articles.title: The $2^j$-rank of a finite abelian group
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a finite abelian group, written
additively, and let $j \ge 1$ be an integer. Writing $2^kA$ for the subgroup
$\{2^k a : a \in A\}$, the $2^j$-rank of $A$ is the dimension over $\mathbb{F}_2$ of the
quotient $2^{j-1}A / 2^jA$, which is an $\mathbb{F}_2$-vector space because $2$ kills it.

articles.title: The subgroup $2^kA$
articles.statement:
For an abelian group $A$, written additively, and a natural number
$k$, $2^kA$ is the subgroup $\{2^k a : a \in A\}$ of $A$, the image of multiplication by $2^k$.

articles.title: A p-group and a proper subgroup with isomorphic automorphism groups (Kourovka 15.27)
articles.statement:
For some
prime $p$ there are a finite $p$-group $G$ of order greater than $2$ and a proper subgroup $H < G$
with $\mathrm{Aut}(G) \cong \mathrm{Aut}(H)$ as groups.

T. Li's example is a $2$-group $G$ of order $32$ with a subgroup $H$ of order $16$.

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Archive of Solved Problems, Problem 15.27 (Ya. G. Berkovich); resolution: T. Li, Arch. Math. 92 (2009), 287-290, Kourovka Archive, Problem 15.27 (answer: Yes, it is possible, for |G| = 2|H| = 32).

articles.title: Berkovich's problem on automorphism groups of p-groups (Kourovka 15.27)
articles.statement:
The statement that
for some prime $p$ there are a finite $p$-group $G$ of order greater than $2$ and a proper subgroup
$H < G$ whose automorphism groups are isomorphic, $\mathrm{Aut}(G) \cong \mathrm{Aut}(H)$.

articles.title: Groups whose automorphisms all preserve conjugacy classes can have outer automorphisms
articles.statement:
The
claim of Kourovka Problem 16.62 is false: there is a group $G$ such that every automorphism of $G$
sends each element $g \in G$ to a conjugate of $g$, but some automorphism of $G$ is not inner,
that is, not of the form $x \mapsto h x h^{-1}$ for any $h \in G$.

Heineken constructed finite $p$-groups all of whose automorphisms preserve every conjugacy class,
and Gaschütz' theorem gives these groups outer automorphisms.

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Archive of Solved Problems, Problem 16.62 (D. MacHale); resolution: H. Heineken, Arch. Math. (Basel) 33 (1979/80), no. 6, 497-503; A. Mann, letter of 20 April 2006, as recorded in the Kourovka Archive, Kourovka Archive, Problem 16.62 (Not necessarily: Heineken's finite p-groups all of whose automorphisms preserve all conjugacy classes have outer automorphisms by Gaschütz' theorem).

articles.title: Claim of Kourovka Problem 16.62
articles.statement:
For every group $G$: if every automorphism of $G$ sends
each element $g \in G$ to a conjugate of $g$ (equivalently, maps every conjugacy class of $G$ into
itself), then every automorphism of $G$ is inner, that is, of the form $x \mapsto h x h^{-1}$ for
some $h \in G$.

articles.title: Class-preserving automorphisms need not be inner
articles.statement:
The claim of Scottish Book Problem 112
is false: there are a group $G$ and an automorphism $\alpha$ of $G$ that sends every element
to a conjugate of itself (for each $x \in G$ there is $g \in G$ with $\alpha(x) = g x g^{-1}$)
but is not inner (there is no $g \in G$ with $\alpha(x) = g x g^{-1}$ for all $x \in G$).

Burnside's 1913 example is such a group: for an odd prime $p$, a group of order $p^6$,
isomorphic to the group of $3 \times 3$ lower unitriangular matrices over the field
$\mathbb{F}_{p^2}$, whose group of class-preserving outer automorphisms is nontrivial.

## Sources

- W. Burnside's 1913 example, as summarized in M. K. Yadav, "Class preserving automorphisms of finite p-groups: A survey", arXiv:1002.1359, §1 (Burnside constructed a group of order `p ^ 6` with `Out_c (G) ≠ 1`).

articles.title: Claim of Scottish Book Problem 112
articles.statement:
The claim that for every group $G$, every
automorphism $\alpha$ of $G$ that sends each element to a conjugate of itself (for each
$x \in G$ there is $g \in G$ with $\alpha(x) = g x g^{-1}$) is inner, that is, there is a
single $g \in G$ with $\alpha(x) = g x g^{-1}$ for all $x \in G$.

articles.title: Equal endomorphism and partial isomorphism counts do not force commutativity
articles.statement:
There is a
finite non-abelian group $G$ with $|\mathrm{End}(G)| = |\mathrm{PIso}(G)|$. Here $\mathrm{End}(G)$
is the set of endomorphisms of $G$, and $\mathrm{PIso}(G)$ is the set of partial isomorphisms of
$G$: the triples $(H, K, f)$ of subgroups $H$, $K$ of $G$ and an isomorphism $f \colon H \to K$.
This answers Kourovka Problem 19.20 (P. J. Cameron) in the negative.

K. Muliarchyk's Theorem 1.1 (2026) gives a non-abelian group of order $512$ for which both counts
equal $129 \cdot 2^{24}$; the Kourovka Notebook (21st issue) answers 19.20 "No, it is not".

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Problem 19.20 (P. J. Cameron); resolution: K. Muliarchyk, A nonabelian group with equally many endomorphisms and partial isomorphisms: a computer-assisted counterexample to Kourovka Problem 19.20, preprint, 2026, Theorem 1.1: a nonabelian group of order 512, nilpotency class two and exponent four, with |PIso(G)| = |End(G)| = 129 · 2^24 (the partial isomorphisms counted by exhaustive enumeration); the Kourovka Notebook (21st issue) marks 19.20 solved: No, it is not, https://kourovkanotebookorg.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/kourovka_19.20_solution.pdf.

articles.title: Kourovka Problem 19.20 (Cameron)
articles.statement:
The statement that every finite group $G$ with
$|\mathrm{End}(G)| = |\mathrm{PIso}(G)|$ is abelian. Here $\mathrm{End}(G)$ is the set of
endomorphisms of $G$, and $\mathrm{PIso}(G)$ is the set of partial isomorphisms of $G$: the triples
$(H, K, f)$ of subgroups $H$, $K$ of $G$ and an isomorphism $f \colon H \to K$.

articles.title: Birkhoff's theorem: every group is the automorphism group of a binary relation
articles.statement:
For every
group $G$ there are a set $Z$ and a binary relation $X \subseteq Z \times Z$ such that $G$ is
the full automorphism group of $X$: there is an injective group homomorphism $\varphi$ from $G$
to the group of permutations of $Z$ whose image is exactly the set of permutations $f$ of $Z$
with $(x, y) \in X \iff (f(x), f(y)) \in X$ for all $x, y \in Z$.

The set $Z$ lies in the same universe as $G$.

## Sources

- S. Ulam, Problem 142 of the Scottish Book, headed "Problem (Ulam) - Theorem (Garrett Birkhoff)"; the representation is Birkhoff's theorem.

articles.title: Full automorphism group of a binary relation
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a group, $Z$ a set and
$X \subseteq Z \times Z$ a binary relation on $Z$. Then $G$ is the full automorphism group of
$X$ when there is an injective group homomorphism $\varphi$ from $G$ to the group of
permutations of $Z$ whose image is exactly the set of permutations $f$ of $Z$ with
$(x, y) \in X \iff (f(x), f(y)) \in X$ for all $x, y \in Z$.

articles.title: Every finite group is the outer automorphism group of a finite group
articles.statement:
For every finite group
$K$ there are a finite group $G$ and a surjective homomorphism $\mathrm{Aut}(G) \to K$ whose
kernel is the group $\mathrm{Inn}(G)$ of inner automorphisms of $G$; equivalently,
$\mathrm{Out}(G) = \mathrm{Aut}(G) / \mathrm{Inn}(G)$ is isomorphic to $K$. That is, the answer
to Kourovka Problem 16.59 is positive.

The Kourovka Archive records the answer "Yes, it does", citing Cornulier's MathOverflow answer.

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Archive of Solved Problems, Problem 16.59 (D. MacHale); resolution: Y. Cornulier, answer to MathOverflow question 372480 (Is every finite group the outer automorphism group of a finite group?), 2020, Kourovka Archive, Problem 16.59 (Yes, it does), https://mathoverflow.net/questions/372480/is-every-finite-group-the-outer-automorphism-group-of-a-finite-group/372563.

articles.title: Kourovka Problem 16.59 (finite groups as outer automorphism groups)
articles.statement:
The statement that
for every finite group $K$ there are a finite group $G$ and a surjective homomorphism
$\mathrm{Aut}(G) \to K$ whose kernel is the group $\mathrm{Inn}(G)$ of inner automorphisms of
$G$, that is, $K$ is isomorphic to $\mathrm{Out}(G) = \mathrm{Aut}(G) / \mathrm{Inn}(G)$.

articles.title: Every group is the outer automorphism group of a centreless metabelian group
articles.statement:
For every group
$G$ there is a metabelian group $M$ (one whose second derived subgroup $M''$ is trivial) with
trivial centre such that the outer automorphism group
$\operatorname{Out}(M) = \operatorname{Aut}(M)/\operatorname{Inn}(M)$ is isomorphic to $G$. This
answers Kourovka Problem 11.26 (Göbel) in the negative (Göbel and Paras).

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Archive of Solved Problems, Problem 11.26 (R. Göbel); resolution: R. Göbel and A. Paras, J. Pure Appl. Algebra 149, no. 3 (2000), 251-266, Kourovka Archive, Problem 11.26: "No, given any group `G` there is a metabelian group `M` with trivial center such that `Out M ≅ G`", https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v49.

articles.title: A group that is not an outer automorphism group of a centreless metabelian group
articles.statement:
The
statement (Kourovka Problem 11.26, Göbel) that there is a group $G$ such that for every metabelian
group $M$ (one whose second derived subgroup $M''$ is trivial) with trivial centre, the outer
automorphism group $\operatorname{Out}(M)$ is not isomorphic to $G$.

articles.title: Outer automorphism group isomorphic to a given group
articles.statement:
For groups $M$ and $G$, the
statement that $\operatorname{Out}(M) \cong G$, expressed without forming the quotient: there is a
surjective homomorphism $\operatorname{Aut}(M) \to G$ whose kernel is exactly the inner
automorphism group $\operatorname{Inn}(M)$, the image of the conjugation map
$M \to \operatorname{Aut}(M)$.

articles.title: Groups with finitely many automorphism orbits
articles.statement:
A group $G$ has finitely many automorphism
orbits if the action of its automorphism group $\operatorname{Aut}(G)$ on $G$ has only finitely
many orbits.

articles.title: Some non-abelian one-relator group is an automorphism group
articles.statement:
There exist a natural number $n$
and an element $r$ of the free group on generators $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$ such that the one-relator
group $\langle x_0, \dots, x_{n-1} \mid r \rangle$ is non-abelian and is isomorphic to the
automorphism group $\operatorname{Aut}(H)$ of some group $H$. This answers Kourovka Problem 16.75
in the affirmative.

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Archive of Solved Problems, Problem 16.75 (M. V. Neshchadim); resolution: D. J. Collins, Proc. London Math. Soc. (3) 36 (1978), no. 3, 480-493; V. A. Churkin, letter of 5 April 2006, as recorded in the Kourovka Archive, Kourovka Archive, Problem 16.75 (Yes, it can: for integers r, s with gcd(r, s) = 1, |r| ≠ |s| and r - s even, G = ⟨a, b | a⁻¹ b^r a = b^s⟩ is isomorphic to Aut(Aut(G)), Collins).

articles.title: Kourovka Problem 16.75: one-relator automorphism groups
articles.statement:
The proposition that there exist
a natural number $n$ and an element $r$ of the free group on generators $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$ such
that the one-relator group $\langle x_0, \dots, x_{n-1} \mid r \rangle$ is non-abelian and is
isomorphic to the automorphism group $\operatorname{Aut}(H)$ of some group $H$. The problem is due
to M. V. Neshchadim.

articles.title: Deaconescu's cyclicity conjecture fails (Kourovka 15.43(b))
articles.statement:
Not every finite group $G$ with
$|\mathrm{Aut}(G)| = \varphi(|G|)$ is cyclic: there is a non-cyclic finite group $G$ with
$|\mathrm{Aut}(G)| = \varphi(|G|)$, where $\varphi$ is Euler's totient function and
$\mathrm{Aut}(G)$ is the group of automorphisms of $G$.

Bray and Wilson prove more than is stated here: there are infinitely many such non-cyclic groups.

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Archive of Solved Problems, Problem 15.43 (M. Deaconescu); resolution: J. N. Bray and R. A. Wilson, On the orders of automorphism groups of finite groups, Bull. London Math. Soc. 37 (2005), no. 3, 381-385, main results (groups with |Aut G| < φ(|G|), infinitely many non-cyclic groups with |Aut G| = φ(|G|), and |Aut G|/φ(|G|) arbitrarily small); Kourovka Archive, Problem 15.43 (both answers negative), https://webspace.maths.qmul.ac.uk/j.n.bray/web/Publ/AutG/.

articles.title: Deaconescu's cyclicity conjecture (Kourovka 15.43(b))
articles.statement:
The statement that every finite group
$G$ with $|\mathrm{Aut}(G)| = \varphi(|G|)$ is cyclic, where $\varphi$ is Euler's totient function
and $\mathrm{Aut}(G)$ is the group of automorphisms of $G$.

articles.title: Green's theorem on prime powers dividing the order of the automorphism group (Kourovka 18.82)
articles.statement:
There is a function $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, the same for all primes, such that for every
$n \in \mathbb{N}$, every prime $p$ and every finite group $G$, if $p^{f(n)}$ divides $|G|$ then
$p^n$ divides $|\mathrm{Aut}(G)|$, where $\mathrm{Aut}(G)$ is the group of automorphisms of $G$.

Ledermann and Neumann (1956) first proved this with a function depending on $p$; J. A. Green (1956)
obtained a function independent of $p$.

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Archive of Solved Problems, Problem 18.82 (R. M. Patne); resolution: J. A. Green, Proc. Roy. Soc. London Ser. A 237 (1956), 574-581 (improving W. Ledermann and B. H. Neumann, Proc. Roy. Soc. London Ser. A 235 (1956), 235-246), Kourovka Archive, Problem 18.82: Yes, there is, https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v49.

articles.title: Patne's prime-power divisibility problem (Kourovka 18.82)
articles.statement:
The statement that there is a
function $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ such that for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, every prime $p$ and
every finite group $G$, if $p^{f(n)}$ divides $|G|$ then $p^n$ divides $|\mathrm{Aut}(G)|$, where
$\mathrm{Aut}(G)$ is the group of automorphisms of $G$.

articles.title: Orders of $p$-groups need not divide orders of their automorphism groups
articles.statement:
For every prime $p$
there is a finite non-cyclic $p$-group $P$ of order greater than $p^2$ whose order does not divide
the order of its automorphism group $\mathrm{Aut}(P)$.

González-Sánchez and Jaikin-Zapirain construct, for each prime $p$, finite $p$-groups $G_i$ with
$|\mathrm{Aut}(G_i)| / |G_i| \to 0$; they are non-abelian, hence non-cyclic of order greater than
$p^2$, and eventually $|\mathrm{Aut}(G_i)| < |G_i|$.

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Archive of Solved Problems, Problem 12.77 (well-known problem; A. I. Starostin); resolution: J. González-Sánchez and A. Jaikin-Zapirain, Finite p-groups with small automorphism group, Forum Math. Sigma 3 (2015), Paper No. e7, main theorem (abstract): for each prime p, finite p-groups G_i with |Aut(G_i)|/|G_i| → 0; Kourovka Archive, Problem 12.77.

articles.title: Divisibility conjecture for orders of automorphism groups of $p$-groups (Kourovka 12.77)
articles.statement:
The statement that there is a prime $p$ such that for every finite non-cyclic $p$-group $P$ of
order greater than $p^2$, the order of $P$ divides the order of its automorphism group
$\mathrm{Aut}(P)$.

The source asks this for every prime $p$; stating it for some prime makes its refutation assert a
counterexample for every prime.

articles.title: Deaconescu's totient lower bound conjecture fails (Kourovka 15.43(a))
articles.statement:
Not every finite group
$G$ satisfies $\varphi(|G|) \le |\mathrm{Aut}(G)|$: there is a finite group $G$ with
$|\mathrm{Aut}(G)| < \varphi(|G|)$, where $\varphi$ is Euler's totient function and
$\mathrm{Aut}(G)$ is the group of automorphisms of $G$.

Bray and Wilson prove more than is stated here: the ratio $|\mathrm{Aut}(G)| / \varphi(|G|)$ can be
made arbitrarily small.

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Archive of Solved Problems, Problem 15.43 (M. Deaconescu); resolution: J. N. Bray and R. A. Wilson, On the orders of automorphism groups of finite groups, Bull. London Math. Soc. 37 (2005), no. 3, 381-385, main results (groups with |Aut G| < φ(|G|), infinitely many non-cyclic groups with |Aut G| = φ(|G|), and |Aut G|/φ(|G|) arbitrarily small); Kourovka Archive, Problem 15.43 (both answers negative), https://webspace.maths.qmul.ac.uk/j.n.bray/web/Publ/AutG/.

articles.title: Deaconescu's totient lower bound conjecture (Kourovka 15.43(a))
articles.statement:
The statement that every
finite group $G$ satisfies $\varphi(|G|) \le |\mathrm{Aut}(G)|$, where $\varphi$ is Euler's totient
function and $\mathrm{Aut}(G)$ is the group of automorphisms of $G$.

articles.title: Normal series with infinite cyclic factors
articles.statement:
A group $G$ has a normal series with infinite
cyclic factors when there are a natural number $n$ and subgroups
$1 = H_0 \le H_1 \le \cdots \le H_n = G$, each normal in $G$, such that every factor
$H_{i+1}/H_i$ is infinite cyclic.

articles.title: Only inner automorphisms despite an infinite cyclic normal series (Kourovka 13.23 refuted)
articles.statement:
There is a nontrivial group $G$ with a normal series with infinite cyclic factors such that every
automorphism of $G$ is inner. So the conjecture of Kourovka Problem 13.23 is false.

Brescia, Ingrosso and Trombetti construct a torsion-free group $G$ of Hirsch length $14$ with a
series $1 = G_0 \trianglelefteq \cdots \trianglelefteq G_{14} = G$ of normal subgroups of $G$
with infinite cyclic factors and $\mathrm{Out}(G) = 1$; the Kourovka Notebook (21st issue)
marks 13.23 solved, "No, not always".

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Problem 13.23 (F. de Giovanni); resolution: M. Brescia, E. Ingrosso and M. Trombetti, A torsion-free supersoluble group with trivial outer automorphism group, preprint (2026), arXiv:2607.11775, abstract: a torsion-free group of Hirsch length 14 with a series 1 = G_0 ◁ ⋯ ◁ G_14 = G of normal subgroups of G with infinite cyclic factors and Out(G) = 1; the Kourovka Notebook (21st issue) marks 13.23 solved, https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.11775.

articles.title: Outer automorphisms of groups with an infinite cyclic normal series (Kourovka 13.23)
articles.statement:
The
conjecture that every nontrivial group with a normal series with infinite cyclic factors has an
automorphism that is not inner.

This is Kourovka Problem 13.23 (F. de Giovanni).

articles.title: Medvedev's theorem on automorphisms of order $p$ with $p^m$ fixed points
articles.statement:
There are functions
$f(p, m)$ and $g(m)$ of natural numbers, with natural-number values, such that for every prime $p$,
every $m \in \mathbb{N}$, every finite $p$-group $G$ and every automorphism $\varphi$ of $G$ of
order $p$ with exactly $p^m$ fixed points, $G$ has a subgroup $H$ of index at most $f(p, m)$ and
nilpotency class at most $g(m)$, that is, $\gamma_{g(m)+1}(H) = 1$, where $\gamma_1(H) = H$ and
$\gamma_{i+1}(H) = [\gamma_i(H), H]$.

This answers Kourovka Problem 10.68 (E. I. Khukhro) in the affirmative; the case $m = 1$ follows
from the theory of $p$-groups of maximal class.

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Archive of Solved Problems, Problem 10.68 (E. I. Khukhro); resolution: Yu. Medvedev, J. London Math. Soc. (2) 59, no. 3 (1999), 787-798, Kourovka Archive, Problem 10.68 ("Yes, it is").

articles.title: Bounded index and bounded class under a $p$-automorphism (Kourovka 10.68)
articles.statement:
The proposition
that there are functions $f(p, m)$ and $g(m)$ of natural numbers, with natural-number values, such
that for every prime $p$, every $m \in \mathbb{N}$, every finite $p$-group $G$ and every
automorphism $\varphi$ of $G$ of order $p$ with exactly $p^m$ fixed points, $G$ has a subgroup $H$
of index at most $f(p, m)$ and nilpotency class at most $g(m)$, that is, $\gamma_{g(m)+1}(H) = 1$,
where $\gamma_1(H) = H$ and $\gamma_{i+1}(H) = [\gamma_i(H), H]$.

articles.title: Almost regular automorphisms of finite $p$-groups and derived length (Kourovka 14.96)
articles.statement:
There
are functions $f \colon \mathbb{N}^3 \to \mathbb{N}$ and $g \colon \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ such
that for every prime $p$, all natural numbers $n$ and $m$, every finite $p$-group $P$ and every
automorphism $\varphi$ of $P$ of order $p^n$ with exactly $p^m$ fixed points, $P$ has a subgroup
of index at most $f(p, n, m)$ that is soluble of derived length at most $g(m)$. So Khukhro's
question of Kourovka Problem 14.96 has a positive answer.

This was proved by Jaikin-Zapirain.

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Archive of Solved Problems, Problem 14.96 (E. I. Khukhro); resolution: A. Jaikin-Zapirain, On almost regular automorphisms of finite p-groups, Adv. Math. 153 (2000), no. 2, 391-402, main theorem (a subgroup of (p, n, m)-bounded index and m-bounded derived length); Kourovka Archive, Problem 14.96 (answer: Yes, it is true).

articles.title: Bounded-index subgroups of bounded derived length (Kourovka 14.96)
articles.statement:
The proposition that
there are functions $f \colon \mathbb{N}^3 \to \mathbb{N}$ and $g \colon \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$
such that for every prime $p$, all natural numbers $n$ and $m$, every finite $p$-group $P$ and
every automorphism $\varphi$ of $P$ of order $p^n$ with exactly $p^m$ fixed points, $P$ has a
subgroup of index at most $f(p, n, m)$ that is soluble of derived length at most $g(m)$.

This is the question posed by E. I. Khukhro as Kourovka Problem 14.96.

articles.title: Bounded normal series for soluble groups with an automorphism of order four
articles.statement:
There are a
natural number $h$ and a function $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ such that, for every natural
number $m$, every finite soluble group $G$ and every automorphism $\varphi$ of $G$ of order $4$
with at most $m$ fixed points, there are normal subgroups $M \le N$ of $G$ with
$|G : N| \le f(m)$, $[[N, N], N] \le M$ (so $N/M$ is nilpotent of class at most $2$) and
$\gamma_{h+1}(M) = 1$ (so $M$ is nilpotent of class at most $h$), where $\gamma_1(M) = M$ and
$\gamma_{i+1}(M) = [\gamma_i(M), M]$. That is, the answer to Kourovka Problem 11.126 is positive.

The Kourovka Archive records the answer "Yes, there do", given by Makarenko and Khukhro.

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Archive of Solved Problems, Problem 11.126 (P. V. Shumyatskiĭ); resolution: N. Yu. Makarenko and E. I. Khukhro, Algebra and Logic 45 (2006), 326-343, Kourovka Archive, Problem 11.126: "Yes, there do", https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v49.

articles.title: Kourovka Problem 11.126 (automorphisms of order four with few fixed points)
articles.statement:
The
statement that there are a natural number $h$ and a function $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ such
that, for every natural number $m$, every finite soluble group $G$ and every automorphism
$\varphi$ of $G$ of order $4$ with at most $m$ fixed points, there are normal subgroups $M \le N$
of $G$ with $|G : N| \le f(m)$, $[[N, N], N] \le M$ (so $N/M$ is nilpotent of class at most $2$)
and $\gamma_{h+1}(M) = 1$ (so $M$ is nilpotent of class at most $h$), where $\gamma_1(M) = M$ and
$\gamma_{i+1}(M) = [\gamma_i(M), M]$.

articles.title: The derived length of a $p$-group is bounded by its sectional rank and the fixed points of an automorphism
articles.statement:
**The derived length of a $p$-group is bounded by its sectional rank and the fixed points of an
automorphism.** There is a function $f : \mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ such that for
every prime $p$, every finite $p$-group $G$, all natural numbers $r$ and $m$ such that $G$ has
sectional rank at most $r$ (every subgroup of $G$ is generated by at most $r$ elements), and every
automorphism $\varphi$ of $G$ with exactly $m$ fixed points, the derived length of $G$ is at most
$f(r, m)$, that is, the term $G^{(f(r, m))}$ of the derived series of $G$ is trivial, where
$G^{(0)} = G$ and $G^{(i+1)} = [G^{(i)}, G^{(i)}]$.

Resolved true: the Kourovka Archive answers 13.56 "Yes, it is", citing Jaikin-Zapirain: the derived
length of a finite $p$-group of sectional rank $r$ with an automorphism having exactly $m$ fixed
points is bounded by a function of $r$ and $m$.

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Archive of Solved Problems, Problem 13.56 (A. Shalev; E. I. Khukhro); resolution: A. Jaikin-Zapirain, Israel J. Math. 129 (2002), 209-220, Kourovka Archive, Problem 13.56 (answer: Yes, it is).

articles.title: Shalev and Khukhro's question on the derived length of $p$-groups with an automorphism
articles.statement:
The
statement that there is a function $f : \mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ such that for
every prime $p$, every finite $p$-group $G$, all natural numbers $r$ and $m$ such that $G$ has
sectional rank at most $r$ (every subgroup of $G$ is generated by at most $r$ elements), and every
automorphism $\varphi$ of $G$ with exactly $m$ fixed points, the derived length of $G$ is at most
$f(r, m)$, that is, the term $G^{(f(r, m))}$ of the derived series of $G$ is trivial, where
$G^{(0)} = G$ and $G^{(i+1)} = [G^{(i)}, G^{(i)}]$.

This is Kourovka Notebook Problem 13.56 (A. Shalev; E. I. Khukhro).

articles.title: Groups of sectional rank at most $r$
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a group and $r$ a natural number. The group
$G$ has sectional rank at most $r$ when every subgroup of $G$ is generated by a set of at most $r$
elements.

For a finite $p$-group $G$, the least such $r$ is the largest rank of an elementary abelian section
of $G$.

articles.title: Fitting height is bounded by the order of an automorphism and its centralizer
articles.statement:
There is a
function $f$ assigning a natural number $f(m, n)$ to every pair of natural numbers $m$, $n$ such
that every finite soluble group $G$ with an automorphism $\varphi$ has Fitting height at most
$f(|\varphi|, |C_G(\varphi)|)$, where $|\varphi|$ is the order of $\varphi$ and $|C_G(\varphi)|$ is
the number of elements of $G$ fixed by $\varphi$.

This answers Kourovka Problem 19.43 (E. I. Khukhro) affirmatively: Khukhro proved the bound, and the
21st issue of the Kourovka Notebook marks 19.43 solved ("Yes, it is").

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Problem 19.43 (E. I. Khukhro); resolution: E. Khukhro, Bull. London Math. Soc. 58 (2026), no. 1, Article ID e70206, the Kourovka Notebook (21st issue) marks 19.43 solved: Yes, it is, https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v49.

articles.title: Kourovka Problem 19.43: Fitting height, automorphism order and centralizer size
articles.statement:
The
statement that there is a function $f$ assigning a natural number $f(m, n)$ to every pair of
natural numbers $m$, $n$ such that every finite soluble group $G$ with an automorphism $\varphi$
has Fitting height at most $f(|\varphi|, |C_G(\varphi)|)$, where $|\varphi|$ is the order of
$\varphi$ and $|C_G(\varphi)|$ is the number of elements of $G$ fixed by $\varphi$.

The problem was posed by E. I. Khukhro.

articles.title: Groups acting freely on abelian groups need not embed in skew-fields (Kourovka 16.54)
articles.statement:
There
is a group $G$ with an action by automorphisms on a nontrivial abelian group $V$ such that
$g \cdot v \ne v$ for all $g \ne 1$ in $G$ and all $v \ne 0$ in $V$, but with no injective
homomorphism into the multiplicative group of any division ring. This answers Kourovka
Problem 16.54 in the negative.

The Kourovka Archive answers "No, it is not" (Nedrenko): the group $2.A_5.2$ with a quaternion
Sylow $2$-subgroup acts freely on an elementary abelian group of order $7^4$, but by Theorem 7 of
Amitsur's classification of finite subgroups of division rings it does not embed in the
multiplicative group of any skew-field.

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Archive of Solved Problems, Problem 16.54 (V. D. Mazurov); resolution: D. Nedrenko, letter of 20 January 2014, as recorded in the Kourovka Archive; S. A. Amitsur, Finite subgroups of division rings, Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 80 (1955), 361-386, Kourovka Archive, Problem 16.54 (No: 2.A_5.2 with a quaternion Sylow 2-subgroup acts freely on an elementary abelian group of order 7^4 but does not embed in the multiplicative group of a skew-field, by Amitsur's Theorem 7).

articles.title: Kourovka Problem 16.54 (free actions and embeddings in skew-fields)
articles.statement:
The statement, a
question of V. D. Mazurov, that every group $G$ with a free action by automorphisms on a
nontrivial abelian group $V$, meaning $g \cdot v \ne v$ for all $g \ne 1$ in $G$ and all $v \ne 0$
in $V$, has an injective homomorphism into the multiplicative group of some division ring.

articles.title: The commutator of an element with an automorphism
articles.statement:
For an automorphism $\varphi$ of a
group $G$ and $x \in G$, $\delta_\varphi(x) = x^{-1} \varphi(x)$. This is the commutator
$[x, \varphi]$ in the Kourovka convention $[x, y] = x^{-1} y^{-1} x y$, with $\varphi$ acting as
$x \mapsto \varphi(x)$; the iterates $\delta_\varphi^n(x)$ are the iterated commutators
$[x, {}_n \varphi]$, with $[x, {}_0 \varphi] = x$.

articles.title: An $e$-automorphism need not be a nil-automorphism
articles.statement:
Vilyatser's assertion in Kourovka
Problem 11.23 is false: there are a group $G$ and an automorphism $\varphi$ of $G$ that is an
$e$-automorphism (for any subgroups $A$ and $B$ of $G$ with $\varphi(A) = A$, $\varphi(B) = B$ and
$A \not\subseteq B$, some $a \in A \setminus B$ has $a^{-1} \varphi(a) \in B$) but not a
nil-automorphism: writing $\delta(x) = x^{-1} \varphi(x)$, some $a \in G$ has $\delta^n(a) \ne 1$
for every $n \ge 0$.

Muliarchyk shows that the cyclic shift of order four on the fourth direct power of the first
Grigorchuk group is such an automorphism, using Bartholdi's characterization of the Engel elements
of the Grigorchuk group; the preprint states that the work was carried out with assistance from
ChatGPT. The Kourovka Notebook (21st issue) marks 11.23 solved, "No, not every".

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Problem 11.23 (V. G. Vilyatser); resolution: K. Muliarchyk, An e-automorphism that is not a nil-automorphism, preprint (2026), main theorem: the cyclic shift `(g₀, g₁, g₂, g₃) ↦ (g₁, g₂, g₃, g₀)` on `Γ⁴`, `Γ` the first Grigorchuk group, is an `e`-automorphism of order four and not a nil-automorphism; the Kourovka Notebook (21st issue) marks 11.23 solved, https://kourovkanotebookorg.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/kourovka_11_23_solution.pdf.

articles.title: Vilyatser's question on $e$-automorphisms (Kourovka 11.23)
articles.statement:
The proposition that every
$e$-automorphism $\varphi$ of a group $G$ is a nil-automorphism of $G$.

articles.title: $e$-automorphisms
articles.statement:
An automorphism $\varphi$ of a group $G$ is an $e$-automorphism if for
any two subgroups $A$ and $B$ of $G$ with $\varphi(A) = A$, $\varphi(B) = B$ and
$A \not\subseteq B$, some $a \in A \setminus B$ has $[a, \varphi] = a^{-1} \varphi(a) \in B$.

articles.title: Nil-automorphisms
articles.statement:
An automorphism $\varphi$ of a group $G$ is a nil-automorphism if for
every $a \in G$ there is $n \ge 0$ with $\delta_\varphi^n(a) = 1$, where
$\delta_\varphi(x) = x^{-1} \varphi(x)$; that is, some iterated commutator $[a, {}_n \varphi]$ is
trivial.

articles.title: Fixed-point subgroup of an automorphism
articles.statement:
For an automorphism $\varphi$ of a group $G$, the
centralizer $C_G(\varphi)$ is the subgroup $\{x \in G : \varphi(x) = x\}$ of fixed points of
$\varphi$.

articles.title: Khukhro's theorem on automorphisms of prime order with centralizer of finite rank
articles.statement:
There are
functions $f \colon \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and $g \colon \mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{N} \to
\mathbb{N}$ with the following property. Let $G$ be a nilpotent group in which every element has
finite order, let $\varphi$ be an automorphism of $G$ of prime order $p$, and let $r$ be a natural
number such that the fixed-point subgroup $C_G(\varphi)$ has rank at most $r$, that is, every
finitely generated subgroup of $C_G(\varphi)$ is generated by at most $r$ elements. Then $G$ has a
normal subgroup $N$, nilpotent of class at most $f(p)$, such that the quotient $G/N$ has rank at
most $g(r, p)$. This is the positive answer to Kourovka Problem 13.58; the case $p = 2$ was proved
earlier by Shumyatsky.

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Archive of Solved Problems, Problem 13.58 (E. I. Khukhro); resolution: E. I. Khukhro, J. London Math. Soc. 77 (2008), 130-148 (the case p = 2: P. Shumyatsky, Arch. Math. 71 (1998), 425-432), Kourovka Archive, Problem 13.58 (answer: Yes, it does).

articles.title: Nilpotent-by-bounded-rank problem for automorphisms of prime order (Kourovka 13.58)
articles.statement:
The
statement that there are functions $f \colon \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and
$g \colon \mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ with the following property. Let $G$ be a
nilpotent group in which every element has finite order, let $\varphi$ be an automorphism of $G$ of
prime order $p$, and let $r$ be a natural number such that the fixed-point subgroup $C_G(\varphi)$
has rank at most $r$, that is, every finitely generated subgroup of $C_G(\varphi)$ is generated by
at most $r$ elements. Then $G$ has a normal subgroup $N$, nilpotent of class at most $f(p)$, such
that the quotient $G/N$ has rank at most $g(r, p)$.

For periodic nilpotent groups this rank is the sectional rank.

articles.title: Groups of bounded rank
articles.statement:
A group $G$ has rank at most $r$, for a natural number $r$, when
every finitely generated subgroup of $G$ is generated by some set of at most $r$ elements.

For periodic nilpotent groups this rank is the sectional rank.

articles.title: Glauberman's theorem on squares of $2$-automorphisms (Kourovka Problem 14.1)
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a
finite group with no nontrivial normal subgroup of odd order, and let $\varphi$ be an automorphism
of $G$ whose order is a power of $2$. If $\varphi$ fixes every element of some Sylow $2$-subgroup
of $G$, then $\varphi^2$ is an inner automorphism of $G$, that is, $\varphi^2$ is conjugation by
some $g \in G$.

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Archive of Solved Problems, Problem 14.1 (R. Zh. Aleev); resolution: G. Glauberman, Math. Z. 107 (1968), 1-20, Kourovka Archive, Problem 14.1 (answer: Yes, it is true).

articles.title: Kourovka Problem 14.1
articles.statement:
The statement that for every finite group $G$ with no nontrivial
normal subgroup of odd order and every automorphism $\varphi$ of $G$ whose order is a power of
$2$, if $\varphi$ fixes every element of some Sylow $2$-subgroup of $G$, then $\varphi^2$ is
conjugation by some element of $G$, that is, $\varphi^2$ is an inner automorphism.

articles.title: Groups whose twisted classes of the identity are all subgroups
articles.statement:
A group $G$ has this
property when, for every automorphism $\varphi$ of $G$, the twisted conjugacy class of the
identity $[e]_\varphi = \{g^{-1}\varphi(g) : g \in G\}$ is a subgroup of $G$.

articles.title: Negative answer to Kourovka Problem 18.15
articles.statement:
The conjecture of Kourovka Problem 18.15 is
false: there is a nontrivial group $G$ with trivial centre such that for every $a \in G$, with
$\varphi$ the inner automorphism $\varphi(g) = aga^{-1}$, the twisted conjugacy class of the
identity $[e]_\varphi = \{g^{-1}\varphi(g) : g \in G\}$ is a subgroup of $G$.

The Kourovka Archive answers 18.15 "No, not always", citing V. V. Bludov's Example 2 in
Gonçalves–Nasybullov (2019), a group with trivial centre in which $[e]_\varphi$ is a subgroup for
every inner automorphism $\varphi$.

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Archive of Solved Problems, Problem 18.15 (V. G. Bardakov, M. V. Neshchadim, T. R. Nasybullov); resolution: V. V. Bludov, Example 2 in D. Gonçalves and T. Nasybullov, On groups where the twisted conjugacy class of the unit element is a subgroup, Comm. Algebra 47 (2019), no. 3, 930-944, Kourovka Archive, Problem 18.15: No, not always; see Bludov's Example 2, https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v49.

articles.title: Kourovka Problem 18.15: an inner twisted class that is not a subgroup
articles.statement:
Every nontrivial
group $G$ with trivial centre has an element $a \in G$ such that, for the inner automorphism
$\varphi(g) = aga^{-1}$, the twisted conjugacy class of the identity
$[e]_\varphi = \{g^{-1}\varphi(g) : g \in G\}$ is not a subgroup of $G$.

The conjecture is due to V. G. Bardakov, M. V. Neshchadim and T. R. Nasybullov.

articles.title: Twisted conjugacy class of the identity (Kourovka 18.14)
articles.statement:
For a group $G$ and an
automorphism $\varphi$ of $G$, the $\varphi$-twisted conjugacy class of the identity is the set
$[e]_\varphi = \{g^{-1}\varphi(g) : g \in G\} \subseteq G$.

articles.title: Twisted conjugacy class of the identity (Kourovka 18.15)
articles.statement:
For a group $G$ and an
automorphism $\varphi$ of $G$, the $\varphi$-twisted conjugacy class of the identity is the set
$[e]_\varphi = \{g^{-1}\varphi(g) : g \in G\} \subseteq G$.

articles.title: Negative answer to the abelian assertion of Kourovka Problem 18.14
articles.statement:
There is a finitely
generated group $G$ that is not abelian although, for every automorphism $\varphi$ of $G$, the
twisted conjugacy class of the identity $[e]_\varphi = \{g^{-1}\varphi(g) : g \in G\}$ is a
subgroup of $G$.

Nicotera's Theorem 1.2 gives, for every $n$ and every odd prime $p$, a finite $p$-group of
nilpotency class $n$ with this property; for $n \ge 2$ it is not abelian.

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Problem 18.14 (V. G. Bardakov, M. V. Neshchadim, T. R. Nasybullov); resolution: C. Nicotera, On finite groups in which the twisted conjugacy classes of the unit element are subgroups, Arch. Math. 123 (2024), no. 3, 225-232, Theorem 1.2 (for every n and every odd prime p, a finite p-group of class n in which [G, φ] is a subgroup for every φ ∈ Aut G) and Corollary 3.1 (an infinite non-nilpotent group with this property); the Kourovka Notebook (21st issue) marks 18.14 solved, https://doi.org/10.1007/s00013-024-02025-6.

articles.title: Kourovka Problem 18.14, abelian assertion for finitely generated groups
articles.statement:
Every finitely
generated group $G$ in which, for every automorphism $\varphi$ of $G$, the twisted conjugacy class
of the identity $[e]_\varphi = \{g^{-1}\varphi(g) : g \in G\}$ is a subgroup of $G$, is abelian.

This is the second assertion of the conjecture of Kourovka Problem 18.14.

articles.title: Negative answer to the nilpotency assertion of Kourovka Problem 18.14
articles.statement:
There is a group $G$
that is not nilpotent although, for every automorphism $\varphi$ of $G$, the twisted conjugacy
class of the identity $[e]_\varphi = \{g^{-1}\varphi(g) : g \in G\}$ is a subgroup of $G$.

Nicotera's Corollary 3.1 gives such an infinite group, a restricted direct product of the finite
groups of Theorem 1.2 for pairwise distinct primes.

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Problem 18.14 (V. G. Bardakov, M. V. Neshchadim, T. R. Nasybullov); resolution: C. Nicotera, On finite groups in which the twisted conjugacy classes of the unit element are subgroups, Arch. Math. 123 (2024), no. 3, 225-232, Theorem 1.2 (for every n and every odd prime p, a finite p-group of class n in which [G, φ] is a subgroup for every φ ∈ Aut G) and Corollary 3.1 (an infinite non-nilpotent group with this property); the Kourovka Notebook (21st issue) marks 18.14 solved, https://doi.org/10.1007/s00013-024-02025-6.

articles.title: Kourovka Problem 18.14, nilpotency assertion
articles.statement:
Every group $G$ in which, for every
automorphism $\varphi$ of $G$, the twisted conjugacy class of the identity
$[e]_\varphi = \{g^{-1}\varphi(g) : g \in G\}$ is a subgroup of $G$, is nilpotent.

This is the first assertion of the conjecture of V. G. Bardakov, M. V. Neshchadim and
T. R. Nasybullov.

articles.title: Number of solutions of a commutator equation
articles.statement:
For an element $g$ of a group $G$, the
number of pairs $(x, y) \in G \times G$ with $[x, y] = x y x^{-1} y^{-1} = g$, taken to be $0$ when
there are infinitely many such pairs.

articles.title: Refutation of Kourovka Problem 12.26
articles.statement:
The proposition of Kourovka Problem 12.26 is false:
it is not the case that for every prime $p$ and every finite $p$-soluble group $G$, the group $G$
has a $p$-block of defect zero if and only if some normal subgroup $N$ of $G$ of order prime to $p$
contains an element $x$ whose centralizer $C_G(x)$ in $G$ has order prime to $p$.

V. I. Zenkov's counterexample: the group $G = 3^2.\mathrm{GL}_2(3)$ of order $432$ is soluble and
has a $2$-block of defect zero (an irreducible character of degree $16$), but the centralizer of
every element of $O_{2'}(G) = 3^2$, the largest normal subgroup of $G$ of odd order, has even order.

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Archive of Solved Problems, Problem 12.26 (Shi Shengming; Jiping Zhang); resolution: V. I. Zenkov, Trudy Inst. Mat. i Mekh. UrO RAN 3 (1995), 36-40 (Russian), Kourovka Archive, Problem 12.26: No; G = 3^2.GL_2(3), p = 2.

articles.title: Kourovka Problem 12.26
articles.statement:
This is the proposition (Shi Shengming) that for every prime $p$ and
every finite $p$-soluble group $G$, the group $G$ has a $p$-block of defect zero if and only if some
normal subgroup $N$ of $G$ of order prime to $p$ contains an element $x$ whose centralizer $C_G(x)$
in $G$ has order prime to $p$.

Equivalently, some $x \in O_{p'}(G)$ has a centralizer of order prime to $p$, since $O_{p'}(G)$ is
the largest normal subgroup of $G$ of order prime to $p$.

articles.title: Kourovka Problem 12.80(a) has a negative answer
articles.statement:
It is not true that for every prime $p$ and
every finite group $G$ whose order is divisible by $p$, the number of irreducible complex characters
of $G$ of $p$-defect zero equals the number of conjugacy classes of $G$ containing an element $g$
for which the number of pairs $(x, y) \in G \times G$ with $[x, y] = x y x^{-1} y^{-1} = g$ is not
divisible by $p$.

L. Barker's counterexample: for $p = 2$ and $G = \mathbb{Z}_3 \times S_3$ there are three
irreducible characters of degree $2$, all of $2$-defect zero (so three $2$-blocks of defect zero),
but only one class, that of $(1, (123))$, with an odd number of solutions of $[x, y] = g$.

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Archive of Solved Problems, Problem 12.80 (K. W. Roggenkamp; S. P. Strunkov); resolution: L. Barker, letter of 27 May 1996 (part a); B. Sambale, letter of 5 May 2021 (part b); as recorded in the Kourovka Archive, Problem 12.80, (a) p = 2, G = ℤ_3 × S_3; (b) p = 2, G = A_5: one 2-block of defect zero, three classes ((123), (12345), (13524)) with an odd number of solutions of [x, y] = g, https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v49.

articles.title: Kourovka Problem 12.80(a): blocks of defect zero and commutator equations
articles.statement:
For every prime
$p$ and every finite group $G$ whose order is divisible by $p$, the number of irreducible complex
characters of $G$ of $p$-defect zero equals the number of conjugacy classes of $G$ containing an
element $g$ for which the number of pairs $(x, y) \in G \times G$ with
$[x, y] = x y x^{-1} y^{-1} = g$ is not divisible by $p$.

Each $p$-block of defect zero contains exactly one irreducible character, and every irreducible
character of $p$-defect zero forms such a block (Brauer), so this is K. W. Roggenkamp's question
whether the number of $p$-blocks of defect zero equals that number of classes.

articles.title: Characters of $p$-defect zero
articles.statement:
For a natural number $p$ and a group $G$, the set of
characters $\chi \colon G \to \mathbb{C}$ of irreducible finite-dimensional complex representations
of $G$ whose degree is divisible by $p^a$, where $a$ is the exponent of $p$ in the prime
factorization of the order $|G|$ (and $a = 0$ when $G$ is infinite or $p$ is not prime).

For a prime $p$ and a finite group $G$, each $p$-block of defect zero contains exactly one
irreducible character, and every such character forms a block of defect zero (Brauer), so these
characters count the $p$-blocks of defect zero.

articles.title: Groups with a $p$-block of defect zero
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a natural number. A group $G$ has a
$p$-block of defect zero when some irreducible finite-dimensional complex representation of $G$ has
degree divisible by $p^{v_p(|G|)}$, where $v_p(|G|)$ is the exponent of $p$ in the prime
factorization of the order $|G|$ of $G$ (this exponent is $0$ when $p$ is not prime or $G$ is
infinite). For a prime $p$ and a finite group $G$, the number $p^{v_p(|G|)}$ is $|G|_p$, the largest
power of $p$ dividing $|G|$.

By Brauer's theory the $p$-blocks of defect zero are exactly the singletons $\{\chi\}$ with $\chi$
irreducible and $|G|_p \mid \chi(1)$.

articles.title: $p$-soluble groups
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a natural number. A group $G$ is $p$-soluble when it has a
subnormal series $1 = H_0 \le H_1 \le \dots \le H_n = G$, each $H_i$ normal in $H_{i+1}$, whose
factors $H_{i+1}/H_i$ are $p$-groups or have order prime to $p$. Here an infinite factor is taken
to have order $0$.

articles.title: Conjugacy classes with commutator count not divisible by $p$
articles.statement:
For a natural number $p$ and
a group $G$, the set of conjugacy classes of $G$ containing an element $g$ such that the number of
pairs $(x, y) \in G \times G$ with $[x, y] = x y x^{-1} y^{-1} = g$ (taken to be $0$ when there are
infinitely many) is not divisible by $p$.

articles.title: Kourovka Problem 12.80(b) has a negative answer
articles.statement:
It is not true that for every prime $p$ and
every finite simple group $G$ whose order is divisible by $p$, the number of irreducible complex
characters of $G$ of $p$-defect zero equals the number of conjugacy classes of $G$ containing an
element $g$ for which the number of pairs $(x, y) \in G \times G$ with
$[x, y] = x y x^{-1} y^{-1} = g$ is not divisible by $p$.

B. Sambale's counterexample: in $A_5$ with $p = 2$ there is one irreducible character of $2$-defect
zero (the character of degree $4$, so one $2$-block of defect zero) but three classes, those of
$(123)$, $(12345)$ and $(13524)$, with an odd number of solutions of $[x, y] = g$.

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Archive of Solved Problems, Problem 12.80 (K. W. Roggenkamp; S. P. Strunkov); resolution: L. Barker, letter of 27 May 1996 (part a); B. Sambale, letter of 5 May 2021 (part b); as recorded in the Kourovka Archive, Problem 12.80, (a) p = 2, G = ℤ_3 × S_3; (b) p = 2, G = A_5: one 2-block of defect zero, three classes ((123), (12345), (13524)) with an odd number of solutions of [x, y] = g, https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v49.

articles.title: Kourovka Problem 12.80(b): the case of simple groups
articles.statement:
For every prime $p$ and every
finite simple group $G$ whose order is divisible by $p$, the number of irreducible complex
characters of $G$ of $p$-defect zero equals the number of conjugacy classes of $G$ containing an
element $g$ for which the number of pairs $(x, y) \in G \times G$ with
$[x, y] = x y x^{-1} y^{-1} = g$ is not divisible by $p$.

articles.title: Character values of a finite group lie in a cyclotomic field
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group of
exponent $n$, and let $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_n)$ be the $n$-th cyclotomic field. There is a ring
homomorphism $\varphi \colon \mathbb{Q}(\zeta_n) \to \mathbb{C}$ such that for every
finite-dimensional complex representation $\rho$ of $G$ on a vector space $V$ and every $g \in G$,
the trace of $\rho(g)$ lies in the image of $\varphi$.

## Sources

- R. Brauer, On the representation of a group of order g in the field of g-th roots of unity, Amer. J. Math. 67 (1945). Problem `brauer_character_in_cyclotomic` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Brauer's splitting field theorem
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group of exponent $n$, let
$K = \mathbb{Q}(\zeta_n)$ be the $n$-th cyclotomic field, and let $\rho$ be a representation of
$G$ on a finite-dimensional complex vector space $V$. Then there are a ring homomorphism
$\varphi \colon K \to \mathbb{C}$, a $K$-vector space $W$ with a representation $\sigma$ of $G$
on $W$, and a $\mathbb{C}$-linear isomorphism $f \colon \mathbb{C} \otimes_K W \to V$, where
$\mathbb{C}$ is regarded as a $K$-algebra via $\varphi$, such that
$f((\mathrm{id}_{\mathbb{C}} \otimes \sigma(g))(x)) = \rho(g)(f(x))$ for all $g \in G$ and all
$x \in \mathbb{C} \otimes_K W$.

## Sources

- R. Brauer, On the representation of a group of order g in the field of g-th roots of unity, Amer. J. Math. 67 (1945), 461–471. Problem `brauer_splitting_field` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Sum of two distinct unit complex numbers
articles.statement:
If $a$ and $b$ are distinct complex numbers
with $|a| = |b| = 1$, then $|a + b| < 2$.

articles.title: Strict triangle inequality for unit complex numbers, multiset form
articles.statement:
Let $s$ be a finite
multiset of complex numbers, each of absolute value $1$, containing two distinct elements. Then
the absolute value of the sum of $s$ is strictly less than the number of elements of $s$,
counted with multiplicity.

articles.title: Strict triangle inequality for unit complex numbers
articles.statement:
Let $\mu_1, \dots, \mu_n$ be complex
numbers with $|\mu_i| = 1$ for every $i$, not all equal. Then
$\left|\sum_{i=1}^{n} \mu_i\right| < n$.

articles.title: Characters of full absolute value have equal eigenvalues
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group,
$V$ a nonzero finite-dimensional complex vector space and $\rho$ an irreducible representation of
$G$ on $V$ with character $\chi$. If $g \in G$ satisfies $|\chi(g)| = \dim V$, then any two roots
of the characteristic polynomial of $\rho(g)$ are equal.

articles.title: Burnside's vanishing theorem for coprime class sizes
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group, let
$\rho$ be an irreducible representation of $G$ on a nonzero finite-dimensional complex vector
space $V$, with character $\chi$, and let $g \in G$. If the size of the conjugacy class of $g$
is coprime to $\dim V$, then $|\chi(g)| = \dim V$ or $\chi(g) = 0$.

Since $\chi(1) = \dim V$, the first alternative says that $g$ lies in the center $Z(\chi)$ of
$\chi$, the set of $h \in G$ with $|\chi(h)| = \chi(1)$.

## Sources

- Bielefeld Theorem 5.

articles.title: Burnside's $p^a q^b$ theorem from the prime-power class corollary
articles.statement:
Suppose that every
finite simple group $H$ having an element $h \ne 1$ whose conjugacy class has size $r^k$ for some
prime $r$ and some $k \ge 1$ has prime order. Then for all primes $p$ and $q$ and all natural
numbers $a$ and $b$, every finite group $G$ of order $p^a q^b$ is solvable.

## Sources

- Bielefeld Theorem 7.

articles.title: Burnside's $p^a q^b$ theorem in the lowest universe
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group whose
underlying type lies in the lowest type universe, let $p$ and $q$ be primes and let $a$ and
$b$ be natural numbers. If $G$ has order $p^a q^b$, then $G$ is solvable.

articles.title: Burnside's $p^a q^b$ theorem
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group, let $p$ and $q$ be primes and
let $a$ and $b$ be natural numbers. If $G$ has order $p^a q^b$, then $G$ is solvable.

articles.title: Bound on the number of irreducible representations
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group. Every
finite set of isomorphism classes of simple finite-dimensional complex representations of $G$
has at most $|G|$ elements.

articles.title: A simple group with a nontrivial linear character has prime order
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite
simple group and let $\rho$ be a representation of $G$ on a complex vector space $V$ of
dimension $1$. If the character of $\rho$ is not the constant function $1$, then the order of
$G$ is a prime number.

articles.title: Conjugacy class of the chosen representative
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group. For every
conjugacy class $K$ of $G$, the set of elements of $K$ equals the conjugacy class of the chosen
representative of $K$.

articles.title: Central scalars are algebraic integers
articles.statement:
Let $\rho$ be an irreducible representation of a
finite group $G$ on a finite-dimensional complex vector space $V$. For every conjugacy class $C$
of $G$, the complex number $\omega_\rho(C)$ by which the class sum $\sum_{x \in C} x$ acts on $V$
is an algebraic integer, that is, integral over $\mathbb{Z}$.

articles.title: Central scalars multiply via the class structure constants
articles.statement:
Let $\rho$ be an irreducible
representation of a finite group $G$ on a finite-dimensional complex vector space $V$, and let
$\omega_\rho(C)$ be the scalar by which the class sum of a conjugacy class $C$ acts on $V$. Fix
a representative $g_C$ of each conjugacy class $C$. For conjugacy classes $C_1$ and $C_2$,

$$\omega_\rho(C_1)\,\omega_\rho(C_2) = \sum_{C} a_{C_1 C_2}^{C}\, \omega_\rho(C),$$

where $C$ runs over all conjugacy classes of $G$ and $a_{C_1 C_2}^{C}$ is the number of pairs
$(x, y) \in C_1 \times C_2$ with $x y = g_C$.

articles.title: Trace formula for central scalars
articles.statement:
Let $\rho$ be an irreducible representation of a
finite group $G$ on a finite-dimensional complex vector space $V$ with character $\chi$, and let
$\omega_\rho(C)$ be the scalar by which the class sum of a conjugacy class $C$ acts on $V$. Then
$\omega_\rho(C) \cdot \dim V = \sum_{x \in C} \chi(x)$.

articles.title: Central scalar of a conjugacy class
articles.statement:
Let $\rho$ be an irreducible representation of a
finite group $G$ on a finite-dimensional complex vector space $V$. For a conjugacy class $C$ of
$G$, the class sum $\sum_{x \in C} x$ is central in the group algebra $\mathbb{C}[G]$, so it acts
on $V$ as multiplication by a complex number. The central scalar $\omega_\rho(C)$ is that number:
$\rho\bigl(\sum_{x \in C} x\bigr) v = \omega_\rho(C)\, v$ for all $v \in V$.

articles.title: Centralizer as a conjugation stabilizer
articles.statement:
For an element $g$ of a finite group $G$, this
is the bijection from the centralizer $C_G(g) = \{x \in G : xg = gx\}$ onto the stabilizer of
$g$ for the action of $G$ on itself by conjugation, $x \cdot y = x y x^{-1}$, that sends each
element $x$ to itself.

articles.title: The scalar center of a nonlinear irreducible representation is proper
articles.statement:
Let $\rho$ be an
irreducible representation of a group $G$ on a finite-dimensional complex vector space $V$ with
$\dim V > 1$. Then the scalar center of $\rho$ is a proper subgroup of $G$.

articles.title: Scalar center of a representation
articles.statement:
Let $\rho$ be a representation of a group $G$ on a
nonzero complex vector space $V$. The scalar center of $\rho$ is the subgroup of $G$ consisting of
the elements $g$ such that $\rho(g) = c \cdot \mathrm{id}_V$ for some $c \in \mathbb{C}$.

articles.title: Integrality of the normalized character value at a coprime class
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite
group, let $\rho$ be an irreducible representation of $G$ on a nonzero finite-dimensional complex
vector space $V$, with character $\chi$, and let $g \in G$. If the size of the conjugacy class of
$g$ is coprime to $\dim V$, then $\chi(g)/\chi(1)$ is an algebraic integer.

## Sources

- Bielefeld Theorem 5, integrality step.

articles.title: Characters are constant on conjugacy classes
articles.statement:
Let $\rho$ be a representation of a finite
group $G$ on a finite-dimensional complex vector space, with character $\chi$, and let $g_l$ be the
chosen representative of a conjugacy class $l$ of $G$. Then $\chi(x) = \chi(g_l)$ for every
$x \in l$.

articles.title: Character vanishing from coprimality and a strict norm bound
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group,
let $\rho$ be an irreducible representation of $G$ on a nonzero finite-dimensional complex vector
space $V$, with character $\chi$, and let $g \in G$. If the size of the conjugacy class of $g$ is
coprime to $\dim V$ and $|\chi(g)| < \dim V$, then $\chi(g) = 0$.

## Sources

- Bielefeld Theorem 5, norm step.

articles.title: Character of a class via its chosen representative
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a group and let $c$ be an
isomorphism class of simple finite-dimensional complex representations of $G$, with chosen
representative $(V, \rho)$. For every $x \in G$, the character of $c$ at $x$ equals the character
of the representation $\rho$ at $x$, namely $\operatorname{tr} \rho(x)$.

articles.title: Characters determine irreducible representations
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group. Two
isomorphism classes of simple finite-dimensional complex representations of $G$ that have the
same character are equal.

articles.title: Character value at the identity
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a group and let $c$ be an isomorphism class of
simple finite-dimensional complex representations of $G$. The character of $c$ at the identity
$1 \in G$ equals the dimension over $\mathbb{C}$ of the chosen representative of $c$.

articles.title: Character of the trivial representation
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group. The character of the
isomorphism class of the trivial representation of $G$ on $\mathbb{C}$ takes the value $1$ at
every $g \in G$.

articles.title: Character of an isomorphism class
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a group. For an isomorphism class $c$ of
simple finite-dimensional complex representations of $G$, the character of $c$ is the function
$\chi_c \colon G \to \mathbb{C}$ given by $\chi_c(g) = \operatorname{tr} \rho(g)$ for any
representative $(V, \rho)$ of $c$. It does not depend on the representative, since isomorphic
representations have the same character.

articles.title: Orthogonality of irreducible characters
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group and let $\chi_i$ and
$\chi_j$ be the characters of isomorphism classes $i$ and $j$ of simple finite-dimensional
complex representations of $G$. Then

$$\frac{1}{|G|} \sum_{g \in G} \chi_i(g)\, \chi_j(g^{-1}) =
