\begin{cases} 1 & \text{if } i = j, \\ 0 & \text{otherwise.} \end{cases}$$

articles.title: Characters at inverses are constant on conjugacy classes
articles.statement:
Let $\rho$ be a representation
of a finite group $G$ on a finite-dimensional complex vector space, with character $\chi$, and let
$g_l$ be the chosen representative of a conjugacy class $l$ of $G$. Then
$\chi(x^{-1}) = \chi(g_l^{-1})$ for every $x \in l$.

articles.title: Character values lie in a cyclotomic field
articles.statement:
Let $\rho$ be a representation of a group $G$
on a finite-dimensional complex vector space, with character $\chi$, and let $g \in G$ have
finite order $m$. Then $\chi(g)$ lies in the subfield of $\mathbb{C}$ generated over $\mathbb{Q}$
by the $m$-th roots of unity.

articles.title: Characteristic roots are not all equal below the degree
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group, let
$\rho$ be a representation of $G$ on a nonzero finite-dimensional complex vector space $V$, with
character $\chi$, and let $g \in G$. If $|\chi(g)| < \dim V$, then the characteristic polynomial
of $\rho(g)$ has two distinct roots.

articles.title: Nonlinear irreducible characters of a simple group vanish on nonidentity classes of coprime size
articles.statement:
**Nonlinear irreducible characters of a simple group vanish on nonidentity classes of
coprime size.** Let $G$ be a finite simple group, let $\rho$ be an irreducible representation of
$G$ on a finite-dimensional complex vector space $V$ of dimension $d > 1$, and let $\chi$ be the
character of $\rho$. If $g \ne 1$ is an element of $G$ whose conjugacy class has size coprime to
$d$, then $\chi(g) = 0$.

articles.title: Character value as the sum of characteristic roots
articles.statement:
Let $\rho$ be a representation of a
group $G$ on a finite-dimensional complex vector space, with character $\chi$, and let $g \in G$.
Then $\chi(g)$ is the sum of the roots of the characteristic polynomial of $\rho(g)$, counted
with multiplicity.

articles.title: Character values are algebraic integers
articles.statement:
Let $\rho$ be a representation of a finite group
$G$ on a finite-dimensional complex vector space, with character $\chi$. Then $\chi(g)$ is an
algebraic integer for every $g \in G$.

Each value $\chi(g)$ is a sum of roots of unity.

articles.title: Eigenvalues of a finite group representation have modulus one
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite
group, $V$ a finite-dimensional complex vector space and $\rho$ a representation of $G$ on $V$.
For every $g \in G$, every root $\mu$ of the characteristic polynomial of $\rho(g)$ satisfies
$|\mu| = 1$.

articles.title: Characteristic roots are killed by the order of the element
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a group, $V$ a
finite-dimensional complex vector space, $\rho$ a representation of $G$ on $V$, and $g \in G$
an element of order $n$, where $n = 0$ if $g$ has infinite order. Then every root $\mu$ of the
characteristic polynomial of $\rho(g)$ satisfies $\mu^n = 1$; in particular, when $g$ has finite
order, $\mu$ is a root of unity.

articles.title: Number of characteristic roots of a representation matrix
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a group, $V$ a
finite-dimensional complex vector space, $\rho$ a representation of $G$ on $V$ and $g \in G$.
The characteristic polynomial of $\rho(g)$ has exactly $\dim_{\mathbb{C}} V$ roots in
$\mathbb{C}$, counted with multiplicity.

articles.title: Contribution of a conjugacy class to the self-pairing sum
articles.statement:
Let $\rho$ be an irreducible
representation of a finite group $G$ on a finite-dimensional complex vector space $V$, with
character $\chi$. For a conjugacy class $l$ of $G$, let $g_l$ be its chosen representative and
$\omega(l)$ the central scalar of $l$, the scalar by which the class sum of $l$ acts on $V$. Then
$\sum_{x \in l} \chi(x)\chi(x^{-1}) = (\dim_{\mathbb{C}} V)\,\omega(l)\,\chi(g_l^{-1})$.

articles.title: Chosen representative of a conjugacy class
articles.statement:
For each conjugacy class $K$ of a group $G$,
the representative of $K$ is an element $g_K \in G$, fixed once and for all by choice, whose
conjugacy class is $K$.

articles.title: Class sums of conjugacy classes are central
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group. For every
conjugacy class $K$ of $G$ and every element $w$ of the complex group algebra $\mathbb{C}[G]$,
the class sum $\widehat{K} = \sum_{x \in K} x$ satisfies $w \widehat{K} = \widehat{K} w$.

articles.title: The class sum of the conjugacy class of an element is central
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group,
let $g \in G$, and let $\widehat{C_g} = \sum_{x \in C_g} x$ be the sum, in the complex group
algebra $\mathbb{C}[G]$, of the elements of the conjugacy class $C_g$ of $g$. Then
$w \widehat{C_g} = \widehat{C_g} w$ for every $w \in \mathbb{C}[G]$.

articles.title: Class size times character ratio is an algebraic integer
articles.statement:
Let $\rho$ be an irreducible
representation of a finite group $G$ on a finite-dimensional complex vector space $V$, with
character $\chi$. For every $g \in G$, if $C$ is the conjugacy class of $g$, then
$|C|\,\chi(g)/\chi(1)$ is an algebraic integer.

## Sources

- Bielefeld Prop 1.

articles.title: Class sums commute with group elements
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group, let $g \in G$, and let
$\widehat{C_g} = \sum_{x \in C_g} x$ be the sum, in the complex group algebra $\mathbb{C}[G]$, of
the elements of the conjugacy class $C_g$ of $g$. Then $\widehat{C_g} h = h \widehat{C_g}$ for
every $h \in G$, where $h$ is viewed as a basis element of $\mathbb{C}[G]$.

articles.title: Products of class sums expand in class sums
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group. For a finite
subset $C$ of $G$ write $\widehat{C} = \sum_{x \in C} x$ in the complex group algebra
$\mathbb{C}[G]$, and for $g \in G$ let $C_g$ be its conjugacy class. Let $g_i, g_j \in G$, and for
each conjugacy class $K$ of $G$ with chosen representative $z_K$ let $a_K$ be the number of pairs
$(x, y) \in C_{g_i} \times C_{g_j}$ with $x y = z_K$. Then
$\widehat{C_{g_i}} \widehat{C_{g_j}} = \sum_K a_K \widehat{K}$, the sum running over all
conjugacy classes $K$ of $G$.

articles.title: Class sum of a finite subset
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a group. The class sum of a finite subset
$C \subseteq G$ is the element $\widehat{C} = \sum_{x \in C} x$ of the complex group algebra
$\mathbb{C}[G]$.

articles.title: Class functions orthogonal to all irreducible characters vanish
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite
group and let $f \colon G \to \mathbb{C}$ be a class function, that is, $f(hgh^{-1}) = f(g)$ for
all $g, h \in G$. Suppose that for every isomorphism class $c$ of simple finite-dimensional
complex representations of $G$, with character $\chi_c$,

$$\frac{1}{|G|} \sum_{g \in G} f(g)\, \chi_c(g^{-1}) = 0.$$

Then $f = 0$.

## Sources

- Zimmerman, Theorem 5 (core step).

articles.title: Expansion of class functions in irreducible characters
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group, let
$f \colon G \to \mathbb{C}$ be a class function, and for each of the finitely many isomorphism
classes $c$ of simple finite-dimensional complex representations of $G$ let $\chi_c$ be its
character. Then

$$f = \sum_{c} \Big(\frac{1}{|G|} \sum_{g \in G} f(g)\, \chi_c(g^{-1})\Big)\, \chi_c,$$

where $c$ runs over all these isomorphism classes.

## Sources

- Zimmerman, Proposition 4 (setup).

articles.title: Coefficients of a product of class sums
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a group, let $C_i$ and $C_j$ be
finite subsets of $G$, and write $\widehat{C} = \sum_{x \in C} x$ in the complex group algebra
$\mathbb{C}[G]$. For every $u \in G$, the coefficient of $u$ in $\widehat{C_i} \widehat{C_j}$ is
the number of pairs $(x, y) \in C_i \times C_j$ with $x y = u$.

articles.title: Class size times centralizer order
articles.statement:
Let $g$ be an element of a finite group $G$, let
$g^G$ be its conjugacy class and let $C_G(g) = \{x \in G : xg = gx\}$ be its centralizer.
Then $|g^G| \cdot |C_G(g)| = |G|$.

articles.title: Orbit–stabilizer for a conjugacy class
articles.statement:
For every element $g$ of a finite group $G$, the
size of the conjugacy class of $g$ times the order of the stabilizer of $g$ under the action of
$G$ on itself by conjugation, $x \cdot y = x y x^{-1}$, equals the order of $G$.

articles.title: Conjugate elements have the same conjugacy class
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group. If
$g_1, g_2 \in G$ are conjugate, then the conjugacy class of $g_1$ equals the conjugacy class of
$g_2$.

articles.title: Conjugacy class
articles.statement:
For an element $g$ of a finite group $G$, the conjugacy class of $g$ is
the finite set $\{h g h^{-1} : h \in G\}$, the orbit of $g$ under the action of $G$ on itself
by conjugation.

articles.title: Conjugacy classes are closed under conjugation
articles.statement:
Let $g$, $h$ and $x$ be elements of a
finite group $G$. If $x$ lies in the conjugacy class of $g$, then so does $h x h^{-1}$.

articles.title: Characteristic roots as elements of the cyclotomic field
articles.statement:
Let $m$ be a positive integer,
let $\rho$ be a representation of a finite group $G$ on a finite-dimensional complex vector
space $V$, and let $g \in G$ be such that every root $\mu$ of the characteristic polynomial of
$\rho(g)$ satisfies $\mu^m = 1$. Each such root $\mu$ is regarded as an element of the subfield
$K \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ obtained by adjoining the $m$-th roots of unity to $\mathbb{Q}$.

articles.title: Members of a conjugacy class are conjugate to its representative
articles.statement:
Let $l$ be a conjugacy
class of a finite group $G$ and $g_l$ its chosen representative. For every $x \in l$ there is
$c \in G$ with $c x c^{-1} = g_l$.

articles.title: A simple group with a prime-power conjugacy class has prime order
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite
simple group and let $g \ne 1$ be an element of $G$ whose conjugacy class has size $r^k$ for some
prime $r$ and some $k \ge 1$. Then the order of $G$ is a prime number.

## Sources

- Bielefeld Corollary 6.

articles.title: The $m$-th cyclotomic field is a splitting field of $X^m - 1$
articles.statement:
For every natural number
$m \neq 0$, the subfield of $\mathbb{C}$ generated over $\mathbb{Q}$ by the $m$-th roots of unity
is a splitting field over $\mathbb{Q}$ of the polynomial $X^m - 1 \in \mathbb{Q}[X]$.

articles.title: Complex roots of $X^m - 1$
articles.statement:
For every natural number $m \neq 0$, the set of complex roots
of the rational polynomial $X^m - 1$ is exactly the set of $m$-th roots of unity in $\mathbb{C}$.

articles.title: The zeroth cyclotomic field is $\mathbb{Q}$
articles.statement:
For $m = 0$ the cyclotomic subfield of
$\mathbb{C}$ is the bottom intermediate field, that is $\mathbb{Q}$ itself: the polynomial
$X^0 - 1$ is zero and is taken to have no roots, so nothing is adjoined.

articles.title: Cyclotomic subfield of $\mathbb{C}$
articles.statement:
For a natural number $m$, the $m$-th cyclotomic
field is the intermediate field of $\mathbb{C}/\mathbb{Q}$ generated over $\mathbb{Q}$ by the
$m$-th roots of unity, that is, by the complex roots of $X^m - 1$.

For $m = 0$ the polynomial $X^0 - 1$ is zero and is taken to have no roots, so the field is
$\mathbb{Q}$.

articles.title: Degrees of irreducible representations divide the group order
articles.statement:
Let $\rho$ be an
irreducible representation of a finite group $G$ on a nonzero finite-dimensional complex vector
space $V$. Then $\dim_{\mathbb{C}} V$ divides $|G|$.

## Sources

- Bielefeld Corollary 2.

articles.title: Pairing of the identity indicator with a character
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group, let
$\delta \colon G \to \mathbb{C}$ be the indicator function of the identity, so $\delta(1) = 1$ and
$\delta(g) = 0$ for $g \neq 1$, and let $\chi_c$ be the character of an isomorphism class $c$ of
simple finite-dimensional complex representations of $G$. Then

$$\frac{1}{|G|} \sum_{g \in G} \delta(g)\, \chi_c(g^{-1}) = \frac{\chi_c(1)}{|G|}.$$

articles.title: Delta function at the identity
articles.statement:
For a finite group $G$, $\delta_1 \colon G \to \mathbb{C}$
is the function with $\delta_1(1) = 1$ and $\delta_1(g) = 0$ for every $g \ne 1$.

articles.title: Field embeddings applied to character values
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a group, $\rho$ a
representation of $G$ on a finite-dimensional complex vector space $V$ with character $\chi$,
let $m$ be a positive integer, and let $g \in G$ be such that every root $\mu$ of the
characteristic polynomial of $\rho(g)$ satisfies $\mu^m = 1$. Let $K \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ be the
field obtained by adjoining the $m$-th roots of unity to $\mathbb{Q}$, and suppose
$\chi(g) \in K$. Then for every $\mathbb{Q}$-algebra homomorphism $\sigma : K \to \mathbb{C}$ we
have $\sigma(\chi(g)) = \sum_\mu \sigma(\mu)$, where the sum runs over the roots $\mu$ of the
characteristic polynomial of $\rho(g)$, counted with multiplicity, each regarded as an element
of $K$.

articles.title: Cancelling a unit-modulus conjugate
articles.statement:
Let $a, b \in \mathbb{C}$ with $|b| = 1$. If
$a \bar{b} = 1$, then $a = b$.

articles.title: Divisors of $p^a q^b$
articles.statement:
Let $p$ and $q$ be primes and let $a$ and $b$ be natural numbers.
Every natural number $d$ dividing $p^a q^b$ has the form $d = p^{a'} q^{b'}$ for some natural
numbers $a'$ and $b'$.

articles.title: Elements with a single eigenvalue act as scalars
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group, $V$ a nonzero
finite-dimensional complex vector space, $\rho$ a representation of $G$ on $V$, $g \in G$ and
$\mu_0 \in \mathbb{C}$. If every root of the characteristic polynomial of $\rho(g)$ equals
$\mu_0$, then $\rho(g) = \mu_0 \cdot \mathrm{id}_V$.

articles.title: One-dimensional representations act by their character
articles.statement:
Let $\rho$ be a representation
of a group $G$ on a complex vector space $V$ of dimension $1$, and let $\chi$ be the character of
$\rho$. Then for every $g \in G$ the operator $\rho(g)$ is multiplication by the scalar $\chi(g)$,
that is, $\rho(g) = \chi(g) \cdot \mathrm{id}_V$.

articles.title: Elements of the scalar center act by scalars
articles.statement:
Let $\rho$ be a representation of a group $G$
on a nonzero complex vector space $V$. If $g$ lies in the scalar center of $\rho$, then there is
$c \in \mathbb{C}$ with $\rho(g) = c \cdot \mathrm{id}_V$.

articles.title: A nontrivial element whose class size is a power of $p$
articles.statement:
Let $p$ and $q$ be primes, let
$a$ and $b$ be natural numbers with $b \ge 1$, and let $G$ be a finite group of order
$p^a q^b$. Then there are an element $g \ne 1$ of $G$ and a natural number $k \le a$ such that
the conjugacy class of $g$ has exactly $p^k$ elements.

In the proof, $g$ is a nontrivial element of the center of a subgroup of $G$ of order $q^b$
(a Sylow $q$-subgroup when $p \ne q$).

articles.title: Schur's lemma for central elements of the group algebra
articles.statement:
Let $\rho$ be an irreducible
representation of a group $G$ on a finite-dimensional complex vector space $V$, extended linearly
to the group algebra $\mathbb{C}[G]$. If $z \in \mathbb{C}[G]$ commutes with every element of
$\mathbb{C}[G]$, then $z$ acts on $V$ as a scalar: there is $c \in \mathbb{C}$ with
$\rho(z) v = c\, v$ for all $v \in V$.

articles.title: An algebraic integer cannot solve $1 + p\beta = 0$ for a prime $p$
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime
number. There is no algebraic integer $\beta \in \mathbb{C}$ with $1 + p\beta = 0$, since such a
$\beta$ would make $-1/p$ an algebraic integer.

articles.title: Isomorphism classes of simple representations
articles.statement:
For a finite group $G$, $\mathrm{Irr}(G)$ is
the set of isomorphism classes of simple finite-dimensional complex representations of $G$.

articles.title: Simple finite-dimensional representations are irreducible (auxiliary form)
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a
finite group and $V$ a simple object of the category of finite-dimensional complex representations
of $G$. If $\sigma$ is a representation of $G$ on the underlying vector space of $V$ that equals the
action of $G$ on $V$, then $\sigma$ is irreducible.

articles.title: Simple finite-dimensional complex representations of a finite group are irreducible
articles.statement:
Let
$G$ be a finite group. If $V$ is a simple object of the category of finite-dimensional complex
representations of $G$, then the representation of $G$ on the underlying vector space of $V$ is
irreducible.

articles.title: Class function
articles.statement:
A function $f \colon G \to \mathbb{C}$ on a finite group $G$ is a class
function when $f(hgh^{-1}) = f(g)$ for all $g, h \in G$, that is, when $f$ is constant on
conjugacy classes.

articles.title: Groups of prime order are solvable
articles.statement:
Every finite group whose order is a prime number is
solvable.

articles.title: Isomorphism of simple representations
articles.statement:
For a finite group $G$, two simple
finite-dimensional complex representations of $G$ are related when they are isomorphic; this is an
equivalence relation on the simple finite-dimensional complex representations of $G$.

articles.title: A linear character as a homomorphism to $\mathbb{C}^\times$
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group and
let $\rho$ be a representation of $G$ on a complex vector space $V$ of dimension $1$, with
character $\chi$. This is the group homomorphism from $G$ to the multiplicative group
$\mathbb{C}^\times$ of nonzero complex numbers that sends $g$ to $\chi(g)$.

articles.title: $X^m - 1$ over $\mathbb{Q}$ and over $\mathbb{C}$
articles.statement:
For every natural number $m$, mapping
the coefficients of the rational polynomial $X^m - 1$ along the inclusion
$\mathbb{Q} \to \mathbb{C}$ gives the complex polynomial $X^m - 1$.

articles.title: Membership in the scalar center
articles.statement:
Let $\rho$ be a representation of a group $G$ on a nonzero
complex vector space $V$. An element $g \in G$ lies in the scalar center of $\rho$ if and only if
$\rho(g) = c \cdot \mathrm{id}_V$ for some $c \in \mathbb{C}$.

articles.title: Elements acting by a scalar lie in the scalar center
articles.statement:
Let $\rho$ be a representation of a
group $G$ on a nonzero complex vector space $V$. If $g \in G$ and $c \in \mathbb{C}$ satisfy
$\rho(g) = c \cdot \mathrm{id}_V$, then $g$ lies in the scalar center of $\rho$.

articles.title: Elements of the scalar center have character of full absolute value
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite
group, $V$ a nonzero finite-dimensional complex vector space and $\rho$ a representation of $G$
on $V$ with character $\chi$. If $g$ lies in the scalar center of $\rho$, then
$|\chi(g)| = \dim V$.

articles.title: Product of a unit complex number with a conjugate unit
articles.statement:
For complex numbers $a$ and $b$
with $|a| = |b| = 1$, we have $|a \bar{b}| = 1$.

articles.title: Real part of a unit complex number other than $1$
articles.statement:
If $w \in \mathbb{C}$ satisfies
$|w| = 1$ and $w \neq 1$, then $\operatorname{Re} w < 1$.

articles.title: Real part of a product with a conjugate
articles.statement:
For complex numbers $a$ and $b$,
$\operatorname{Re} a \operatorname{Re} b + \operatorname{Im} a \operatorname{Im} b =
\operatorname{Re}(a \bar{b})$.

articles.title: Column orthogonality at the identity
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group and, for each isomorphism
class $c$ of simple finite-dimensional complex representations of $G$, let $\chi_c$ be its
character. For every $g \in G$ with $g \ne 1$, $\sum_c \chi_c(1)\,\chi_c(g) = 0$, where the sum runs
over all such classes $c$.

Equivalently, the character of the regular representation vanishes away from the identity.

articles.title: Chosen representative of an isomorphism class
articles.statement:
For a finite group $G$ and an isomorphism
class $c$ of simple finite-dimensional complex representations of $G$, this is a simple
finite-dimensional complex representation of $G$ in the class $c$, fixed by the axiom of choice.

articles.title: Products of central-scalar generators stay in their span
articles.statement:
Let $\rho$ be an irreducible
representation of a finite group $G$ on a finite-dimensional complex vector space $V$, and let
$S_\rho$ be the finite set of complex numbers consisting of $1$ and the scalars by which the
class sums of the conjugacy classes of $G$ act on $V$. If $a, b \in S_\rho$, then $ab$ lies in
the $\mathbb{Z}$-linear span of $S_\rho$.

articles.title: Generators of the central-scalar ring
articles.statement:
Let $\rho$ be an irreducible representation of a
finite group $G$ on a finite-dimensional complex vector space $V$, and let $\omega_\rho(C)$ be
the scalar by which the class sum of a conjugacy class $C$ acts on $V$. The set $S_\rho$ is the
finite set of complex numbers consisting of $1$ and the values $\omega_\rho(C)$ for all
conjugacy classes $C$ of $G$.

articles.title: Ring generated by the central scalars
articles.statement:
Let $\rho$ be an irreducible representation of a
finite group $G$ on a finite-dimensional complex vector space $V$, and let $S_\rho$ be the finite
set of complex numbers consisting of $1$ and the scalars by which the class sums of the
conjugacy classes of $G$ act on $V$. The $\mathbb{Z}$-linear span of $S_\rho$ is closed under
multiplication, and this is that span as a $\mathbb{Z}$-subalgebra of $\mathbb{C}$.

articles.title: Self-orthogonality of an irreducible character
articles.statement:
Let $\rho$ be an irreducible representation
of a finite group $G$ on a finite-dimensional complex vector space, with character $\chi$. Then
$\sum_{g \in G} \chi(g)\chi(g^{-1}) = |G|$.

articles.title: Irreducible representations are simple
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group and $\sigma$ an
irreducible representation of $G$ on a finite-dimensional complex vector space $V$. Then $V$ with
the action $\sigma$ is a simple object of the category of finite-dimensional complex
representations of $G$.

articles.title: Class structure constants are class functions
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group, let
$g_i, g_j \in G$ with conjugacy classes $C_{g_i}$ and $C_{g_j}$, and for $z \in G$ let $a(z)$ be
the number of pairs $(x, y) \in C_{g_i} \times C_{g_j}$ with $x y = z$. If $u, z \in G$ are
conjugate, then $a(u) = a(z)$.

articles.title: Structure constants of a pair of subsets
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group. For finite subsets
$C_i, C_j \subseteq G$ and an element $z \in G$, the structure constant is the number of pairs
$(x, y) \in C_i \times C_j$ with $xy = z$.

articles.title: Sum of squared degrees
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group and, for each isomorphism class $c$ of
simple finite-dimensional complex representations of $G$, let $\chi_c$ be its character. Then
$\sum_c \chi_c(1)^2 = |G|$, where the sum runs over all such classes $c$.

articles.title: Splitting a sum over conjugacy classes
articles.statement:
For a finite group $G$ and every function
$f : G \to \mathbb{C}$, $\sum_{g \in G} f(g) = \sum_{l} \sum_{x \in l} f(x)$, where $l$ runs over
the conjugacy classes of $G$.

articles.title: The trivial irreducible class
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group. The trivial representation of
$G$ on $\mathbb{C}$, where every element of $G$ acts as the identity, is simple, and this is its
class among the isomorphism classes of simple finite-dimensional complex representations of
$G$.

articles.title: The averaging operator of a class function is $G$-equivariant
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group,
let $M$ be a module over the group algebra $\mathbb{C}[G]$ with a compatible $\mathbb{C}$-module
structure, and write $\rho(h)$ for the action of $h \in G$ on $M$. If $f : G \to \mathbb{C}$ is a
class function, then its averaging operator $T_f = \sum_{g \in G} f(g)\,\rho(g^{-1})$ satisfies
$\rho(h)(T_f x) = T_f(\rho(h) x)$ for all $h \in G$ and $x \in M$.

articles.title: Zimmerman's averaging operator
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group, let $M$ be a module over the
group algebra $\mathbb{C}[G]$ with a compatible $\mathbb{C}$-module structure, and write
$\rho(g)$ for the action of $g \in G$ on $M$. For a function $f : G \to \mathbb{C}$, the averaging
operator of $f$ is the $\mathbb{C}$-linear endomorphism $T_f = \sum_{g \in G} f(g)\,\rho(g^{-1})$
of $M$.

articles.title: Irreducible complex representation degrees
articles.statement:
For a group $G$, the set of natural numbers $d$
such that $G$ has an irreducible complex representation of finite dimension $d$; for a finite
group these are the degrees $\chi(1)$ of its irreducible characters.

articles.title: Largest $p$-adic exponent of the irreducible degrees
articles.statement:
For a natural number $p$ and a group
$G$, $e_p(G)$ is the supremum in $\mathbb{N}$ of the exponents of $p$ in the prime factorizations
of the dimensions of the finite-dimensional irreducible complex representations of $G$, where the
supremum of an empty or unbounded set is $0$. For a prime $p$ and a finite group $G$, it is the
largest $e$ such that $p^e$ divides the degree $\chi(1)$ of some irreducible character $\chi$ of
$G$.

articles.title: Character degrees of Sylow subgroups are bounded in terms of those of the group
articles.statement:
There is a
function $f \colon \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ such that for every prime $p$, every finite group
$G$ and every Sylow $p$-subgroup $P$ of $G$, $e_p(P) \le f(e_p(G))$, where $e_p(H)$ is the
largest exponent of $p$ dividing an irreducible character degree of $H$.

One function works for all primes, since Yang and Qian's bound $|G : F(G)|_p \le p^{k e_p(G)}$,
with $F(G)$ the Fitting subgroup of $G$, has an absolute constant $k$.

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Archive of Solved Problems, Problem 15.62 (A. Moretó); resolution: Yong Yang and Guohua Qian, Adv. Math. 328 (2018), 356-366, abstract (|G : F(G)|_p ≤ p^(k e_p(G)) for a constant k, F(G) the Fitting subgroup, which settles Moretó's conjecture that e_p(P) = log_p b(P), b(P) the largest character degree of P, is bounded by a function of e_p(G)); Kourovka Archive, Problem 15.62 (answer: Yes, it is true); the solvable case is due to A. Moretó and T. R. Wolf, Adv. Math. 184 (2004), 18-36.

articles.title: Kourovka Problem 15.62 ($p$-parts of character degrees of Sylow subgroups)
articles.statement:
The statement,
asked by A. Moretó, that there is a function $f \colon \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ such that
$e_p(P) \le f(e_p(G))$ for every prime $p$, every finite group $G$ and every Sylow $p$-subgroup $P$
of $G$, where $e_p(H)$ is the largest exponent of $p$ dividing an irreducible character degree of
$H$.

articles.title: Equivalent complex matrix representations (Kourovka 16.67)
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a group and $n$ a
natural number. Two homomorphisms $\rho, \sigma \colon G \to \mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{C})$ are
equivalent when there is a single invertible matrix $P \in \mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{C})$ with
$\sigma(g) = P \rho(g) P^{-1}$ for every $g \in G$.

articles.title: Irreducible complex matrix representations (Kourovka 16.67)
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a group and $n$ a
natural number. A homomorphism $\rho \colon G \to \mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{C})$ is irreducible when
$n \ge 1$ and every subspace $W$ of $\mathbb{C}^n$ such that $\rho(g) v \in W$ for all $g \in G$
and all $v \in W$ is either $0$ or $\mathbb{C}^n$.

articles.title: Symmetric groups have many irreducible characters of equal degree
articles.statement:
Moretó's conjecture
holds: for every natural number $k$ there is a natural number $n_0$ such that for every
$n \ge n_0$ there are a natural number $d$ and irreducible representations
$\rho_1, \dots, \rho_k$ of the symmetric group $S_n$ into $\mathrm{GL}_d(\mathbb{C})$ that are
pairwise inequivalent.

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Archive of Solved Problems, Problem 16.67 (A. Moretó); resolution: D. A. Craven, Symmetric group character degrees and hook numbers, Proc. London Math. Soc. (3) 96 (2008), 26-50, arXiv:0709.0897, Theorem 1.2 (the size of a largest set of irreducible characters of S_n of one degree tends to infinity), the case k = 1 of Theorem 1.1 (for any k and ℓ and all sufficiently large n, S_n has k disjoint sets of ℓ irreducible characters, equal degrees within each set); Kourovka Archive, Problem 16.67 (This is proved), https://arxiv.org/abs/0709.0897.

articles.title: Moretó's conjecture on equal character degrees of symmetric groups
articles.statement:
For every natural
number $k$ there is a natural number $n_0$ such that for every $n \ge n_0$ there are a natural
number $d$ and irreducible representations $\rho_1, \dots, \rho_k$ of the symmetric group $S_n$
into $\mathrm{GL}_d(\mathbb{C})$ that are pairwise inequivalent: $\rho_i$ and $\rho_j$ are not
equivalent whenever $i \ne j$.

Since irreducible complex characters correspond to equivalence classes of irreducible complex
representations and the degree of a character is the dimension, this says that $S_n$ has at least
$k$ distinct irreducible complex characters of the same degree.

articles.title: Kourovka Problem 11.97 has a negative answer
articles.statement:
There is a finite set $S$ of complex numbers
such that for every natural number $N$ there is a finite non-abelian simple group $G$ with more
than $N$ elements and an element $g \in G$ at which the set of values of the irreducible complex
characters of $G$ is exactly $S$.

The Kourovka Archive records (V. D. Mazurov) that every complex irreducible character of
$L_2(2^m)$, $m \ge 2$, takes a value in $\{0, 1, -1\}$ at an involution, so some subset of
$\{0, 1, -1\}$ is the set of values at an involution for infinitely many of these non-abelian
simple groups.

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Archive of Solved Problems, Problem 11.97 (S. P. Strunkov); resolution: V. D. Mazurov, Kourovka Archive, Problem 11.97: "No; all complex irreducible characters of the groups `L_2(2^m)`, `m ≥ 2`, take the values `0, ±1` on involutions", https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v49.

articles.title: Kourovka Problem 11.97 (simple groups with a given set of character values)
articles.statement:
The
statement that for every finite set $S$ of complex numbers there is a bound $N$ such that every
finite non-abelian simple group $G$ having an element $g$ at which the set of values of the
irreducible complex characters of $G$ is exactly $S$ has order at most $N$. The problem is due to
S. P. Strunkov.

"Only finitely many such groups" up to isomorphism is stated as this bound on the order.

articles.title: Values of the irreducible characters at an element
articles.statement:
For an element $g$ of a group $G$, the
set of complex numbers $\chi(g)$, where $\chi$ ranges over the characters of the irreducible
finite-dimensional complex representations of $G$.

articles.title: Convolution theorem for one-dimensional characters
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group, let
$\varphi : G \to \mathbb{C}$ satisfy $\varphi(1) = 1$ and $\varphi(xy) = \varphi(x)\varphi(y)$
for all $x, y \in G$ (a one-dimensional character), and let $f, g : G \to \mathbb{C}$. Writing
$f \ast g$ for the convolution $(f \ast g)(x) = \sum_{y \in G} f(y)\, g(y^{-1} x)$, we have

$$
\sum_{x \in G} \varphi(x)\,(f \ast g)(x) =
\Big(\sum_{x \in G} \varphi(x) f(x)\Big)\Big(\sum_{x \in G} \varphi(x) g(x)\Big).
$$

Proof: Swap the finite sums, reindex by $x = yz$, and use multiplicativity of $\varphi$ to
factor the character pairing, following Terras, Ch. 2–3.

## Sources

- A. Terras, Fourier Analysis on Finite Groups and Applications, Ch. 2–3 (the Fourier transform takes convolution to pointwise products).

articles.title: Associativity of convolution
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group and write $f \ast g$ for the
convolution $(f \ast g)(x) = \sum_{y \in G} f(y)\, g(y^{-1} x)$ of functions on $G$. For all
$f, g, h : G \to \mathbb{C}$ we have $(f \ast g) \ast h = f \ast (g \ast h)$.

Proof: Expand into double sums, swap them, and reindex by left multiplication,
following the finite group-algebra argument in Terras, Ch. 1.

## Sources

- A. Terras, Fourier Analysis on Finite Groups and Applications, Ch. 1 (the group algebra).

articles.title: Convolution on a finite abelian group is commutative
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite abelian group and
write $f \ast g$ for the convolution $(f \ast g)(x) = \sum_{y \in G} f(y)\, g(y^{-1} x)$ of
functions on $G$. For all $f, g : G \to \mathbb{C}$ we have $f \ast g = g \ast f$.

Proof: Reindex by $y \mapsto y^{-1} x$ and use commutativity in $G$ and in $\mathbb{C}$,
as in the commutative group-algebra argument in Terras, Ch. 2.

## Sources

- A. Terras, Fourier Analysis on Finite Groups and Applications, Ch. 2 (commutative group algebra of an abelian group).

articles.title: The delta function at the identity is a left unit for convolution
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group,
write $f \ast g$ for the convolution $(f \ast g)(x) = \sum_{y \in G} f(y)\, g(y^{-1} x)$ of
functions on $G$, and let $\delta_1 : G \to \mathbb{C}$ be given by $\delta_1(1) = 1$ and
$\delta_1(x) = 0$ for $x \neq 1$. Then $\delta_1 \ast f = f$ for every $f : G \to \mathbb{C}$.

Proof: Expand the convolution and collapse the sum at the unique nonzero value
of the delta function, following the identity-element argument in Terras, Ch. 1.

## Sources

- A. Terras, Fourier Analysis on Finite Groups and Applications, Ch. 1 (identity of the group algebra).

articles.title: Convolution on a finite group
articles.statement:
For a finite group $G$ and functions
$f, g : G \to \mathbb{C}$, the convolution $f \ast g : G \to \mathbb{C}$ is defined by
$(f \ast g)(x) = \sum_{y \in G} f(y)\, g(y^{-1} x)$ for $x \in G$.

articles.title: Frobenius determinant theorem
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group and let $r$ be the number of
conjugacy classes of $G$. Then there exist polynomials $p_1, \dots, p_r$ in
$\mathbb{C}[x_g : g \in G]$ such that each $p_j$ is irreducible, $p_i$ and $p_j$ are not associated
for $i \neq j$, and the group determinant of $G$ equals $\prod_{j=1}^{r} p_j^{\deg p_j}$, where
$\deg p_j$ is the total degree of $p_j$.

## Sources

- Knill, *Some fundamental theorems in mathematics*, §171. Problem `frobenius_group_determinant` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Group determinant
articles.statement:
For a finite group $G$, the group determinant $\Theta(G)$ is the
determinant of the group matrix of $G$, the $G \times G$ matrix over $\mathbb{C}[x_g : g \in G]$
whose entry at $(g, h)$ is the variable $x_{gh}$; it is a polynomial in these variables.

articles.title: Group matrix
articles.statement:
For a finite group $G$, the group matrix of Dedekind and Frobenius is the
$G \times G$ matrix over the polynomial ring $\mathbb{C}[x_g : g \in G]$ whose entry at $(g, h)$ is
the variable $x_{gh}$.

articles.title: The Gaussian integers $\alpha_i$
articles.statement:
For
$a \colon \mathbb{Z}/4 \times \mathbb{Z}/4 \to \mathbb{Z}$ with differences $d_0, \dots, d_7$ (so
$d_i = a(i, 0) - a(i, 2)$ and $d_{i+4} = a(i, 1) - a(i, 3)$ for $0 \le i \le 3$), the Gaussian
integers $\alpha_0, \dots, \alpha_3 \in \mathbb{Z}[\sqrt{-1}]$ are
$\alpha_i = d_i + d_{i+4} \sqrt{-1}$.

## Sources

- Yuka Yamaguchi and Naoya Yamaguchi, *Integer Group Determinants for C_4^2*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A30, Section 2 (notation after Corollary 2).

articles.title: The sums $b_i$
articles.statement:
For $a \colon \mathbb{Z}/4 \times \mathbb{Z}/4 \to \mathbb{Z}$ and
$i \in \mathbb{Z}/4$, $b_i = \bigl(a(i, 0) + a(i, 2)\bigr) + \bigl(a(i, 1) + a(i, 3)\bigr)$. In the
paper's indexing $a_{r + 4s} = a(r, s)$ this is $b_i = (a_i + a_{i+8}) + (a_{i+4} + a_{i+12})$
for $0 \le i \le 3$.

## Sources

- Yuka Yamaguchi and Naoya Yamaguchi, *Integer Group Determinants for C_4^2*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A30, Section 2 (notation after Corollary 2).

articles.title: The Gaussian integer $\beta$
articles.statement:
For $a \colon \mathbb{Z}/4 \times \mathbb{Z}/4 \to \mathbb{Z}$
with Gaussian integers $\alpha_0, \dots, \alpha_3$,
$\beta = (\alpha_0 + \alpha_2)^2 - (\alpha_1 + \alpha_3)^2 \in \mathbb{Z}[\sqrt{-1}]$.

## Sources

- Yuka Yamaguchi and Naoya Yamaguchi, *Integer Group Determinants for C_4^2*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A30, Section 2 (definition before Lemma 1).

articles.title: The alternating sums $c_i$
articles.statement:
For $a \colon \mathbb{Z}/4 \times \mathbb{Z}/4 \to \mathbb{Z}$
and $i \in \mathbb{Z}/4$, $c_i = \bigl(a(i, 0) + a(i, 2)\bigr) - \bigl(a(i, 1) + a(i, 3)\bigr)$. In
the paper's indexing $a_{r + 4s} = a(r, s)$ this is $c_i = (a_i + a_{i+8}) - (a_{i+4} + a_{i+12})$
for $0 \le i \le 3$.

## Sources

- Yuka Yamaguchi and Naoya Yamaguchi, *Integer Group Determinants for C_4^2*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A30, Section 2 (notation after Corollary 2).

articles.title: Factorization shapes of $D_4(b) D_4(c)$
articles.statement:
Let
$a \colon \mathbb{Z}/4 \times \mathbb{Z}/4 \to \mathbb{Z}$ have sums $b_i$ and alternating sums
$c_i$, let $D_4$ be the $4 \times 4$ circulant determinant, and suppose
$b_0 + b_2 \not\equiv b_1 + b_3 \pmod 2$. Put $x = b_0 b_2 + b_1 b_3$, $y = c_0 c_2 + c_1 c_3$
and $D = D_4(b) D_4(c)$. If $(x, y) \equiv (0, 0)$ or $(2, 2) \pmod 4$, then
$D = (8k + 1)(8l + 1)$ for some integers $k \equiv l \pmod 2$. If
$(x, y) \equiv (0, 2)$ or $(2, 0) \pmod 4$, then $D = (8k + 1)(8l + 1)$ for some integers
$k \not\equiv l \pmod 2$. If $(x, y) \equiv (1, 1)$ or $(-1, -1) \pmod 4$, then
$D = (8k - 3)(8l - 3)$ for some integers $k \equiv l \pmod 2$. If
$(x, y) \equiv (1, -1)$ or $(-1, 1) \pmod 4$, then $D = (8k - 3)(8l - 3)$ for some integers
$k \not\equiv l \pmod 2$.

## Sources

- Yuka Yamaguchi and Naoya Yamaguchi, *Integer Group Determinants for C_4^2*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A30, Lemma 9.

articles.title: $D_4(b) D_4(c)$ modulo $16$
articles.statement:
Let
$a \colon \mathbb{Z}/4 \times \mathbb{Z}/4 \to \mathbb{Z}$ have sums $b_i$ and alternating sums
$c_i$, and let $D_4$ be the $4 \times 4$ circulant determinant. If
$b_0 + b_2 \not\equiv b_1 + b_3 \pmod 2$, then
$D_4(b) D_4(c) \equiv 1 - 4(b_0 b_2 + b_1 b_3 + c_0 c_2 + c_1 c_3) \pmod{16}$.

## Sources

- Yuka Yamaguchi and Naoya Yamaguchi, *Integer Group Determinants for C_4^2*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A30, Lemma 10.

articles.title: A prime factor $8l - 3$ of $D_4(b) D_4(c)$
articles.statement:
Let
$a \colon \mathbb{Z}/4 \times \mathbb{Z}/4 \to \mathbb{Z}$ have sums $b_i$, alternating sums
$c_i$ and Gaussian integer $\beta$, let $D_4$ be the $4 \times 4$ circulant determinant, and let
$P$ be the set of positive primes $p \equiv 5 \pmod 8$. Suppose
$b_0 + b_2 \not\equiv b_1 + b_3 \pmod 2$ and that the norm $\beta \bar\beta \equiv -3 \pmod 8$,
and put $Q = b_0 b_2 + b_1 b_3 + c_0 c_2 + c_1 c_3$. If $Q \equiv 0 \pmod 4$, then
$D_4(b) D_4(c) = (8k - 3)(8l - 3)$ for some integers $k \not\equiv l \pmod 2$ with
$8l - 3 \in P$. If $Q \equiv 2 \pmod 4$, then $D_4(b) D_4(c) = (8k - 3)(8l - 3)$ for some
integers $k \equiv l \pmod 2$ with $8l - 3 \in P$.

## Sources

- Yuka Yamaguchi and Naoya Yamaguchi, *Integer Group Determinants for C_4^2*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A30, Lemma 11.

articles.title: The power of $2$ in $D_4(b) D_4(c)$
articles.statement:
Let
$a \colon \mathbb{Z}/4 \times \mathbb{Z}/4 \to \mathbb{Z}$ have sums $b_i$ and alternating sums
$c_i$, let $D_4$ be the $4 \times 4$ circulant determinant, put $D = D_4(b) D_4(c)$, and say
that $D \in 2^e \mathbb{Z}_{\mathrm{odd}}$ when $D = 2^e (2t + 1)$ for some integer $t$.
If every $b_i$ is even, then $D \in 2^8 \mathbb{Z}_{\mathrm{odd}}$ when
$b_0 + b_1 + b_2 + b_3 \equiv c_0 + c_1 + c_2 + c_3 \equiv 2 \pmod 4$, and $2^{12} \mid D$
otherwise. If every $b_i$ is odd, then $D \in 2^8 \mathbb{Z}_{\mathrm{odd}}$ under the same
condition, and $2^{11} \mid D$ otherwise. If $b_0 \equiv b_2$, $b_1 \equiv b_3$ and
$b_0 \not\equiv b_1 \pmod 2$, then $D \in 2^{10} \mathbb{Z}_{\mathrm{odd}}$ when
$b_0 - b_2 \equiv b_1 - b_3 \equiv c_0 - c_2 \equiv c_1 - c_3 \equiv 2 \pmod 4$, and
$2^{11} \mid D$ otherwise. If $b_0 + b_2$ and $b_1 + b_3$ are both odd, put
$u = (b_0 + b_2)(b_1 + b_3)$ and $v = (c_0 + c_2)(c_1 + c_3)$; then
$D \in 2^8 \mathbb{Z}_{\mathrm{odd}}$ when $u \equiv \pm 3$ and $v \equiv \pm 3 \pmod 8$, and
$2^9 \mid D$ otherwise.

## Sources

- Yuka Yamaguchi and Naoya Yamaguchi, *Integer Group Determinants for C_4^2*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A30, Lemma 15.

articles.title: Two conditions forcing $b_0 b_2 + b_1 b_3 + c_0 c_2 + c_1 c_3 \equiv 2 \pmod 4$
articles.statement:
Let
$a \colon \mathbb{Z}/4 \times \mathbb{Z}/4 \to \mathbb{Z}$ have sums $b_i$, alternating sums
$c_i$ and Gaussian integers $\beta$, $\gamma$; let $D_4$ be the $4 \times 4$ circulant
determinant, and put $D = D_4(b) D_4(c)$, $N = \beta \bar\beta \gamma \bar\gamma$ and
$Q = b_0 b_2 + b_1 b_3 + c_0 c_2 + c_1 c_3$. If every $b_i$ is odd and $D = 2^{11} (2t + 1)$
for some integer $t$, then $Q \equiv 2 \pmod 4$. If $b_0 \equiv b_2$, $b_1 \equiv b_3$ and
$b_0 \not\equiv b_1 \pmod 2$, and $D = 2^{11} (2t + 1)$ and $N = 2^4 (2s + 1)$ for some
integers $t$ and $s$, then $Q \equiv 2 \pmod 4$.

## Sources

- Yuka Yamaguchi and Naoya Yamaguchi, *Integer Group Determinants for C_4^2*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A30, Lemma 17.

articles.title: Cross terms of the $d_i$ modulo $4$
Difference of the squared sums of squares of the $d_i$
articles.statement:
Let
$a \colon \mathbb{Z}/4 \times \mathbb{Z}/4 \to \mathbb{Z}$, and let $d_i = a(i, 0) - a(i, 2)$ and
$d_{i+4} = a(i, 1) - a(i, 3)$ for $0 \le i \le 3$. Then

$$
\bigl((d_0 + d_2)^2 + (d_4 + d_6)^2 + (d_1 + d_3)^2 + (d_5 + d_7)^2\bigr)^2 -
\bigl((d_0 - d_2)^2 + (d_4 - d_6)^2 + (d_1 - d_3)^2 + (d_5 - d_7)^2\bigr)^2 =
8 \Bigl(\sum_{i=0}^{7} d_i^2\Bigr)(d_0 d_2 + d_4 d_6 + d_1 d_3 + d_5 d_7).
$$

## Sources

- Yuka Yamaguchi and Naoya Yamaguchi, *Integer Group Determinants for C_4^2*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A30, Lemma 4.

articles.title: The differences $d_i$ of a function on $C_4^2$
articles.statement:
For
$a \colon \mathbb{Z}/4 \times \mathbb{Z}/4 \to \mathbb{Z}$, the integers $d_0, \dots, d_7$ are
$d_i = a(i, 0) - a(i, 2)$ and $d_{i+4} = a(i, 1) - a(i, 3)$ for $0 \le i \le 3$. Writing
$a_{r + 4s}$ for $a(r, s)$, this is the paper's $d_i = a_i - a_{i+8}$ for $0 \le i \le 7$.

## Sources

- Yuka Yamaguchi and Naoya Yamaguchi, *Integer Group Determinants for C_4^2*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A30, Section 2 (notation after Corollary 2).

articles.title: The exceptional set $A$ for $C_4^2$
articles.statement:
Let $P$ be the set of positive primes
$p \equiv 5 \pmod 8$. The set $A \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ consists of all products
$(8k - 3)(8l - 3)(8m - 3)(8n - 3)$ with $k, l, m, n \in \mathbb{Z}$ such that $8l - 3$,
$8m - 3$ and $8n - 3$ lie in $P$ and $k + l \not\equiv m + n \pmod 2$.

## Sources

- Yuka Yamaguchi and Naoya Yamaguchi, *Integer Group Determinants for C_4^2*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A30, Theorem 1 (definition of `A`).

articles.title: The Gaussian integer $\gamma$ of a function on $C_4^2$
articles.statement:
For
$a \colon \mathbb{Z}/4 \times \mathbb{Z}/4 \to \mathbb{Z}$, let
$\alpha_i = (a(i, 0) - a(i, 2)) + (a(i, 1) - a(i, 3))\sqrt{-1} \in \mathbb{Z}[\sqrt{-1}]$
for $0 \le i \le 3$. Then
$\gamma = (\alpha_0 - \alpha_2)^2 + (\alpha_1 - \alpha_3)^2 \in \mathbb{Z}[\sqrt{-1}]$.

## Sources

- Yuka Yamaguchi and Naoya Yamaguchi, *Integer Group Determinants for C_4^2*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A30, Section 2 (definition before Lemma 1).

articles.title: The group determinant of $C_4^2$ modulo $2$
articles.statement:
Let $a \colon \mathbb{Z}/4 \times \mathbb{Z}/4 \to \mathbb{Z}$. For $0 \le i \le 3$ let
$b_i = a(i, 0) + a(i, 2) + a(i, 1) + a(i, 3)$, $c_i = a(i, 0) + a(i, 2) - a(i, 1) - a(i, 3)$
and $\alpha_i = (a(i, 0) - a(i, 2)) + (a(i, 1) - a(i, 3))\sqrt{-1} \in \mathbb{Z}[\sqrt{-1}]$,
and let $\beta = (\alpha_0 + \alpha_2)^2 - (\alpha_1 + \alpha_3)^2$ and
$\gamma = (\alpha_0 - \alpha_2)^2 + (\alpha_1 - \alpha_3)^2$, with complex conjugates $\bar\beta$
and $\bar\gamma$. Let $D_4(x_0, x_1, x_2, x_3)$ be the determinant of the $4 \times 4$
circulant matrix with first row $(x_0, x_1, x_2, x_3)$.
Then the group determinant $D_{4 \times 4}(a) = \det\bigl(a(h - g)\bigr)_{g, h}$, with $g, h$
ranging over $\mathbb{Z}/4 \times \mathbb{Z}/4$, satisfies
$D_{4 \times 4}(a) \equiv D_4(b) \equiv D_4(c) \equiv \beta\bar\beta \equiv \gamma\bar\gamma
\pmod 2$.

## Sources

- Yuka Yamaguchi and Naoya Yamaguchi, *Integer Group Determinants for C_4^2*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A30, Lemma 2.

articles.title: Factorization of the complex group determinant of $C_4^2$
articles.statement:
For every
$y \colon \mathbb{Z}/4 \times \mathbb{Z}/4 \to \mathbb{C}$,

$$
\det\bigl(y(h - g)\bigr)_{g, h \in \mathbb{Z}/4 \times \mathbb{Z}/4} =
\prod_{k=0}^{3} D_4\bigl(z_k(0), z_k(1), z_k(2), z_k(3)\bigr), \qquad
z_k(r) = \sum_{s=0}^{3} i^{ks} y(r, s),
$$

where $i = \sqrt{-1}$ and $D_4(x_0, x_1, x_2, x_3)$ is the determinant of the $4 \times 4$
circulant matrix with first row $(x_0, x_1, x_2, x_3)$.

## Sources

- Yuka Yamaguchi and Naoya Yamaguchi, *Integer Group Determinants for C_4^2*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A30, Corollary 2.

articles.title: A prime factor $p \equiv 5 \pmod 8$ of $D_4(b) D_4(c) \beta\bar\beta \gamma\bar\gamma$
articles.statement:
Let $a \colon \mathbb{Z}/4 \times \mathbb{Z}/4 \to \mathbb{Z}$. For $0 \le i \le 3$ let
$b_i = a(i, 0) + a(i, 2) + a(i, 1) + a(i, 3)$, $c_i = a(i, 0) + a(i, 2) - a(i, 1) - a(i, 3)$
and $\alpha_i = (a(i, 0) - a(i, 2)) + (a(i, 1) - a(i, 3))\sqrt{-1} \in \mathbb{Z}[\sqrt{-1}]$,
and let $\beta = (\alpha_0 + \alpha_2)^2 - (\alpha_1 + \alpha_3)^2$ and
$\gamma = (\alpha_0 - \alpha_2)^2 + (\alpha_1 - \alpha_3)^2$, with complex conjugates $\bar\beta$
and $\bar\gamma$. Let $D_4(x_0, x_1, x_2, x_3)$ be the determinant of the $4 \times 4$
circulant matrix with first row $(x_0, x_1, x_2, x_3)$.
Let $P$ be the set of positive primes $p \equiv 5 \pmod 8$. Suppose that $b_0 + b_2$ and
$b_1 + b_3$ are odd, that $D_4(b) D_4(c) = 2^8 (2t + 1)$ for some integer $t$, and that
$\beta\bar\beta \gamma\bar\gamma = 2^7 (2t' + 1)$ for some integer $t'$. Then there are $p \in P$
and $m \in \mathbb{Z}$ with $D_4(b) D_4(c) \beta\bar\beta \gamma\bar\gamma = 2^{15} p (2m + 1)$.

## Sources

- Yuka Yamaguchi and Naoya Yamaguchi, *Integer Group Determinants for C_4^2*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A30, Lemma 19.

articles.title: Basic integer group determinants of $C_4^2$
articles.statement:
For every integer $m$, the integers
$16m + 1$, $2^{16} (4m + 1)$, $2^{16} (4m - 1)$ and $2^{16} \cdot 2m$ all lie in the set
$S(C_4^2)$ of integer group determinants of $C_4^2 = \mathbb{Z}/4 \times \mathbb{Z}/4$.

## Sources

- Yuka Yamaguchi and Naoya Yamaguchi, *Integer Group Determinants for C_4^2*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A30, Lemma 20.

articles.title: Four-factor integer group determinants of $C_4^2$
articles.statement:
Let
$P$ be the set of positive primes $p \equiv 5 \pmod 8$, and let $k, l, m, n$ be integers such
that $16l - 3$, $16l + 5$, $16m - 3$, $16m + 5$, $16n - 3$ and $16n + 5$ all lie in $P$. Then
the four integers $(16k - 3)(16l + 5)(16m - 3)(16n - 3)$,
$(16k - 3)(16l + 5)(16m + 5)(16n + 5)$, $(16k + 5)(16l - 3)(16m - 3)(16n - 3)$ and
$(16k + 5)(16l - 3)(16m + 5)(16n + 5)$ all lie in the set $S(C_4^2)$ of integer group
determinants of $C_4^2 = \mathbb{Z}/4 \times \mathbb{Z}/4$.

All six membership hypotheses are assumed for each of the four conclusions, as in the paper's
shared hypothesis list.

## Sources

- Yuka Yamaguchi and Naoya Yamaguchi, *Integer Group Determinants for C_4^2*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A30, Lemma 21.

articles.title: Integer group determinants of $C_4^2$ of the form $2^{15} p (2m + 1)$
articles.statement:
Let $P$ be
the set of positive primes $p \equiv 5 \pmod 8$. For every integer $m$ and every $p \in P$, the
integer $2^{15} p (2m + 1)$ lies in the set $S(C_4^2)$ of integer group determinants of
$C_4^2 = \mathbb{Z}/4 \times \mathbb{Z}/4$.

## Sources

- Yuka Yamaguchi and Naoya Yamaguchi, *Integer Group Determinants for C_4^2*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A30, Lemma 22.

articles.title: Norms of β and γ as differences of squares (C₄²)
articles.statement:
Let $a$ be an integer-valued function
on $C_4^2 = \mathbb{Z}/4 \times \mathbb{Z}/4$, with associated integers $d_0, \dots, d_7$ and
Gaussian integers $\beta$, $\gamma$, and write $\beta\bar\beta$, $\gamma\bar\gamma$ for the norms of
$\beta$ and $\gamma$. Then

$$\beta\bar\beta = \bigl((d_0 + d_2)^2 + (d_4 + d_6)^2 + (d_1 + d_3)^2 + (d_5 + d_7)^2\bigr)^2 -
4\bigl((d_0 + d_2)(d_1 + d_3) + (d_4 + d_6)(d_5 + d_7)\bigr)^2$$

and

$$\gamma\bar\gamma = \bigl((d_0 - d_2)^2 + (d_4 - d_6)^2 + (d_1 - d_3)^2 + (d_5 - d_7)^2\bigr)^2 -
4\bigl((d_0 - d_2)(d_5 - d_7) - (d_4 - d_6)(d_1 - d_3)\bigr)^2.$$

## Sources

- Yuka Yamaguchi and Naoya Yamaguchi, *Integer Group Determinants for C_4^2*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A30, Lemma 3.

articles.title: Norms of β and γ as products of sums of two squares (C₄²)
articles.statement:
Let $a$ be an integer-valued
function on $C_4^2 = \mathbb{Z}/4 \times \mathbb{Z}/4$, with associated integers $d_0, \dots, d_7$
and Gaussian integers $\beta$, $\gamma$, and write $\beta\bar\beta$, $\gamma\bar\gamma$ for the
norms of $\beta$ and $\gamma$. Then

$$\beta\bar\beta = \bigl((d_0 + d_2 + d_1 + d_3)^2 + (d_4 + d_6 + d_5 + d_7)^2\bigr)
\bigl((d_0 + d_2 - d_1 - d_3)^2 + (d_4 + d_6 - d_5 - d_7)^2\bigr)$$

and

$$\gamma\bar\gamma = \bigl((d_0 - d_2 - d_5 + d_7)^2 + (d_4 - d_6 + d_1 - d_3)^2\bigr)
\bigl((d_0 - d_2 + d_5 - d_7)^2 + (d_4 - d_6 - d_1 + d_3)^2\bigr).$$

## Sources

- Yuka Yamaguchi and Naoya Yamaguchi, *Integer Group Determinants for C_4^2*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A30, Lemma 1.

articles.title: A prime factor p ≡ −3 mod 8 of ββ̄γγ̄ in the even case (C₄²)
articles.statement:
Let $a$ be an integer-valued
function on $C_4^2 = \mathbb{Z}/4 \times \mathbb{Z}/4$, with associated integers $b_i$, $c_i$
$(0 \le i \le 3)$ and Gaussian integers $\beta$, $\gamma$, write $\beta\bar\beta$ and
$\gamma\bar\gamma$ for the norms of $\beta$ and $\gamma$, and let $P$ be the set of primes
$p \equiv -3 \pmod 8$. Suppose that $b_0 + b_2 \equiv b_1 + b_3 \equiv 0 \pmod 2$, that
$\beta\bar\beta\gamma\bar\gamma = 2^4(2t + 1)$ for some integer $t$, and that
$b_0b_2 + b_1b_3 + c_0c_2 + c_1c_3 \equiv 2 \pmod 4$. Then
$\beta\bar\beta\gamma\bar\gamma = 2^4 p(2m + 1)$ for some $p \in P$ and some integer $m$.

## Sources

- Yuka Yamaguchi and Naoya Yamaguchi, *Integer Group Determinants for C_4^2*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A30, Lemma 18.

articles.title: Two prime factors ≡ −3 mod 8 of ββ̄γγ̄ (C₄²)
articles.statement:
Let $a$ be an integer-valued function on
$C_4^2 = \mathbb{Z}/4 \times \mathbb{Z}/4$, with associated integers $b_i$, $c_i$ $(0 \le i \le 3)$
and Gaussian integers $\beta$, $\gamma$, write $\beta\bar\beta$, $\gamma\bar\gamma$ for the norms of
$\beta$ and $\gamma$, let $P$ be the set of primes $p \equiv -3 \pmod 8$, and put
$Q = b_0b_2 + b_1b_3 + c_0c_2 + c_1c_3$. Suppose that $b_0 + b_2 \not\equiv b_1 + b_3 \pmod 2$ and
$\beta\bar\beta \equiv -3 \pmod 8$. If $Q \equiv 0 \pmod 4$, there are integers $j$, $m$, $n$ with
$8m - 3 \in P$, $8n - 3 \in P$, $j \equiv m + n \pmod 2$ and
$\beta\bar\beta\gamma\bar\gamma = (8j + 1)(8m - 3)(8n - 3)$. If $Q \equiv 2 \pmod 4$, the same holds
with $j \not\equiv m + n \pmod 2$ in place of $j \equiv m + n \pmod 2$.

## Sources

- Yuka Yamaguchi and Naoya Yamaguchi, *Integer Group Determinants for C_4^2*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A30, Lemma 13.

articles.title: The power of $2$ in $\beta\bar\beta\gamma\bar\gamma$
articles.statement:
Let
$a \colon \mathbb{Z}/4 \times \mathbb{Z}/4 \to \mathbb{Z}$ have sums $b_i$, alternating sums
$c_i$, differences $d_0, \dots, d_7$ and Gaussian integers $\beta$, $\gamma$, and put
$N = \beta \bar\beta \gamma \bar\gamma$, the product of the norms of $\beta$ and $\gamma$. If
$b_0 + b_2$ and $b_1 + b_3$ are both even, then $N = 2^4 (2t + 1)$ for some integer $t$ when
$b_0 + b_1 + b_2 + b_3 \not\equiv c_0 + c_1 + c_2 + c_3 \pmod 4$, and $2^8 \mid N$ when
$b_0 + b_1 + b_2 + b_3 \equiv c_0 + c_1 + c_2 + c_3 \pmod 4$. If $b_0 + b_2$ and $b_1 + b_3$
are both odd, put
$d = \bigl((d_0 + d_2)(d_5 + d_7) + (d_4 + d_6)(d_1 + d_3)\bigr)
\bigl((d_0 - d_2)(d_1 - d_3) + (d_4 - d_6)(d_5 - d_7)\bigr)$; then $N = 2^7 (2t + 1)$ for
some integer $t$ when $d \equiv 2 \pmod 4$, and $2^8 \mid N$ when $d \equiv 0 \pmod 4$.

## Sources

- Yuka Yamaguchi and Naoya Yamaguchi, *Integer Group Determinants for C_4^2*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A30, Lemma 16.

articles.title: The difference of the norms of β and γ modulo 16 (C₄²)
articles.statement:
Let $a$ be an integer-valued
function on $C_4^2 = \mathbb{Z}/4 \times \mathbb{Z}/4$, with associated integers $b_i$, $c_i$
$(0 \le i \le 3)$ and Gaussian integers $\beta$, $\gamma$, and write $\beta\bar\beta$,
$\gamma\bar\gamma$ for the norms of $\beta$ and $\gamma$. If
$b_0 + b_2 \not\equiv b_1 + b_3 \pmod 2$, then
$\beta\bar\beta - \gamma\bar\gamma \equiv 4(b_0b_2 + b_1b_3 + c_0c_2 + c_1c_3) \pmod{16}$.

## Sources

- Yuka Yamaguchi and Naoya Yamaguchi, *Integer Group Determinants for C_4^2*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A30, Lemma 12.

articles.title: The C₄² notation at the indicator of the identity
articles.statement:
Let $\delta$ be the integer-valued
function on $C_4^2 = \mathbb{Z}/4 \times \mathbb{Z}/4$ that is $1$ at $(0, 0)$ and $0$ elsewhere.
For $a = \delta$ the associated integers are $b = c = (1, 0, 0, 0)$ and
$d = (1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0)$, and the associated Gaussian integers are $\beta = \gamma = 1$.

## Sources

- Yuka Yamaguchi and Naoya Yamaguchi, *Integer Group Determinants for C_4^2*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A30, Section 2 (notation after Corollary 2).

articles.title: Factorization of the 4 × 4 circulant determinant
articles.statement:
For every commutative ring $R$ and all
$x_0, x_1, x_2, x_3 \in R$, the $4 \times 4$ circulant determinant $D_4$ satisfies

$$D_4(x_0, x_1, x_2, x_3) =
\bigl((x_0 + x_2)^2 - (x_1 + x_3)^2\bigr)\bigl((x_0 - x_2)^2 + (x_1 - x_3)^2\bigr).$$

## Sources

- Yuka Yamaguchi and Naoya Yamaguchi, *Integer Group Determinants for C_4^2*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A30, Corollary 1.

articles.title: The 4 × 4 circulant determinant modulo 16 at two parity patterns
articles.statement:
For all integers
$k$, $l$, $m$, $n$, the $4 \times 4$ circulant determinant $D_4$ satisfies
$D_4(2k + 1, 2l, 2m, 2n) \equiv 8m + 1 \pmod{16}$ and
$D_4(2k, 2l + 1, 2m + 1, 2n + 1) \equiv 8(k + l + n) - 3 \pmod{16}$.

## Sources

- Yuka Yamaguchi and Naoya Yamaguchi, *Integer Group Determinants for C_4^2*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A30, Lemma 6.

articles.title: The 4 × 4 circulant determinant of (1, 0, 0, 0)
articles.statement:
Over every commutative ring $R$, the
$4 \times 4$ circulant determinant satisfies $D_4(1, 0, 0, 0) = 1$.

## Sources

- Yuka Yamaguchi and Naoya Yamaguchi, *Integer Group Determinants for C_4^2*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A30, Section 2 (definition of `D_n`).

articles.title: Powers of $2$ dividing the $C_4$ group determinant at four parity patterns
articles.statement:
Let
$D(x_0, x_1, x_2, x_3)$ be the group determinant of $C_4$, that is the determinant of the
$4 \times 4$ circulant matrix with $(i, j)$ entry $x_{i - j}$ (indices mod $4$). For integers
$k, l, m, n$ put $D_1 = D(2k, 2l, 2m, 2n)$, $D_2 = D(2k+1, 2l+1, 2m+1, 2n+1)$,
$D_3 = D(2k, 2l+1, 2m, 2n+1)$, $D_4 = D(2k, 2l, 2m+1, 2n+1)$,
$w_3 = (2k+2l+1)(2m+2n+1)$ and $w_4 = (2k+2m+1)(2l+2n+1)$, and write $2^e \mathbb{Z}_{odd}$
for the set of integers $2^e(2t+1)$ with $t \in \mathbb{Z}$. Then:

* if $k + m \not\equiv l + n \pmod 2$ then $D_1 \in 2^4 \mathbb{Z}_{odd}$, and if
  $k + m \equiv l + n \pmod 2$ then $2^8 \mid D_1$;
* if $k + m \not\equiv l + n \pmod 2$ then $D_2 \in 2^4 \mathbb{Z}_{odd}$; if
  $(k + m)(l + n) \equiv -1 \pmod 4$ then $D_2 \in 2^7 \mathbb{Z}_{odd}$; and if
  $k + m \equiv l + n \pmod 2$ and $(k + m)(l + n) \not\equiv -1 \pmod 4$ then $2^9 \mid D_2$;
* if $k - m$ and $l - n$ are both odd then $D_3 \in 2^5 \mathbb{Z}_{odd}$; if
  $k \equiv m \pmod 2$ and $w_3 \equiv \pm 3 \pmod 8$ then $D_3 \in 2^6 \mathbb{Z}_{odd}$; and if
  neither of these two conditions holds then $2^7 \mid D_3$;
* if $w_4 \equiv \pm 3 \pmod 8$ then $D_4 \in 2^4 \mathbb{Z}_{odd}$, and if
  $w_4 \equiv \pm 1 \pmod 8$ then $2^5 \mid D_4$.

## Sources

- Yuka Yamaguchi and Naoya Yamaguchi, *Integer Group Determinants for C_4^2*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A30, Lemma 7.

articles.title: The group determinant of $C_4$
articles.statement:
For a commutative ring $R$ and
$x = (x_0, x_1, x_2, x_3) \in R^4$, $D_4(x_0, x_1, x_2, x_3)$ is the determinant of the
$4 \times 4$ circulant matrix whose $(i, j)$ entry is $x_{i - j}$, indices taken mod $4$.

## Sources

- Yuka Yamaguchi and Naoya Yamaguchi, *Integer Group Determinants for C_4^2*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A30, Section 2 (definition of `D_n`).

articles.title: Even integer group determinants of $C_4 \times C_4$
articles.statement:
Let $C_4$ be the cyclic group of
order $4$, $S(C_4^2)$ the set of integer group determinants of $C_4 \times C_4$ and $P$ the set
of positive primes $p \equiv -3 \pmod 8$, and let $z \in S(C_4^2)$. If $z$ is even, then
$2^{15} \mid z$. If $z = 2^{15}(2t + 1)$ for some integer $t$, then $z = 2^{15} p (2m + 1)$ for
some $p \in P$ and some integer $m$.

## Sources

- Yuka Yamaguchi and Naoya Yamaguchi, *Integer Group Determinants for C_4^2*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A30, Lemma 14.

articles.title: $5$ and $13$ lie in $P$
articles.statement:
The integers $5$ and $13$ both belong to the set $P$ of
positive primes $p \equiv -3 \pmod 8$.

## Sources

- Yuka Yamaguchi and Naoya Yamaguchi, *Integer Group Determinants for C_4^2*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A30, Theorem 1 (definition of `P`).

articles.title: Integer group determinants of $C_4 \times C_4$
articles.statement:
Let $C_4$ be the cyclic group of order
$4$, let $S(C_4^2)$ be the set of integer group determinants of $C_4 \times C_4$, let $P$ be the
set of positive primes $p \equiv -3 \pmod 8$, and let $A$ be the set of products
$(8k-3)(8l-3)(8m-3)(8n-3)$ with $k, l, m, n \in \mathbb{Z}$, $8l-3, 8m-3, 8n-3 \in P$ and
$k + l \not\equiv m + n \pmod 2$. Then $A$ is a proper subset of
$\{16m - 7 \mid m \in \mathbb{Z}\}$, and

$$S(C_4^2) = \{16m + 1 \mid m \in \mathbb{Z}\} \cup
\{2^{15} p (2m + 1) \mid p \in P, m \in \mathbb{Z}\} \cup
\{2^{16} m \mid m \in \mathbb{Z}\} \cup A.$$

## Sources

- Yuka Yamaguchi and Naoya Yamaguchi, *Integer Group Determinants for C_4^2*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A30, Theorem 1.

articles.title: Integer group determinants
articles.statement:
For a finite group $G$, written additively and not
necessarily commutative, $S(G)$ is the set of integers $\det(x_{g - h})_{g, h \in G}$, where $x$
ranges over all functions $G \to \mathbb{Z}$.

## Sources

- Yuka Yamaguchi and Naoya Yamaguchi, *Integer Group Determinants for C_4^2*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A30, Section 1 (definition of `S(G)`).

articles.title: The exceptional set $A$ contains $1625$
articles.statement:
Let $P$ be the set of positive primes
$p \equiv -3 \pmod 8$ and $A$ the set of products $(8k-3)(8l-3)(8m-3)(8n-3)$ with
$k, l, m, n \in \mathbb{Z}$, $8l-3, 8m-3, 8n-3 \in P$ and $k + l \not\equiv m + n \pmod 2$.
Then $1625 \in A$: take $k = l = m = 1$ and $n = 2$, so that $1625 = 5 \cdot 5 \cdot 5 \cdot 13$.

## Sources

- Yuka Yamaguchi and Naoya Yamaguchi, *Integer Group Determinants for C_4^2*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A30, Theorem 1 (definition of `A`).

articles.title: Odd integer group determinants of $C_4 \times C_4$
articles.statement:
Let $C_4$ be the cyclic group of
order $4$, $S(C_4^2)$ the set of integer group determinants of $C_4 \times C_4$ and $P$ the set
of positive primes $p \equiv -3 \pmod 8$, and let $A$ be the set of products
$(8k-3)(8l-3)(8m-3)(8n-3)$ with $k, l, m, n \in \mathbb{Z}$, $8l-3, 8m-3, 8n-3 \in P$ and
$k + l \not\equiv m + n \pmod 2$. Every odd $z \in S(C_4^2)$ is of the form $16m + 1$ for some
integer $m$ or lies in $A$.

## Sources

- Yuka Yamaguchi and Naoya Yamaguchi, *Integer Group Determinants for C_4^2*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A30, Lemma 8.

articles.title: $1$ is an integer group determinant
articles.statement:
For every finite group $G$, written additively,
$1 \in S(G)$, where $S(G)$ is the set of integer group determinants of $G$: the indicator
function of the identity element gives the identity matrix.

## Sources

- Yuka Yamaguchi and Naoya Yamaguchi, *Integer Group Determinants for C_4^2*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A30, Section 1 (definition of `S(G)`).

articles.title: Primes congruent to $-3$ modulo $8$
articles.statement:
$P$ is the set of positive prime integers $p$
with $p \equiv -3 \pmod 8$, that is, $p \equiv 5 \pmod 8$.

## Sources

- Yuka Yamaguchi and Naoya Yamaguchi, *Integer Group Determinants for C_4^2*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A30, Theorem 1 (definition of `P`).

articles.title: Sums of two squares congruent to −3 modulo 8
articles.statement:
Let $a$ and $b$ be integers with
$a^2 + b^2 \equiv -3 \pmod 8$. Then there are integers $k$ and $l$ such that $8l - 3$ lies in
the set $P$ of positive primes congruent to $5$ modulo $8$, and $a^2 + b^2 = (8k + 1)(8l - 3)$.

## Sources

- Yuka Yamaguchi and Naoya Yamaguchi, *Integer Group Determinants for C_4^2*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A30, Corollary 3.

articles.title: Number of irreducible characters
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group. The number of irreducible
complex characters of $G$, that is, of functions $G \to \mathbb{C}$ that are the character of
some simple finite-dimensional complex representation of $G$, equals the number of conjugacy
classes of $G$.

Proof: The irreducible characters are linearly independent and span the class functions, so
they form a basis of that space; compare its cardinality with the known dimension of that
space (P. Etingof et al., *Introduction to representation theory*, arXiv:0901.0827,
Theorem 3.5 and Corollary 3.6).

## Sources

- J.-P. Serre, Linear Representations of Finite Groups, GTM 42, §2.7 (number of irreducible characters).

articles.title: Characters are class functions
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a group and $k$ a field. For every
finite-dimensional representation $V$ of $G$ over $k$, the character of $V$, the function
sending $g \in G$ to the trace of the linear map by which $g$ acts on $V$, is a class
function on $G$.

## Sources

- J.-P. Serre, Linear Representations of Finite Groups, GTM 42, §2.1 (the character is constant on conjugacy classes).

articles.title: Evaluating a class function on conjugacy classes
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a group and $k$ a
field. For every class function $f : G \to k$ and every $x \in G$, the function on
conjugacy classes that corresponds to $f$ under the linear isomorphism between class
functions and functions on conjugacy classes takes the value $f(x)$ at the conjugacy
class of $x$.

articles.title: Lifting a function on conjugacy classes
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a group and $k$ a field. For
every function $q$ from the set of conjugacy classes of $G$ to $k$ and every $x \in G$,
the class function that corresponds to $q$ under the inverse of the linear isomorphism
between class functions and functions on conjugacy classes takes at $x$ the value of $q$
at the conjugacy class of $x$.

articles.title: Class functions as functions on conjugacy classes
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a group and $k$ a
field, and write $[x]$ for the conjugacy class of $x \in G$. This is the $k$-linear
isomorphism from the space of class functions $G \to k$ to the vector space of all
functions from the set of conjugacy classes of $G$ to $k$ that sends a class function $f$
to the function $[x] \mapsto f(x)$; its inverse sends a function $q$ on conjugacy classes
to the class function $x \mapsto q([x])$.

articles.title: The space of class functions
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a group and $k$ a field. The space of
class functions $G \to k$ is the $k$-linear subspace of the vector space of all functions
$G \to k$, under pointwise addition and scalar multiplication, consisting of the class
functions.

articles.title: Class functions agree on conjugate elements
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a group and let
$f : G \to k$ be a class function with values in a set $k$. If $x, y \in G$ are conjugate,
then $f(x) = f(y)$.

articles.title: A class function orthogonal to all irreducible characters vanishes
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite
group and let $f : G \to \mathbb{C}$ satisfy $f(hgh^{-1}) = f(g)$ for all $g, h \in G$. Suppose
that for every simple finite-dimensional complex representation $W$ of $G$, with character
$\chi_W$,

$$\frac{1}{|G|} \sum_{g \in G} f(g)\, \chi_W(g^{-1}) = 0.$$

Then $f = 0$.

articles.title: Dimension of the space of class functions
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group and $k$ a field.
The space of class functions $G \to k$ is a $k$-vector space whose dimension equals the
number of conjugacy classes of $G$.

Proof: The linear isomorphism between class functions and functions on conjugacy classes
reduces this to the space of all functions from the finite set of conjugacy classes of
$G$ to $k$, whose dimension is the number of conjugacy classes.

## Sources

- J.-P. Serre, Linear Representations of Finite Groups, GTM 42, §2.7, Theorem 6 (dimension count for class functions).

articles.title: Class functions factor through conjugacy classes
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a group and $k$ a set,
and write $[x]$ for the conjugacy class of $x \in G$. A function $f : G \to k$ is a class
function if and only if there is a function $q$ from the set of conjugacy classes of $G$
to $k$ such that $f(x) = q([x])$ for all $x \in G$.

Proof: A class function is constant on each conjugacy class, so it descends to a function
on conjugacy classes. Conversely, if $f(x) = q([x])$ for all $x \in G$, then for all
$g, h \in G$ we have $f(h g h^{-1}) = q([h g h^{-1}]) = q([g]) = f(g)$, because
$h g h^{-1}$ and $g$ are conjugate.

## Sources

- J.-P. Serre, Linear Representations of Finite Groups, GTM 42, §2 (class functions as functions on conjugacy classes).

articles.title: Class functions on a group
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a group and $k$ a set. A function
$f : G \to k$ is a class function when it is constant on conjugacy classes, that is,
$f(h g h^{-1}) = f(g)$ for all $g, h \in G$.

articles.title: Characters of nonisomorphic simple representations are linearly independent
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be
a finite group and let $(V_i)_{i \in I}$ be a family of simple finite-dimensional complex
representations of $G$ such that $V_i \cong V_j$ implies $i = j$. Then the characters of the
$V_i$ are linearly independent over $\mathbb{C}$.

articles.title: Irreducible characters are linearly independent
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group. The irreducible
complex characters of $G$, that is, the functions $G \to \mathbb{C}$ that are the character of
some simple finite-dimensional complex representation of $G$, are linearly independent over
$\mathbb{C}$ in the space of functions $G \to \mathbb{C}$.

Proof: Apply row orthogonality (C. Teleman, *Representation Theory*, Cambridge lecture
notes, 2005, Theorem 8.10) as coordinate functionals to a vanishing finite linear
combination of pairwise distinct irreducible characters.

## Sources

- J.-P. Serre, Linear Representations of Finite Groups, GTM 42, §2.5 (independence of irreducible characters).

articles.title: Irreducible characters span the class functions
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group and let
$f : G \to \mathbb{C}$ satisfy $f(hgh^{-1}) = f(g)$ for all $g, h \in G$. Then $f$ is a
$\mathbb{C}$-linear combination of irreducible complex characters of $G$, that is, of functions
$G \to \mathbb{C}$ that are the character of some simple finite-dimensional complex representation
of $G$.

Proof: Subtract the orthogonal projection onto the irreducible characters. The
remainder vanishes by Schur's lemma, Maschke's theorem, and the regular
representation on a small model of the complex group algebra, as in the proof of
Teleman's Theorem 9.3 (completeness of characters).

## Sources

- J.-P. Serre, Linear Representations of Finite Groups, GTM 42, §2.7, Theorem 6 (irreducible characters span the class functions).

articles.title: Irreducible representations are simple objects
articles.statement:
Let $k$ be a field, $G$ a group and
$\rho$ an irreducible representation of $G$ on a finite-dimensional $k$-vector space $V$. Then
$\rho$, viewed as an object of the category of finite-dimensional representations of $G$ over
$k$, is a simple object.

articles.title: Four isotypic components in a tensor square for a simple group of order 10200960
articles.statement:
There
exist a finite simple group $G$ of order $10200960$ and an irreducible complex representation
$\rho$ of $G$ on a vector space $V$ of dimension $22$ such that the tensor square $V \otimes V$,
regarded as a module over the group algebra $\mathbb{C}[G]$ through the diagonal action
$g \mapsto \rho(g) \otimes \rho(g)$, has exactly $4$ isotypic components.

## Sources

- É. Mathieu, Sur les fonctions cinq fois transitives de 24 quantités, J. Math. Pures Appl. (1873); ATLAS of Finite Groups, M₂₃ character table. Problem `m23_irrep_tensor_square_decomp` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: McKay conjecture (Cabanes–Späth theorem)
articles.statement:
For every finite group $G$, every prime $p$ and
every Sylow $p$-subgroup $P$ of $G$, with normalizer $N_G(P)$ in $G$, the sets
$\mathrm{Irr}_{p'}(G)$ and $\mathrm{Irr}_{p'}(N_G(P))$ of irreducible complex characters of
degree not divisible by $p$ have the same cardinality.

## Sources

- M. Cabanes and B. Späth, *The McKay conjecture*, Ann. of Math. 203(3) (2026), arXiv:2410.20392, doi:10.4007/annals.2026.203.3.5.

articles.title: Irreducible characters of $p'$-degree
articles.statement:
For a group $G$ and a natural number $p$,
$\mathrm{Irr}_{p'}(G)$ is the set of functions $G \to \mathbb{C}$ that are characters of simple
finite-dimensional complex representations of $G$ whose dimension is not divisible by $p$.

Two simple representations have equal characters exactly when they are isomorphic, so these
characters correspond bijectively to the isomorphism classes of such representations, which is
what the McKay conjecture counts.

articles.title: No insoluble group has independent permutation characters (Kourovka 11.9)
articles.statement:
There is no
finite non-soluble group $G$ such that, choosing a representative $H$ of each conjugacy class of
subgroups of $G$, the rational-valued permutation characters $1_H^G$ of $G$ on the left cosets of
these subgroups $H$ are linearly independent over $\mathbb{Q}$.

Brescia, Ingrosso and Trombetti prove that these permutation characters are linearly independent
if and only if $G$ is cyclic; the Kourovka Notebook (21st issue) marks 11.9 solved, "No, there
are no such groups".

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Problem 11.9 (Ya. G. Berkovich); resolution: M. Brescia, E. Ingrosso and M. Trombetti, On the independence of permutation characters, arXiv:2608.16957 (2026), main theorem: the characters `π_H`, `H` over representatives of the conjugacy classes of subgroups, are linearly independent iff `G` is cyclic; the Kourovka Notebook (21st issue) marks 11.9 solved, https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.16957.

articles.title: Finite insoluble groups with independent permutation characters (Kourovka 11.9)
articles.statement:
The assertion that there is a finite non-soluble group $G$ such that, choosing a representative
$H$ of each conjugacy class of subgroups of $G$, the rational-valued permutation characters
$1_H^G$ of $G$ on the left cosets of these subgroups $H$ are linearly independent over
$\mathbb{Q}$.

articles.title: Characters of a group
articles.statement:
A function $\varphi : G \to \mathbb{C}$ on a group $G$ is a
character of $G$ when there are a finite-dimensional complex vector space $V$ and a
representation $\rho$ of $G$ on $V$ whose character $g \mapsto \operatorname{tr} \rho(g)$ equals
$\varphi$.

articles.title: Rational permutation character on the cosets of a subgroup
articles.statement:
For a subgroup $H$ of a group
$G$, the permutation character $1_H^G : G \to \mathbb{Q}$ sends $g \in G$ to the number of left
cosets $xH$ of $H$ with $gxH = xH$, and to $0$ when $g$ fixes infinitely many cosets.

articles.title: Complex permutation character on the cosets of a subgroup
articles.statement:
For a subgroup $H$ of a group
$G$, the permutation character $1_H^G : G \to \mathbb{C}$ sends $g \in G$ to the number of left
cosets $xH$ of $H$ with $gxH = xH$, and to $0$ when $g$ fixes infinitely many cosets. For finite
$G$ and the trivial subgroup $H = 1$ this is the regular character $1^G$.

articles.title: Strunkov's two-generation criterion fails (Kourovka 12.79)
articles.statement:
It is not true that for every
finite group $G$ and all $a, b \in G$ such that Strunkov's class function
$1^G - 1_{\langle a \rangle}^G - 1_{\langle b \rangle}^G - 1_{\langle ab \rangle}^G + 2$ is a
character of $G$, the elements $a$ and $b$ generate $G$. Here $1_H^G$ is the permutation character
of $G$ on the cosets of a subgroup $H$, $1^G = 1_1^G$, $\langle x \rangle$ is the cyclic subgroup
generated by $x$, and $2$ is the constant function with value $2$.

Counterexample (S. V. Skresanov, 2019): $G = A_4$ and $a = b = (1\,2\,3)$. The function takes the
values $2, 2, -1, -1$ on the classes of $1$, $(1\,2)(3\,4)$, $(1\,2\,3)$, $(1\,3\,2)$, so it is
the sum of the two nontrivial linear characters of $A_4$, while $\langle a, b \rangle$ has
order $3$.

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Archive of Solved Problems, Problem 12.79 (S. P. Strunkov); resolution: S. V. Skresanov, Algebra Logic 58 (2019), no. 3, 249-253, Kourovka Archive, Problem 12.79: No, not always; counterexample G = A_4, a = b = (123).

articles.title: Strunkov's two-generation criterion (Kourovka 12.79)
articles.statement:
The assertion that for every finite
group $G$ and all $a, b \in G$, if Strunkov's class function
$1^G - 1_{\langle a \rangle}^G - 1_{\langle b \rangle}^G - 1_{\langle ab \rangle}^G + 2$ is a
character of $G$, then $a$ and $b$ generate $G$. Here $1_H^G$ is the permutation character of $G$
on the cosets of a subgroup $H$, $1^G = 1_1^G$, $\langle x \rangle$ is the cyclic subgroup
generated by $x$, and $2$ is the constant function with value $2$.

articles.title: Strunkov's class function
articles.statement:
For elements $a, b$ of a group $G$, Strunkov's function
$\varphi : G \to \mathbb{C}$ is

$$\varphi = 1^G - 1_{\langle a \rangle}^G - 1_{\langle b \rangle}^G - 1_{\langle ab \rangle}^G + 2$$

where $1_H^G$ is the complex permutation character of $G$ on the cosets of a subgroup $H$,
$1^G = 1_1^G$ is the one for the trivial subgroup, $\langle x \rangle$ is the cyclic subgroup
generated by $x$, and $2$ is the constant function with value $2$.

articles.title: Rational group (conjugacy form, Kourovka 15.25)
articles.statement:
A group $G$ is rational when every element
$g \in G$ is conjugate in $G$ to $g^k$ for every natural number $k$ coprime to the order of $g$ (an
element of infinite order counts as having order $0$, so for it only $k = 1$ qualifies).

For finite groups this is equivalent to every irreducible complex character taking only rational
values.

articles.title: Rational groups, conjugacy form
articles.statement:
A group $G$ is rational if every element $g \in G$ is
conjugate to $g^k$ for every natural number $k$ coprime to the order of $g$, where an element of
infinite order has order $0$, so that only $k = 1$ is coprime to it. For finite groups this is the
classical equivalent form of the condition that all ordinary characters of $G$ are
rational-valued.

articles.title: Sylow 2-subgroups of rational groups need not be rational (Kourovka 16.36)
articles.statement:
There is a
finite rational group with a Sylow $2$-subgroup that is not rational as a group in its own right.
Here a group is rational if every element $g$ is conjugate to $g^k$ for every natural number $k$
coprime to the order of $g$.

The Kourovka Archive answers 16.36 "No, not always", citing Isaacs and Navarro (2012).

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Archive of Solved Problems, Problem 16.36 (M. R. Darafsheh); resolution: I. M. Isaacs and G. Navarro, Math. Z. 272 (2012), 937-945, Kourovka Archive, Problem 16.36 (No, not always).

articles.title: Darafsheh's question on Sylow 2-subgroups of rational groups (Kourovka 16.36)
articles.statement:
The
conjecture that for every finite rational group $G$, every Sylow $2$-subgroup of $G$, viewed as a
group in its own right, is rational. Here a group is rational if every element $g$ is conjugate
to $g^k$ for every natural number $k$ coprime to the order of $g$.

articles.title: Sylow 2-subgroups of the symmetric groups of degree $2^n$ are rational (Kourovka 15.25)
articles.statement:
For
every natural number $n$, every Sylow $2$-subgroup $P$ of the symmetric group $S_{2^n}$ on $2^n$
points is rational as a group in its own right: every $g \in P$ is conjugate within $P$ to $g^k$ for
every natural number $k$ coprime to the order of $g$.

A Sylow $2$-subgroup $T_n$ of $S_{2^n}$ is the wreath product of $T_{n-1}$ with a group of order
$2$, which is rational when $T_{n-1}$ is (Kletzing, Corollary 70), so induction on $n$ applies.

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Archive of Solved Problems, Problem 15.25 (Ya. G. Berkovich); resolution: A. Mann, letter of 1 October 2002, as recorded in the Kourovka Archive, Problem 15.25, using D. Kletzing, Structure and representations of Q-groups, Lecture Notes in Math. 1084, Springer, Berlin, 1984, Corollary 70, Kourovka Archive, Problem 15.25 (answer: Yes, they are; T_n = T_(n-1) wr C_2 and wreath products with C_2 preserve rationality), https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v49.

articles.title: Kourovka Problem 15.25 (statement)
articles.statement:
The statement that for every natural number $n$, every
Sylow $2$-subgroup $P$ of the symmetric group $S_{2^n}$ on $2^n$ points is rational as a group in
its own right: every $g \in P$ is conjugate within $P$ to $g^k$ for every natural number $k$ coprime
to the order of $g$.

articles.title: Simply reducible group
articles.statement:
A group $G$ is simply reducible when the character of every
irreducible finite-dimensional complex representation of $G$ is real-valued, and for all
irreducible finite-dimensional complex representations $U$, $V$ and $W$ of $G$, the space
$\mathrm{Hom}_G(U, V \otimes W)$ of $G$-equivariant linear maps from $U$ to the tensor product
$V \otimes W$ has complex dimension at most $1$.

For finite $G$, by Maschke's and Schur's theorems this dimension is the multiplicity of $U$ in
$V \otimes W$, so the second condition says that $V \otimes W$ has no repeated irreducible
constituents.

articles.title: Finite simply reducible groups are soluble
articles.statement:
Every finite simply reducible group is soluble;
