the matrices in the generating set of the Suzuki group (all of which are invertible).

articles.title: Brauer–Fowler theorem
articles.statement:
There is a function $f \colon \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ such that
for every finite nonabelian simple group $G$ and every element $t \in G$ of order $2$, with
centralizer $C_G(t)$ in $G$, the order of $G$ satisfies $|G| \le f(|C_G(t)|)$.

## Sources

- R. Brauer and K. A. Fowler, On groups of even order, Ann. of Math. (2) 62 (1955), 565-583. https://doi.org/10.2307/1970080. Problem `brauer_fowler` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Brauer–Suzuki theorem
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group, let $O(G)$, the odd core of $G$, be the
subgroup generated by all normal subgroups of $G$ of odd order, let $n \ge 3$, and let $P$ be a
Sylow $2$-subgroup of $G$ isomorphic to the generalized quaternion group $Q_{2^n}$ of order $2^n$.
If $t \in P$ has order $2$, then the image of $t$ in $G / O(G)$ lies in the center of $G / O(G)$.

## Sources

- R. Brauer and M. Suzuki, On finite groups of even order whose 2-Sylow group is a quaternion group, Proc. Nat. Acad. Sci. U.S.A. 45 (1959), 1757-1759. https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.45.12.1757. Problem `brauer_suzuki` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Odd core of a group
articles.statement:
The odd core $O(G)$ of a group $G$ is the supremum, in the lattice of
subgroups of $G$, of all normal subgroups of $G$ whose order is finite and odd.

For a finite group this is the largest normal subgroup of odd order, classically denoted $O(G)$
(in older notation $O_{2'}(G)$): the join of two normal subgroups of odd order is again a normal
subgroup of odd order, so the supremum is itself one. For an infinite group the definition still
makes sense as a subgroup, though it need not be of odd order.

articles.title: Glauberman's $Z^*$-theorem
articles.statement:
**Glauberman's $Z^*$-theorem.** Let $G$ be a finite group and let $t \in G$ be an involution
($t \neq 1$ and $t^2 = 1$) such that every conjugate $g t g^{-1}$ of $t$ that commutes with $t$
equals $t$. Then there is a normal subgroup $N$ of $G$ of odd order such that
$g t g^{-1} t^{-1} \in N$ for every $g \in G$.

## Sources

- G. Glauberman, Central elements in core-free groups, J. Algebra 4 (1966). Problem `glauberman_zStar` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Odd core from normal subgroups of odd-order elements
articles.statement:
For a group $G$, $O(G)$ is the join,
in the lattice of subgroups of $G$, of all normal subgroups $N$ of $G$ such that every element of
$N$ has finite odd order. In a periodic group this join is again a normal subgroup consisting of
elements of odd order, so it is the largest such subgroup.

articles.title: A periodic counterexample to Borovik's question (Kourovka 11.13)
articles.statement:
For a group $G$, let $O(G)$
be the join of all normal subgroups of $G$ all of whose elements have odd order. There exist a
periodic group $G$ and an involution $i \in G$ such that $g^{-1} i g i$ has odd order for every
$g \in G$, but the image of $i$ in $G / O(G)$ is not central: $g i g^{-1} i^{-1} \notin O(G)$ for
some $g \in G$. This answers Kourovka Problem 11.13 in the negative.

For finite groups the answer is yes, by Glauberman's $Z^*$-theorem.

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Archive of Solved Problems, Problem 11.13 (A. V. Borovik); resolution: E. B. Durakov and A. I. Sozutov, Algebra and Logic 52, no. 5 (2013), 422-425, Kourovka Archive, Problem 11.13: "No, not always", https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v49.

articles.title: Borovik's question on involutions with odd-order products (Kourovka 11.13)
articles.statement:
For a group
$G$, let $O(G)$ be the join of all normal subgroups of $G$ all of whose elements have odd order.
This is the statement that for every periodic group $G$ and every involution $i \in G$ such that
$g^{-1} i g i$ has odd order for every $g \in G$, the image of $i$ in $G / O(G)$ is central, that
is, $g i g^{-1} i^{-1} \in O(G)$ for every $g \in G$.

articles.title: Gorenstein–Walter theorem
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite nonabelian simple group, and let $P$ be a
Sylow $2$-subgroup of $G$ that is isomorphic to the dihedral group $D_n$ for some natural number
$n$ (of order $2n$ when $n \ge 1$; $D_0$ is the infinite dihedral group). Then $G$ is isomorphic
to the alternating group $A_7$, or to the projective special linear group
$\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{F}_q)$ for some power $q = p^k$ of an odd prime $p$ with $q \ge 5$.

## Sources

- D. Gorenstein and J. H. Walter, The characterization of finite groups with dihedral Sylow 2-subgroups, J. Algebra 2 (1965), 85-151, 218-270, 354-393. https://doi.org/10.1016/0021-8693(65)90027-X. Problem `gorenstein_walter` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Involutions commuting with an element
articles.statement:
For an element $t$ of a group $G$, this is the
set of involutions of $G$ that commute with $t$: the elements $s \in G$ of order $2$ with
$st = ts$.

articles.title: Finitely many finite simple groups with an involution commuting with few involutions
articles.statement:
For
every natural number $n$ there is a bound $N$ such that every finite simple group $G$ containing
an involution $t$ that commutes with at most $n$ involutions of $G$ (counting $t$ itself) has
order at most $N$.

This answers Kourovka Problem 11.96(a) in the affirmative; the Kourovka Notebook (21st issue)
marks it solved, "Yes", modulo the classification of finite simple groups.

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Problem 11.96 (S. P. Strunkov); resolution: S. V. Skresanov, J. Group Theory 27, no. 6 (2024), 1197-1202, the Kourovka Notebook (21st issue) marks 11.96 solved: (a) yes (mod CFSG), and a locally finite group with such an involution is finite of `n`-bounded order; (b) no, `PSL_2(ℝ)` is an infinite simple group with an involution and no Klein four-subgroup, https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v49.

articles.title: Strunkov's finiteness question for simple groups (Kourovka 11.96(a))
articles.statement:
This is the statement
that for every natural number $n$ there is a bound $N$ such that every finite simple group $G$
containing an involution $t$ that commutes with at most $n$ involutions of $G$ (counting $t$
itself) has order at most $N$. Bounding the order expresses "only finitely many such groups up to
isomorphism".

articles.title: Locally finite fields (Kourovka 18.59)
articles.statement:
A field $P$ is locally finite when, for every
finite subset $s$ of $P$, the subfield of $P$ generated by $s$ is finite.

articles.title: An infinite simple group with an involution commuting with few involutions
articles.statement:
There exist a
natural number $n$ and an infinite simple group $G$ containing an involution $t$ that commutes
with at most $n$ involutions of $G$ (counting $t$ itself). This answers Kourovka Problem 11.96(b)
in the negative.

For example, $\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{R})$ is an infinite simple group that contains an involution
but no Klein four-subgroup, so each of its involutions commutes with no involution other than
itself ($n = 1$); the Kourovka Notebook (21st issue) marks 11.96(b) solved, "No", citing Skresanov.

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Problem 11.96 (S. P. Strunkov); resolution: S. V. Skresanov, J. Group Theory 27, no. 6 (2024), 1197-1202, the Kourovka Notebook (21st issue) marks 11.96 solved: (a) yes (mod CFSG), and a locally finite group with such an involution is finite of `n`-bounded order; (b) no, `PSL_2(ℝ)` is an infinite simple group with an involution and no Klein four-subgroup, https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v49.

articles.title: Strunkov's question on infinite simple groups (Kourovka 11.96(b))
articles.statement:
This is the statement
that for every natural number $n$, no infinite simple group $G$ contains an involution $t$ that
commutes with at most $n$ involutions of $G$ (counting $t$ itself).

articles.title: Negative answer to Kourovka Problem 18.59
articles.statement:
There is no periodic group $G$ that contains an
involution, in which all involutions are conjugate, and for which there is an infinite locally
finite field $P$ of characteristic $2$ such that the centralizer of every involution $i$ of $G$ is
isomorphic to $\langle i \rangle \times \mathrm{PSL}_2(P)$. Here $\langle i \rangle$ is the cyclic
subgroup generated by $i$ and $\mathrm{PSL}_2(P)$ is the quotient of $\mathrm{SL}_2(P)$ by its
centre.

Muliarchyk's Theorem 3 proves more: no group, periodic or not, has a single nonempty conjugacy
class of involutions whose centralizers are isomorphic to $C_2 \times \mathrm{PSL}_2(P)$ for an
infinite locally finite field $P$ of characteristic $2$.

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Problem 18.59 (D. V. Lytkina); resolution: K. Muliarchyk, Involution centralizers and a linear obstruction: Kourovka Problems 18.59 and 18.60, preprint, 2026, Theorem 3: no group has a single nonempty conjugacy class of involutions with involution centralizers isomorphic to C_2 × PSL_2(P), P an infinite locally finite field of characteristic two (periodicity not needed); the Kourovka Notebook (21st issue) marks 18.59 solved, https://kourovkanotebookorg.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/kourovka_18_59-18_60_solution.pdf.

articles.title: Kourovka Problem 18.59 on involution centralizers
articles.statement:
The proposition (Kourovka 18.59, D. V.
Lytkina) that there are a periodic group $G$ which contains an involution and in which all
involutions are conjugate, and an infinite locally finite field $P$ of characteristic $2$, such
that the centralizer of every involution $i$ of $G$ is isomorphic to
$\langle i \rangle \times \mathrm{PSL}_2(P)$. Here $\langle i \rangle$ is the cyclic subgroup
generated by $i$ and $\mathrm{PSL}_2(P) = L_2(P)$ is the quotient of $\mathrm{SL}_2(P)$ by its
centre.

The field $P$ is chosen once for all involutions; since all involutions are conjugate, this is
equivalent to allowing a field for each involution.

articles.title: The standard 23-cycle in $M_{23}$
articles.statement:
The permutation of $\{0, 1, \dots, 22\}$ that sends
$i$ to $i + 1$ for $i < 22$ and sends $22$ to $0$, that is, the 23-cycle
$(0\ 1\ 2\ \cdots\ 22)$. It is the first of the two standard generators of the Mathieu group
$M_{23}$.

articles.title: The standard product of four 5-cycles in $M_{23}$
articles.statement:
The permutation of the points
$\{0, 1, \dots, 22\}$ given by the product of the four disjoint 5-cycles
$(2\ 16\ 9\ 6\ 8)(3\ 12\ 13\ 18\ 4)(7\ 17\ 10\ 11\ 22)(14\ 19\ 21\ 20\ 15)$, where a cycle
$(a_1\ a_2\ \cdots\ a_5)$ sends $a_k$ to $a_{k+1}$ for $k < 5$ and sends $a_5$ to $a_1$. It
fixes the three remaining points $0$, $1$ and $5$, and it is the second of the two standard
generators of the Mathieu group $M_{23}$.

articles.title: Subgroups containing $M_{23}$
articles.statement:
A subgroup $H$ of the symmetric group on
$\{0, 1, \dots, 22\}$ contains the Mathieu group $M_{23}$ if and only if $H$ contains both the
standard 23-cycle and the standard product of four 5-cycles that generate $M_{23}$.

articles.title: The Mathieu group $M_{23}$
articles.statement:
The subgroup of the symmetric group on $\{0, 1, \dots, 22\}$
generated by the standard 23-cycle $(0\ 1\ 2\ \cdots\ 22)$ and the standard product of four
disjoint 5-cycles $(2\ 16\ 9\ 6\ 8)(3\ 12\ 13\ 18\ 4)(7\ 17\ 10\ 11\ 22)(14\ 19\ 21\ 20\ 15)$.

articles.title: Negative answer to Farb's Question 7.3
articles.statement:
It is not the case that for every natural number
$n > 3$ the automorphism group $\mathrm{Aut}(F_n)$ of the free group on $n$ generators is
automatic.

Bridson and Vogtmann, with Handel and Mosher, proved more: $\mathrm{Aut}(F_n)$ has exponential
Dehn function for every $n \ge 3$, while automatic groups have at most quadratic Dehn functions
(Epstein et al.), so $\mathrm{Aut}(F_n)$ is automatic for no $n \ge 3$.

## Sources

- M. R. Bridson, K. Vogtmann, The Dehn functions of Out(F_n) and Aut(F_n), Annales de l'Institut Fourier 62(5) (2012) 1811-1817, arXiv:1011.1506, https://arxiv.org/abs/1011.1506.

articles.title: Automaticity of automorphism groups of free groups (Farb's Question 7.3)
articles.statement:
The statement
that for every natural number $n > 3$ the automorphism group $\mathrm{Aut}(F_n)$ of the free group
$F_n$ on $n$ generators is an automatic group.

## Sources

- Question 7.3 [AMR-109-0302], Farb - Problems on Mapping Class Groups and Related Topics, PDF p. 339, https://www.math.uchicago.edu/~farb/papers/mcgbook.pdf.

articles.title: Automatic group
articles.statement:
A group $G$ is automatic if there are a finite alphabet $A$, an
involution $\iota$ of $A$, a map $\mathrm{ev} \colon A \to G$ with
$\mathrm{ev}(\iota(a)) = \mathrm{ev}(a)^{-1}$ for all $a \in A$, a language $L$ of words over $A$
that is exactly the set of words accepted by some deterministic finite automaton, and a natural
number $k$ with the following properties. Write $\overline{w} \in G$ for the product of the
images under $\mathrm{ev}$ of the letters of a word $w$, and $w(t)$ for the prefix of $w$ of
length $t$ (all of $w$ if $t$ exceeds its length). Every element of $G$ equals $\overline{w}$ for
some $w \in L$. For all $u, v \in L$ such that $\overline{u} = \overline{v}$, or
$\overline{u}\,\mathrm{ev}(a) = \overline{v}$ for some letter $a$, and for every $t \in \mathbb{N}$,
the element $\overline{u(t)}^{-1}\,\overline{v(t)}$ equals $\overline{w}$ for some word $w$ of
length at most $k$.

This is the fellow-traveller characterization of automatic groups (Epstein et al., Word
Processing in Groups, Theorem 2.3.5).

## Sources

- Question 7.3 [AMR-109-0302], Farb - Problems on Mapping Class Groups and Related Topics, PDF p. 339, https://www.math.uchicago.edu/~farb/papers/mcgbook.pdf.

articles.title: Groups whose endomorphisms with non-cyclic images are determined by two elements
articles.statement:
A group
$F$ has this property when there exist elements $g, h \in F$ such that any two endomorphisms
$\varphi, \psi$ of $F$ whose images are not cyclic subgroups and which satisfy
$\varphi(g) = \psi(g)$ and $\varphi(h) = \psi(h)$ are equal.

articles.title: Endomorphisms of free groups with non-cyclic images are determined by two elements
articles.statement:
For every
natural number $n$, the free group $F_n$ of rank $n$ contains two elements $g$ and $h$ such that
any two endomorphisms $\varphi, \psi$ of $F_n$ whose images are not cyclic subgroups and which
satisfy $\varphi(g) = \psi(g)$ and $\varphi(h) = \psi(h)$ are equal.

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Archive of Solved Problems, Problem 13.66 (V. E. Shpil'rain); resolution: (a) D. Lee, J. Algebra 247 (2002), no. 2, 509-540; (b) E. I. Timoshenko, Math. Notes 62 (1998), no. 5-6, 767-770, Kourovka Archive, Problem 13.66 (answers: a) Yes, one can; b) No, not always).

articles.title: Shpil'rain's two-element problem for free groups (Kourovka 13.66(a))
articles.statement:
For every natural
number $n$, the free group $F_n$ of rank $n$ contains two elements $g$ and $h$ such that any two
endomorphisms of $F_n$ whose images are not cyclic subgroups and which agree at $g$ and at $h$
are equal; that is, $F_n$ has its endomorphisms with non-cyclic images determined by two
elements.

articles.title: Endomorphisms of free metabelian groups are not always determined by two elements
articles.statement:
For a
natural number $n$, let $M_n = F_n / F_n''$ be the free metabelian group of rank $n$, the quotient
of the free group $F_n$ of rank $n$ by its second derived subgroup. There is an $n$ such that for
all elements $g, h \in M_n$ there are endomorphisms $\varphi \ne \psi$ of $M_n$ whose images are
not cyclic subgroups and which satisfy $\varphi(g) = \psi(g)$ and $\varphi(h) = \psi(h)$.

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Archive of Solved Problems, Problem 13.66 (V. E. Shpil'rain); resolution: (a) D. Lee, J. Algebra 247 (2002), no. 2, 509-540; (b) E. I. Timoshenko, Math. Notes 62 (1998), no. 5-6, 767-770, Kourovka Archive, Problem 13.66 (answers: a) Yes, one can; b) No, not always).

articles.title: Shpil'rain's two-element problem for free metabelian groups (Kourovka 13.66(b))
articles.statement:
For every
natural number $n$, the free metabelian group $M_n = F_n / F_n''$ of rank $n$ (the quotient of the
free group $F_n$ of rank $n$ by its second derived subgroup) contains two elements $g$ and $h$
such that any two endomorphisms of $M_n$ whose images are not cyclic subgroups and which agree at
$g$ and at $h$ are equal.

articles.title: The free metabelian group $M_n$
articles.statement:
For a natural number $n$, the free metabelian group of
rank $n$ is the quotient $F_n / F_n''$ of the free group $F_n$ on $n$ generators by its second
derived subgroup $F_n'' = [F_n', F_n']$, where $F_n' = [F_n, F_n]$ is the derived subgroup of
$F_n$.

articles.title: Farb's question on Property FA for finite-index subgroups of $\operatorname{Aut}(F_n)$
articles.statement:
The proposition that for every natural number $n \ge 4$, every subgroup of finite index in the
automorphism group $\operatorname{Aut}(F_n)$ of the free group $F_n$ on $n$ generators has Serre's
Property FA.

## Sources

- Farb Question 2.8 [AMR-109-0276] (PDF p. 331).

articles.title: Finite-index subgroups of $\operatorname{Aut}(F_n)$ have Property FA for $n \ge 4$
articles.statement:
For every
natural number $n \ge 4$, every subgroup of finite index in the automorphism group
$\operatorname{Aut}(F_n)$ of the free group $F_n$ on $n$ generators has Serre's Property FA.

This answers Farb's Question 2.8 positively: $\operatorname{Aut}(F_n)$ has Kazhdan's property (T)
for $n \ge 4$ (Kaluba–Kielak–Nowak for $n \ge 6$, Kaluba–Nowak–Ozawa for $n = 5$, Nitsche for
$n = 4$), property (T) passes to finite-index subgroups, and it implies Serre's Property FA
(Watatani).

## Sources

- Marek Kaluba, Dawid Kielak and Piotr W. Nowak, On property (T) for Aut(F_n) and SL_n(Z), Ann. of Math. 193 (2021), arXiv:1812.03456, https://arxiv.org/abs/1812.03456; Martin Nitsche, Computer proofs for Property (T), and SDP duality, arXiv:2009.05134v3 (2022), https://arxiv.org/abs/2009.05134.

articles.title: Some $\mathrm{Aut}(F_n)$ with $n > 3$ has no finite-index subgroup of positive first Betti number
articles.statement:
**Some $\mathrm{Aut}(F_n)$ with $n > 3$ has no finite-index subgroup of positive first Betti
number.** It is not the case that for every natural number $n > 3$ the automorphism group
$\mathrm{Aut}(F_n)$ of the free group $F_n$ on $n$ generators has a finite-index subgroup $H$ whose
first Betti number, the $\mathbb{Z}$-rank of the abelianization of $H$, is positive.

The case $n = 5$ fails: Kaluba, Nowak and Ozawa proved that $\mathrm{Aut}(F_5)$ has Kazhdan's
property (T), which passes to finite-index subgroups and forces finite abelianization, so every
finite-index subgroup of $\mathrm{Aut}(F_5)$ has first Betti number $0$.

## Sources

- M. Kaluba, P. W. Nowak, N. Ozawa, Aut(F5) has property (T), Math. Ann. 375 (2019), no. 3-4, 1169-1191, https://arxiv.org/abs/1712.07167.

articles.title: Farb's positive first Betti number question for $\mathrm{Aut}(F_n)$
articles.statement:
The proposition that
for every natural number $n > 3$, the automorphism group $\mathrm{Aut}(F_n)$ of the free group
$F_n$ on $n$ generators has a finite-index subgroup $H$ whose first Betti number, the
$\mathbb{Z}$-rank of the abelianization of $H$, is positive.

## Sources

- Farb Question 2.5 [AMR-109-0273] (PDF p. 330).

articles.title: First Betti number of a group
articles.statement:
The first Betti number of a group $G$ is the rank, as a
cardinal, of its abelianization $G^{\mathrm{ab}}$ viewed as a $\mathbb{Z}$-module.

## Sources

- [AMR-109-0273] (Question 2.5, PDF p. 330).

articles.title: Serre's Property FA
articles.statement:
A group $G$ has Property FA when every action of $G$ on a tree
without edge inversion has a global fixed vertex: for every tree $T$ with vertex set $V$ and every
homomorphism $\alpha$ from $G$ to the group of permutations of $V$ such that each $\alpha(g)$
satisfies $\alpha(g)(u) \sim \alpha(g)(v) \iff u \sim v$ for all vertices $u, v$ (where $\sim$ is
adjacency in $T$), and such that no $\alpha(g)$ swaps the two ends of an edge, there is a vertex
$v$ with $\alpha(g)(v) = v$ for all $g \in G$.

## Sources

- [AMR-109-0276] (Question 2.8, PDF p. 331).

articles.title: Norm of an automorphism of a free group
articles.statement:
Let $F_n$ be the free group on the basis
$x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$, and for $w \in F_n$ let $|w|$ be the length of the reduced word
representing $w$. The norm of an automorphism $\alpha$ of $F_n$ is
$\|\alpha\| = \max(|\alpha(x_0)|, \dots, |\alpha(x_{n-1})|)$, taken to be $0$ when $n = 0$.

articles.title: Fixed points of free group automorphisms are decidable (Kourovka 10.25)
articles.statement:
For every natural
number $r$ there is a computable function $f$ which takes the images of the $r$ free generators of
the free group $F_r$, each encoded as a word in the generators and their inverses, and returns a
Boolean, such that whenever the endomorphism $\varphi$ of $F_r$ sending each generator to its image
is bijective, $f$ returns true exactly when $\varphi(w) = w$ for some $w \neq 1$ in $F_r$.

The Kourovka Archive answers Problem 10.25 "Yes, it does", citing Bogopolski and Maslakova (2016),
who give an algorithm computing a basis of the fixed subgroup of an automorphism of a free group of
finite rank; the automorphism has a non-trivial fixed point exactly when that basis is nonempty.

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Archive of Solved Problems, Problem 10.25 (G. S. Makanin); resolution: O. Bogopolski and O. Maslakova, Int. J. Algebra Comput. 26, no. 1 (2016), 29-67, algorithm computing a basis of the fixed subgroup of an automorphism of a free group of finite rank; Kourovka Archive, Problem 10.25 ("Yes, it does").

articles.title: Decidability of fixed points of free group automorphisms (Kourovka 10.25)
articles.statement:
The assertion
that for every natural number $r$ there is a computable function $f$ which takes the images of the
$r$ free generators of the free group $F_r$, each encoded as a word in the generators and their
inverses, and returns a Boolean, such that whenever the endomorphism $\varphi$ of $F_r$ sending each
generator to its image is bijective, $f$ returns true exactly when $\varphi(w) = w$ for some
$w \neq 1$ in $F_r$.

articles.title: Endomorphism of a free group given by generator images
articles.statement:
Let $F_r$ be the free group on
generators $e_0, \dots, e_{r-1}$. Given, for each $i < r$, a word $u_i$ in these generators and
their inverses, this is the endomorphism of $F_r$ sending each $e_i$ to the element of $F_r$
represented by $u_i$.

articles.title: Kourovka Problem 14.23 holds for each rank
articles.statement:
For every $n$ there is a computable function
$f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ such that for every automorphism $\alpha$ of the free group $F_n$
on $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$, the fixed subgroup $\mathrm{Fix}(\alpha)$ has a finite free basis all
of whose elements have reduced word length at most $f(\|\alpha\|)$, where $\|\alpha\|$ is the
maximum of the reduced word lengths of $\alpha(x_0), \dots, \alpha(x_{n-1})$.

This follows from the algorithm computing a basis of $\mathrm{Fix}(\alpha)$ (Kharlampovich,
Proposition 2); the Kourovka Notebook (21st issue) records this answer.

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Problem 14.23 (O. V. Bogopolski); resolution: O. Kharlampovich, Two observations on Problems 14.23 and 17.32 of the Kourovka Notebook, preprint (2026), Proposition 2 (each rank); O. Kharlampovich, A counterexample to the rank-uniform form of Kourovka Notebook Problem 14.23, preprint (2026), Theorem 1, the Kourovka Notebook (21st issue) marks 14.23 solved: true for each given rank, false if one function must work for all ranks, https://kourovkanotebookorg.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/kourovka_14_23_uniform_counterexample.pdf.

articles.title: Kourovka Problem 14.23, rank-dependent form
articles.statement:
For every $n$ there is a computable
function $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ such that for every automorphism $\alpha$ of the free
group $F_n$ on $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$, the fixed subgroup $\mathrm{Fix}(\alpha)$ has a finite
free basis all of whose elements have reduced word length at most $f(\|\alpha\|)$, where
$\|\alpha\|$ is the maximum of the reduced word lengths of $\alpha(x_0), \dots, \alpha(x_{n-1})$.

This is the form of Kourovka Notebook Problem 14.23 (O. V. Bogopolski) in which $f$ may depend
on the rank $n$.

articles.title: Kourovka Problem 14.23 fails uniformly in the rank
articles.statement:
There is no computable function
$f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ such that for every $n$ and every automorphism $\alpha$ of the
free group $F_n$ on $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$, the fixed subgroup $\mathrm{Fix}(\alpha)$ has a
finite free basis all of whose elements have reduced word length at most $f(\|\alpha\|)$, where
$\|\alpha\|$ is the maximum of the reduced word lengths of $\alpha(x_0), \dots, \alpha(x_{n-1})$.

Kharlampovich (Theorem 1) proves more: for every $r \ge 3$ there is an automorphism $\alpha_r$
of the free group of rank $2r - 1$ with $\|\alpha_r\| = 3$ such that every generating set of
$\mathrm{Fix}(\alpha_r)$ contains an element of length at least $r$, so no function at all,
computable or not, works for all ranks; the Kourovka Notebook (21st issue) records this answer.

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Problem 14.23 (O. V. Bogopolski); resolution: O. Kharlampovich, Two observations on Problems 14.23 and 17.32 of the Kourovka Notebook, preprint (2026), Proposition 2 (each rank); O. Kharlampovich, A counterexample to the rank-uniform form of Kourovka Notebook Problem 14.23, preprint (2026), Theorem 1, the Kourovka Notebook (21st issue) marks 14.23 solved: true for each given rank, false if one function must work for all ranks, https://kourovkanotebookorg.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/kourovka_14_23_uniform_counterexample.pdf.

articles.title: Kourovka Problem 14.23, rank-uniform form
articles.statement:
There is a computable function
$f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ such that for every $n$ and every automorphism $\alpha$ of the
free group $F_n$ on $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$, the fixed subgroup $\mathrm{Fix}(\alpha)$ has a
finite free basis all of whose elements have reduced word length at most $f(\|\alpha\|)$, where
$\|\alpha\|$ is the maximum of the reduced word lengths of $\alpha(x_0), \dots, \alpha(x_{n-1})$.

This is the form of Kourovka Notebook Problem 14.23 (O. V. Bogopolski) in which one $f$ must
work for all ranks $n$.

articles.title: Fixed subgroup of a free group automorphism
articles.statement:
For an automorphism $\alpha$ of the free
group $F_n$ on $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$, the fixed subgroup of $\alpha$ is the subgroup
$\mathrm{Fix}(\alpha) = \{x \in F_n \mid \alpha(x) = x\}$ of $F_n$.

articles.title: Fixed subgroups with a short free basis
articles.statement:
Let $\alpha$ be an automorphism of the free group
$F_n$ on $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$, let $|w|$ be the length of the reduced word representing
$w \in F_n$, and let $L$ be a natural number. The fixed subgroup $\mathrm{Fix}(\alpha)$ has a
short free basis with bound $L$ when, for some $k \ge 0$, it has a free basis
$y_1, \dots, y_k$ with $|y_i| \le L$ for every $i$.

articles.title: Encoded words in a free group of finite rank
articles.statement:
A word of rank $r$ is a finite list of pairs
$(i, \varepsilon)$ with $i < r$ and $\varepsilon$ a Boolean. It encodes the element of the free
group $F_r$ of rank $r$ that is the product of its letters, where $(i, \mathrm{true})$ stands for
the $i$-th free generator and $(i, \mathrm{false})$ for its inverse.

articles.title: Free products of subgroups of $\mathrm{Aut}(F_n)$ embed in some $\mathrm{Aut}(F_m)$
articles.statement:
For
every natural number $n \ge 2$ and all subgroups $G$ and $H$ of the automorphism group
$\mathrm{Aut}(F_n)$ of the free group $F_n$ of rank $n$, there are a natural number $m$ and an
injective group homomorphism from the free product $G \ast H$ to $\mathrm{Aut}(F_m)$.

Jayadevan constructs, for subgroups $G \le \mathrm{Aut}(F_n)$ and $H \le \mathrm{Aut}(F_k)$ with
no finite-generation hypothesis, an embedding of $G \ast H$ in $\mathrm{Aut}(F_{n+k+3})$; the
Kourovka Notebook (21st issue) answers 18.11 "Yes, it is true" (AI solution confirmed by V. G.
Bardakov).

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Problem 18.11 (V. G. Bardakov); resolution: A. Jayadevan, Free products of free-group automorphism groups: a finite-rank embedding by separating cocycles, preprint, Zenodo record 22722085 (2026), abstract (for G ≤ Aut(F_n), H ≤ Aut(F_m), G ∗ H embeds in Aut(F_{n+m+3}); no finite-generation hypothesis); the Kourovka Notebook (21st issue) marks 18.11 solved (Yes, it is true; AI solution confirmed by V. G. Bardakov), https://zenodo.org/records/22722085.

articles.title: Bardakov's question on free products in $\mathrm{Aut}(F_n)$ (Kourovka 18.11)
articles.statement:
The statement
that for every natural number $n \ge 2$ and all subgroups $G$ and $H$ of the automorphism group
$\mathrm{Aut}(F_n)$ of the free group $F_n$ of rank $n$, there are a natural number $m$ and an
injective group homomorphism from the free product $G \ast H$ to $\mathrm{Aut}(F_m)$.

articles.title: IA-automorphism group of a free group is not linear
articles.statement:
Resolved false: the Kourovka Archive answers 15.10 No: `IA(Fₙ)` is not linear for `n ≥ 5` (Pettet)
and for every `n ≥ 3` (Bardakov and Mikhailov). Source: E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.),
Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026),
Archive of Solved Problems, Problem 15.10 (Yu. I. Merzlyakov; V. G. Bardakov); resolution: V. G.
Bardakov and R. Mikhailov, Commun. Algebra 36 (2008), no. 4, 1489-1499 (n ≥ 3); A. Pettet,
Cohomology of some subgroups of the automorphism group of a free group, Ph.D. thesis, 2006 (n ≥ 5),
Kourovka Archive, Problem 15.10.

articles.title: Kourovka Problem 15.10 (statement): linearity of IA-automorphism groups of free groups
articles.statement:
The statement that for some $n \ge 3$ the group $\mathrm{IA}(F_n)$ of automorphisms of the free
group $F_n$ on $n$ generators that act trivially on its abelianization $F_n/[F_n, F_n]$ is linear,
that is, there are a field $K$, a natural number $m$ and an injective group homomorphism
$\mathrm{IA}(F_n) \to \mathrm{GL}_m(K)$.

articles.title: IA-automorphisms of a free group
articles.statement:
For a natural number $n$, let $F_n$ be the free group on
$n$ generators. $\mathrm{IA}(F_n)$ is the subgroup of the automorphism group of $F_n$ consisting of
the automorphisms $\varphi$ that act trivially on the abelianization $F_n/[F_n, F_n]$, that is,
such that $\varphi(x)$ and $x$ have the same image in $F_n/[F_n, F_n]$ for every $x \in F_n$.

articles.title: Outer automorphism group of a free group
articles.statement:
For a natural number $n$, let $F_n$ be the free
group on $n$ generators. Its outer automorphism group $\mathrm{Out}(F_n)$ is the quotient of the
automorphism group $\mathrm{Aut}(F_n)$ by the normal subgroup generated by the inner
automorphisms. Since the inner automorphisms already form a normal subgroup $\mathrm{Inn}(F_n)$,
this is $\mathrm{Aut}(F_n) / \mathrm{Inn}(F_n)$.

articles.title: The word problem for Aut(Fₙ) is solvable in polynomial time
articles.statement:
Let $n \ge 2$ and let $F_n$ be the
free group on $n$ generators. For every natural number $k$ and every family
$g_0, \dots, g_{k-1}$ of automorphisms of $F_n$ that generates $\operatorname{Aut}(F_n)$, the word
problem of $\operatorname{Aut}(F_n)$ for this family belongs to the complexity class P. Here a word
is a finite list of letters $(i, b)$ with $i \in \mathbb{N}$ and $b$ a boolean, the letter
$(i, \mathrm{true})$ standing for $g_i$ and $(i, \mathrm{false})$ for $g_i^{-1}$, and the word
problem is the decision problem on bitstrings that accepts exactly the bitstrings that decode,
under the canonical bitstring encoding of lists of pairs of a natural number and a boolean, to a
word whose letter indices are all below $k$ and whose product in $\operatorname{Aut}(F_n)$ is the
identity; bitstrings that do not decode to a word are rejected.

Schleimer proves (Theorem 5.2) that the word problem for $\operatorname{Aut}(F_m)$ is solvable in
polynomial time, and observes (Remark 5.1) that changing the generating set alters running times
by at most a multiplicative constant; the Kourovka Archive answers 16.109 "Yes, there is".

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Archive of Solved Problems, Problem 16.109 (V. E. Shpilrain); resolution: S. Schleimer, Polynomial-time word problems, Comment. Math. Helv. 83 (2008), 741-765, Theorem 5.2 (the word problem for Aut(F_m) is polynomial time) and Remark 5.1 (choosing a different generating set alters running times by at most a multiplicative constant); Kourovka Archive, Problem 16.109 (Yes, there is), https://wrap.warwick.ac.uk/44057/.

articles.title: Polynomial-time word problem for Aut(Fₙ) (Kourovka 16.109)
articles.statement:
The proposition that for
every $n \ge 2$, writing $F_n$ for the free group on $n$ generators, for every natural number $k$
and every family $g_0, \dots, g_{k-1}$ of automorphisms of $F_n$ that generates
$\operatorname{Aut}(F_n)$, the word problem of $\operatorname{Aut}(F_n)$ for the family
$(g_i)$, a decision problem on bitstrings, belongs to the complexity class P.

articles.title: The word problem of Aut(Fₙ) for a family of automorphisms
articles.statement:
Let $F_n$ be the free group on
$n$ generators and let $g_0, \dots, g_{k-1}$ be automorphisms of $F_n$. A word is a finite list of
letters $(i, b)$ with $i \in \mathbb{N}$ and $b$ a boolean. The word problem for $(g_i)$ is the
decision problem that accepts a bitstring $x$ exactly when $x$ decodes, under the canonical
bitstring encoding of lists of pairs of a natural number and a boolean, to a word $w$ such that
every letter $(i, b)$ of $w$ has $i < k$ and the automorphism spelled by $w$ over $(g_i)$ is the
identity; here the letter $(i, \mathrm{true})$ stands for $g_i$ and $(i, \mathrm{false})$ for
$g_i^{-1}$. Bitstrings that do not decode to a word are rejected.

articles.title: The automorphism spelled by a word
articles.statement:
Let $F_n$ be the free group on $n$ generators and let
$g_0, \dots, g_{k-1}$ be automorphisms of $F_n$. A word $w = ((i_1, b_1), \dots, (i_r, b_r))$ is a
finite list of letters $(i, b)$ with $i \in \mathbb{N}$ and $b$ a boolean. The automorphism
spelled by $w$ over $(g_i)$ is the product $a_1 a_2 \cdots a_r$ in $\operatorname{Aut}(F_n)$,
whose group operation is composition, where for $i_j < k$ the factor $a_j$ is $g_{i_j}$ if $b_j$ is
true and $g_{i_j}^{-1}$ if $b_j$ is false, and for $i_j \ge k$ the factor $a_j$ is the identity.
The empty word spells the identity.

articles.title: Abelianized Cartesian powers of free groups can have torsion
articles.statement:
For some integer $n \ge 2$, the
abelianization of the unrestricted (Cartesian) product $F_n^{\mathbb{N}}$ of countably many copies
of the free group $F_n$ of rank $n$ contains a nontrivial element of finite order. That is, the
torsion-freeness asked for in Kourovka Problem 13.18 fails.

The Kourovka Archive answers 13.18 "No, it may contain elements of order 2" (O. Kharlampovich and
A. Myasnikov, 2001).

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Archive of Solved Problems, Problem 13.18 (A. M. Gaglione, D. Spellman); resolution: O. Kharlampovich and A. Myasnikov, in: Knots, braids, and mapping class groups (New York, 1998), Amer. Math. Soc., 2001, 77-83, Kourovka Archive, Problem 13.18: No, it may contain elements of order 2.

articles.title: Torsion-freeness of abelianized Cartesian powers of free groups (Kourovka 13.18)
articles.statement:
The
statement, posed by A. M. Gaglione and D. Spellman, that for every integer $n \ge 2$ the
abelianization of the unrestricted (Cartesian) product $F_n^{\mathbb{N}}$ of countably many copies
of the free group $F_n$ of rank $n$ is torsion-free: none of its nontrivial elements has finite
order.

articles.title: Bogopolski's Cayley–Hamilton analogue fails for free groups (Kourovka 17.32)
articles.statement:
There are a
natural number $n$, an element $w$ of the free group $F_n$ of rank $n$ and an automorphism
$\varphi$ of $F_n$ such that $w, \varphi(w), \dots, \varphi^n(w)$ generate $F_n$ but
$w, \varphi(w), \dots, \varphi^{n-1}(w)$ do not.

Ionin and Semidetnov (Answer 8.2) give the example $n = 2$, $F_2 = \langle x, y \rangle$, $w = xy$
and $\varphi(x) = yx$, $\varphi(y) = x$. The Kourovka Notebook (21st issue) answers 17.32 "No, it
is not true", citing their preprint and a preprint of O. Kharlampovich.

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Problem 17.32 (O. V. Bogopolski); resolution: V. Ionin and A. Semidetnov, On some more problems from the Kourovka Notebook, preprint, arXiv:2608.29219 (2026; solutions found with the assistance of large language models and checked by the authors, per its abstract); O. Kharlampovich, preprint (2026), Ionin-Semidetnov, Answer 8.2 (the assertion fails for n = 2: w = xy, φ(x) = yx, φ(y) = x); the Kourovka Notebook (21st issue) marks 17.32 solved (No, it is not true), https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.29219.

articles.title: Bogopolski's Cayley–Hamilton question for free groups (Kourovka 17.32)
articles.statement:
The assertion
that for every natural number $n$, every element $w$ of the free group $F_n$ of rank $n$ and every
automorphism $\varphi$ of $F_n$, if $w, \varphi(w), \dots, \varphi^n(w)$ generate $F_n$, then
already $w, \varphi(w), \dots, \varphi^{n-1}(w)$ generate $F_n$.

articles.title: Free groups of rank at least 3 have proper two-generated characteristic quotients
articles.statement:
For every
natural number $n \ge 3$, the free group $F_n$ on $n$ generators has a characteristic subgroup
$C \ne F_n$ such that the quotient $F_n / C$ is generated by two elements; since $2 < n$, the
quotient is generated by fewer than $n$ elements.

Resolved true: Coulon and Fournier-Facio (Theorem 1.1) prove that for all $n \ge 2$ the free group
$F_n$ admits continuum many pairwise non-isomorphic 2-generated infinite simple characteristic
quotients; for $n \ge 3$ such a quotient $F_n / C$ is generated by fewer than $n$ elements, and
$C$ is proper since the quotient is infinite. The Kourovka Notebook (21st issue) answers 17.62
"Yes, it is possible".

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Problem 17.62 (J. Conrad); resolution: R. Coulon and F. Fournier-Facio, Infinite simple characteristic quotients, preprint, arXiv:2312.11684, Theorem 1.1 (for all n ≥ 2, the free group of rank n admits continuum many pairwise non-isomorphic, 2-generated, infinite, simple, characteristic quotients; Section 1 notes that this answers Problem 17.62); the Kourovka Notebook (21st issue) marks 17.62 solved (Yes, it is possible; moreover, for all n ≥ 2, F_n admits continuum many pairwise non-isomorphic infinite simple characteristic 2-generated quotients), https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.11684.

articles.title: Kourovka Problem 17.62 (two-generated characteristic quotients of free groups)
articles.statement:
The
statement that for every natural number $n \ge 3$ the free group $F_n$ on $n$ generators has a
characteristic subgroup $C \ne F_n$ such that the quotient $F_n / C$ is generated by two elements,
hence by fewer than $n$ elements. This is the positive answer to Problem 17.62 (J. Conrad) in
every rank where two generators are fewer than $n$.

articles.title: Inclusion of derived subgroups does not imply inclusion in free groups
articles.statement:
There exist a free
group $F$ and non-cyclic subgroups $U$ and $V$ of $F$ such that the commutator subgroup $[U, U]$
is contained in the commutator subgroup $[V, V]$ but $U$ is not contained in $V$. That is, the
conjecture of Kourovka Problem 13.62 is false; the Kourovka Archive credits this answer to
M. J. Dunwoody.

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Archive of Solved Problems, Problem 13.62 (V. P. Shaptala); resolution: M. J. Dunwoody, Arch. Math. 16 (1965), 153-157, Kourovka Archive, Problem 13.62 (answer: No, it does not).

articles.title: Inclusion of derived subgroups in free groups (Kourovka 13.62)
articles.statement:
The conjecture of
V. P. Shaptala that for every free group $F$ and all non-cyclic subgroups $U$ and $V$ of $F$, if
the commutator subgroup $[U, U]$ is contained in the commutator subgroup $[V, V]$, then $U$ is
contained in $V$.

articles.title: Free metabelian group of rank $n$ (Kourovka 19.94)
articles.statement:
For a natural number $n$, let $F_n$
be the free group on $n$ generators. The free metabelian group of rank $n$ is the quotient
$M_n = F_n / F_n''$ of $F_n$ by its second derived subgroup $F_n'' = [[F_n, F_n], [F_n, F_n]]$.

articles.title: Equally distributed elements need not be automorphic (Kourovka 19.94)
articles.statement:
It is not the case
that for every natural number $n$ and all words $w_1, w_2$ in the free group $F_n$ of rank $n$,
the words $w_1$ and $w_2$ have the same distribution if and only if some automorphism of the free
metabelian group $M_n = F_n / F_n''$ maps the image of $w_1$ in $M_n$ to the image of $w_2$.

Ionin and Semidetnov (Answer 2.2) give two elements of the free metabelian group of rank $2$ with
the same distribution on every finite metabelian group that no automorphism maps one to the other
(the converse direction is automatic). The solution was found with the assistance of large
language models and checked by the authors; the 21st issue of the Kourovka Notebook marks 19.94
solved ("No, it is not true").

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Problem 19.94 (E. I. Timoshenko); resolution: V. Ionin and A. Semidetnov, On Some More Problems from the Kourovka Notebook, preprint, arXiv:2608.29219 (2026), Section 2, Answer 2.2 with Proposition 2.3 and Lemmas 2.6-2.7: in M₂ = ⟨x, y⟩ with c = [x, y] and a^z = z⁻¹az, the elements g₁ = c^{x²y⁷}(c^x)⁻¹(c^{xy⁷})⁻¹c and g₂ = c^{x³y⁷}(c^x)⁻¹(c^{x²y⁷})⁻¹c have the same distribution on every finite metabelian group but lie in distinct Aut(M₂)-orbits; found with the assistance of large language models and checked by the authors; the Kourovka Notebook (21st issue) marks 19.94 solved: No, it is not true, https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.29219.

articles.title: Timoshenko's question on equally distributed elements (Kourovka 19.94)
articles.statement:
The statement that
for every natural number $n$ and all words $w_1, w_2$ in the free group $F_n$ of rank $n$, the
words $w_1$ and $w_2$ have the same distribution if and only if some automorphism of the free
metabelian group $M_n = F_n / F_n''$ maps the image of $w_1$ in $M_n$ to the image of $w_2$.

articles.title: Words with the same distribution
articles.statement:
Let $n$ be a natural number and $F_n$ the free group on
generators $x_1, \dots, x_n$. Words $w_1, w_2 \in F_n$ have the same distribution when, for every
finite metabelian group $G$ (that is, $G'' = 1$) and every $g \in G$, the number of tuples
$(a_1, \dots, a_n) \in G^n$ with $w_1(a_1, \dots, a_n) = g$ equals the number of tuples with
$w_2(a_1, \dots, a_n) = g$. Here $w(a_1, \dots, a_n)$ is the image of $w$ under the homomorphism
$F_n \to G$ sending $x_i$ to $a_i$.

Since $G$ is metabelian, this depends only on the images of $w_1, w_2$ in the free metabelian group
$F_n / F_n''$.

articles.title: Compressed subgroups of free groups of finite rank are inert (Kourovka 19.102)
articles.statement:
For every
$n \in \mathbb{N}$, every compressed subgroup $H$ of the free group $F_n$ on $n$ generators is
inert.

The Kourovka Notebook (21st issue) answers 19.102 "Yes, it is true" (A. Jaikin-Zapirain, 2024),
whose Corollary 1.2 proves that compressed and inert are equivalent for finitely generated
subgroups of a free group.

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Problem 19.102 (E. Ventura); resolution: A. Jaikin-Zapirain, Free groups are L^2-subgroup rigid, preprint, arXiv:2403.09515 (2024), abstract and Corollary 1.2: for a finitely generated subgroup H of a free group F, H is compressed iff H is inert iff H is L²-independent, answering the question of Dicks and Ventura (Kourovka 19.102); the Kourovka Notebook (21st issue) marks 19.102 solved, https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.09515.

articles.title: Ventura's compressed-implies-inert problem in finite rank (Kourovka 19.102)
articles.statement:
The
proposition that for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, every compressed subgroup of the free group $F_n$ on
$n$ generators is inert.

articles.title: Fixed subgroups of endomorphisms of free groups are inert
articles.statement:
Let $n \in \mathbb{N}$, let $F_n$ be
the free group on $n$ generators, and for a subgroup $H \le F_n$ let $r(H)$ be its rank, the least
size of a finite generating set of $H$, or $\infty$ if $H$ is not finitely generated. For every
endomorphism $\varphi$ of $F_n$, the fixed subgroup $\{x \in F_n \mid \varphi(x) = x\}$ of
$\varphi$ is inert in $F_n$: its intersection with every subgroup $K \le F_n$ has rank at most
$r(K)$. This answers Kourovka Problem 19.105 (E. Ventura) in the affirmative.

The Kourovka Notebook (21st issue) answers 19.105 "Yes, it is true", citing A. Jaikin-Zapirain
(2024), whose Corollary 1.2 proves that compressed and inert are equivalent for finitely generated
subgroups of a free group.

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Problem 19.105 (E. Ventura); resolution: A. Jaikin-Zapirain, Free groups are L^2-subgroup rigid, preprint, arXiv:2403.09515 (2024), Corollary 1.2: for a finitely generated subgroup of a free group, compressed iff inert; the Kourovka Notebook (21st issue) answers 19.105 "Yes, it is true" citing this preprint, https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.09515.

articles.title: Kourovka Problem 19.105 (Ventura) for free groups of finite rank
articles.statement:
The statement that for
every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and every endomorphism $\varphi$ of the free group $F_n$ on $n$ generators,
the fixed subgroup $\{x \in F_n \mid \varphi(x) = x\}$ of $\varphi$ is inert in $F_n$.

articles.title: Subgroup of a free group generated by a list of words
articles.statement:
Let $F_n$ be the free group on
generators $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$. A word is a finite list of letters $(i, b)$ with $i < n$ and $b$
a boolean, where $(i, \mathrm{true})$ stands for $x_i$ and $(i, \mathrm{false})$ for $x_i^{-1}$.
Given a finite list of words, this is the subgroup of $F_n$ generated by the elements of $F_n$
that the words represent, each word representing the product of its letters.

articles.title: Inertness is decidable in free groups of finite rank (Kourovka Problem 19.104)
articles.statement:
For every
natural number $n$, let $F_n$ be the free group on generators $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$, and give a
finitely generated subgroup of $F_n$ by a finite list of generating words in the letters
$x_i^{\pm 1}$. Then there is an algorithm deciding, for such a list, whether the subgroup $H$ it
generates is inert, that is, whether $r(H \cap K) \le r(K)$ for every subgroup $K$ of $F_n$. Here
the rank $r(L)$ of a subgroup $L$ is the least size of a finite generating set of $L$, and
$r(L) = \infty$ when $L$ is not finitely generated; "an algorithm" means that the predicate on
lists of words is computable.

Jaikin-Zapirain proved that a finitely generated subgroup of a free group is inert if and only if
it is compressed, and compressedness is known to be decidable.

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Problem 19.104 (E. Ventura); resolution: A. Jaikin-Zapirain, Free groups are L^2-subgroup rigid, preprint, arXiv:2403.09515 (2024), Corollary 1.3(2) (citing Kourovka 19.104): it is algorithmically decidable, for a finitely generated subgroup of a free group, whether it is inert (compressedness is decidable and equivalent to inertness by Corollary 1.2); the Kourovka Notebook (21st issue) marks 19.104 solved, https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.09515.

articles.title: Kourovka Problem 19.104 (statement): deciding inertness
articles.statement:
The statement that for every
natural number $n$ there is an algorithm deciding, for a finite list of words in the generators
$x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$ of the free group $F_n$ and their inverses, whether the subgroup of $F_n$
they generate is inert; that is, the predicate on lists of words is computable.

articles.title: The intersection of two compressed subgroups of a finite-rank free group is compressed
articles.statement:
For
every natural number $n$ and all subgroups $H$ and $K$ of the free group $F_n$ on $n$
generators, if $H$ and $K$ are compressed, then $H \cap K$ is compressed. That is, Kourovka
Problem 19.103 has a positive answer for the intersection of two subgroups of a free group of
finite rank.

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Problem 19.103 (E. Ventura); resolution: A. Jaikin-Zapirain, Free groups are L^2-subgroup rigid, preprint, arXiv:2403.09515 (2024), Corollary 1.3(1) (citing Kourovka 19.103): the intersection of two compressed subgroups of a free group is again compressed, from Corollary 1.2 (compressed iff inert for finitely generated subgroups); the Kourovka Notebook (21st issue) marks 19.103 solved, https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.09515.

articles.title: Kourovka Problem 19.103 for two compressed subgroups
articles.statement:
The statement that for every
natural number $n$ and all subgroups $H$ and $K$ of the free group $F_n$ on $n$ generators, if $H$
and $K$ are compressed, then $H \cap K$ is compressed.

articles.title: Compressed subgroup of a free group (Kourovka 19.103)
articles.statement:
A subgroup $H$ of the free group
$F_n$ on $n$ generators is compressed when $r(H) \le r(K)$ for every subgroup $K$ of $F_n$ that
contains $H$, where $r$ denotes the rank of a subgroup.

articles.title: Compressed subgroup of a free group of finite rank
articles.statement:
Let $F_n$ be the free group on $n$
generators and $r(K) \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$ the rank of a subgroup $K$. A subgroup $H$ of
$F_n$ is compressed when $r(H) \le r(K)$ for every subgroup $K$ of $F_n$ containing $H$.

articles.title: Inert subgroups of a free group
articles.statement:
Let $F_n$ be the free group on $n$ generators and let
$r(K)$ denote the rank of a subgroup $K$. A subgroup $H \le F_n$ is inert if
$r(H \cap K) \le r(K)$ for every subgroup $K \le F_n$.

articles.title: Inert subgroup of a free group of finite rank
articles.statement:
A subgroup $H$ of the free group $F_n$ on
$n$ generators is inert if $r(H \cap K) \le r(K)$ for every subgroup $K$ of $F_n$, where the rank
$r(L)$ of a subgroup $L$ is the least size of a finite generating set of $L$, and $\infty$ when $L$
is not finitely generated.

articles.title: Inert subgroup of a free group of finite rank
articles.statement:
Let $F_n$ be the free group on $n$
generators and $r(K) \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$ the rank of a subgroup $K$. A subgroup $H$ of
$F_n$ is inert when $r(H \cap K) \le r(K)$ for every subgroup $K$ of $F_n$.

articles.title: Rank of a subgroup (Kourovka 19.103)
articles.statement:
For a subgroup $H$ of a group $G$, the rank
$r(H) \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$ is the least number of elements of a finite subset of $G$ that
generates $H$, with $r(H) = \infty$ when $H$ is not finitely generated.

articles.title: Rank of a subgroup
articles.statement:
For a subgroup $H$ of a group $G$, the rank $r(H)$ is the least size of
a finite subset of $G$ that generates $H$, or $\infty$ if $H$ is not finitely generated.

articles.title: Rank of a subgroup, possibly infinite
articles.statement:
For a subgroup $H$ of a group $G$, the rank
$r(H) \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$ is the least size of a finite subset of $G$ that generates
$H$, and $r(H) = \infty$ if $H$ is not finitely generated.

articles.title: Rank of a subgroup
articles.statement:
For a subgroup $H$ of a group $G$, the rank
$r(H) \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$ is the least size of a finite subset of $G$ that generates
$H$, with $r(H) = \infty$ when $H$ is not finitely generated.

articles.title: Negative answer to Kourovka 11.82 on shortest elements of normal closures
articles.statement:
There are a free
group $F$, an element $r \ne 1$ of $F$, and a nontrivial element $s$ of the normal closure $R$ of
$r$ in $F$ whose reduced word length is minimal among the nontrivial elements of $R$, such that $s$
is conjugate neither to $r$ nor to $r^{-1}$, nor, for any $f \in F$, to
$[r, f] = r^{-1} f^{-1} r f$ or to $[r^{-1}, f] = r f^{-1} r^{-1} f$.

The Kourovka Archive answers 11.82 "No, not always" (McCool).

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Archive of Solved Problems, Problem 11.82 (V. N. Remeslennikov); resolution: J. McCool, Glasgow Math. J. 43, no. 1 (2001), 123-124, Kourovka Archive, Problem 11.82: "No, not always", https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v49.

articles.title: Shortest elements of normal closures in free groups (Kourovka 11.82, Remeslennikov)
articles.statement:
The
statement that for every free group $F$ and every $r \ne 1$ in $F$, if $s$ is a nontrivial element
of the normal closure $R$ of $r$ in $F$ whose reduced word length is minimal among the nontrivial
elements of $R$, then $s$ is conjugate to $r$, to $r^{-1}$, or, for some $f \in F$, to
$[r, f] = r^{-1} f^{-1} r f$ or to $[r^{-1}, f] = r f^{-1} r^{-1} f$.

articles.title: No massive normally independent set in the free group of rank two
articles.statement:
There is no subset $E$ of
the free group $F_2$ on two generators such that no element $w \in E$ lies in the normal closure
of $E \setminus \{w\}$ and, for every real number $c$ with $0 < c < 3$ and every natural number
$N$, there is $n \ge N$ for which at least $c^n$ elements of $E$ have reduced word length $n$.

Koch-Hyde and Olive prove that a subset $S$ of the ball $B_n$ of the free group $F_r$ in which no
$x \in S$ lies in the subgroup generated by $S \setminus \{x\}$ has $|S| = O((2r - 1)^{n/2})$.
Normal independence implies this independence, so for every such $E \subseteq F_2$ the set $E_n$
of its elements of length $n$ has $|E_n| = O(3^{n/2})$, and the growth rate is at most
$\sqrt 3 < 3$. The Kourovka Notebook (21st issue) marks Problem 10.13 solved, "No, there is no
such set".

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Problem 10.13 (R. I. Grigorchuk); resolution: L. Koch-Hyde and É. Olive, Two problems about bases and independent sets in free groups, arXiv:2609.00382 (2026), Theorem 1.7 (an independent set S ⊆ B_n ⊆ F_r has |S| = O((2r - 1)^{n/2})) and the Solution to Problem 1.5; the Kourovka Notebook (21st issue) marks 10.13 solved, https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.00382.

articles.title: Grigorchuk's problem on massive independent sets in the free group of rank two
articles.statement:
The
statement that some subset $E$ of the free group $F_2$ on two generators is normally independent
(no $w \in E$ lies in the normal closure of $E \setminus \{w\}$) and massive: for every real number
$c$ with $0 < c < 3$ and every natural number $N$ there is $n \ge N$ such that the set $E_n$ of
elements of $E$ of reduced word length $n$ has at least $c^n$ elements.

Since $F_2$ has $4 \cdot 3^{n-1}$ reduced words of length $n \ge 1$, $\limsup |E_n|^{1/n} \le 3$
always, so massiveness says $\limsup |E_n|^{1/n} = 3$, as in Kourovka Notebook Problem 10.13
(R. I. Grigorchuk).

articles.title: Normally independent sets in the free group of rank two
articles.statement:
A subset $E$ of the free group
$F_2$ on two generators is normally independent when no element $w \in E$ lies in the normal
closure of $E \setminus \{w\}$, the smallest normal subgroup of $F_2$ containing
$E \setminus \{w\}$.

articles.title: Orbit-blocking words exist (Kourovka Problem 20.88)
articles.statement:
For every $r \ge 1$ and every element $u$
of the free group $F_r$ on $r$ generators there is $v \in F_r$ such that, for every automorphism
$\varphi$ of $F_r$ for which the reduced word of $\varphi(u)$ is cyclically reduced, the reduced
word of $v$ is not a subword (a contiguous factor) of the reduced word of $\varphi(u)$.

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Problem 20.88 (V. Shpilrain); resolution: L. Koch-Hyde, S. O'Connor, É. Olive and V. Shpilrain, Orbit-blocking words in free groups, preprint, arXiv:2505.00477 (2025), Theorem 6.1 and Section 6: for every w ∈ F_r there are w-orbit-blocking words, i.e. words v that are not subwords of the cyclic reduction of φ(w) for any automorphism φ (built from primitivity-blocking words such as x₁² ⋯ x_r² x₁); Kourovka Notebook (21st issue), Problem 20.88: Yes, it is true, https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.00477.

articles.title: Kourovka Problem 20.88 (statement)
articles.statement:
The statement that for every $r \ge 1$ and every
element $u$ of the free group $F_r$ on $r$ generators there is $v \in F_r$ such that, for every
automorphism $\varphi$ of $F_r$ for which the reduced word of $\varphi(u)$ is cyclically reduced,
the reduced word of $v$ is not a subword (a contiguous factor) of the reduced word of $\varphi(u)$.

articles.title: The almost-palindromic width of $F_2$ is infinite (Kourovka 19.8)
articles.statement:
There are no positive
integers $m$ and $c$ such that every element of the free group $F_2$ on generators $x, y$ is a
product of at most $c$ elements, each represented by an almost $m$-palindrome, that is, by a word
in $x^{\pm 1}, y^{\pm 1}$ (not necessarily reduced) that differs from a palindrome of the same
length in at most $m$ positions. So the question of Kourovka Problem 19.8 has a negative answer.

Staiger proved more: for every $m \ge 0$, the $m$-almost-palindromic width of every non-abelian
free group is infinite.

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Problem 19.8 (V. G. Bardakov); resolution: M. Staiger, On the almost-palindromic width of free groups, J. Algebra 659 (2024), 475-481 (arXiv:2306.15752), Section 1: m-almost-palindromes are words of the free monoid on the letters x^{±1}, y^{±1} (not necessarily reduced) within Hamming distance m of a palindrome, and the width is taken for the group elements they represent; Theorem 1: for a non-abelian free group F and every m ≥ 0 the m-almost-palindromic width of F is infinite; the Kourovka Notebook (21st issue) marks 19.8 solved: No, there are no such integers, https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.15752.

articles.title: Finite almost-palindromic width of $F_2$ (Kourovka 19.8)
articles.statement:
The proposition that there are
positive integers $m$ and $c$ such that every element of the free group $F_2$ on generators $x, y$
is a product of at most $c$ elements, each represented by an almost $m$-palindrome, that is, by a
word in $x^{\pm 1}, y^{\pm 1}$ (not necessarily reduced) that differs from a palindrome of the
same length in at most $m$ positions.

This is the question posed by V. G. Bardakov as Kourovka Problem 19.8.

articles.title: Almost palindromes
articles.statement:
For a natural number $m$, a word $w$ in the letters $x^{\pm 1}$ and
$y^{\pm 1}$ is an almost $m$-palindrome if there is a palindrome $p$ in the same letters with the
same length as $w$ such that $w$ and $p$ differ in at most $m$ positions. The word $w$ need not be
reduced.

articles.title: Free metabelian group $M_n$ (Kourovka 14.85)
articles.statement:
For a natural number $n$, the free metabelian
group $M_n = F_n / F_n''$ of rank $n$: the quotient of the free group $F_n$ on $n$ generators by
its second derived subgroup $F_n'' = [[F_n, F_n], [F_n, F_n]]$.

articles.title: Primitive elements of the free metabelian group
articles.statement:
Let $F_n$ be the free group on $n$
generators, let $F_n''$ be its second derived subgroup, and let $M_n = F_n / F_n''$ be the free
metabelian group of rank $n$. Let $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$ be the images in $M_n$ of the free
generators of $F_n$. An element $y$ of $M_n$ is primitive when $y = \sigma(x_i)$ for some
automorphism $\sigma$ of $M_n$ and some index $i$; that is, $y$ is the image of a standard basis
element under an automorphism of $M_n$.

articles.title: Primitive-preserving endomorphisms of free metabelian groups are automorphisms
articles.statement:
For every
natural number $n$, every endomorphism $\varphi$ of the free metabelian group $M_n$ of rank $n$
that maps every primitive element of $M_n$ to a primitive element is bijective, hence an
automorphism of $M_n$. This answers Kourovka Problem 14.85 positively.

Ionin and Semidetnov (Section 1, Answer 1.2) prove that every primitive-preserving endomorphism of
the free metabelian group $M_n$ is an automorphism; the Kourovka Notebook (21st issue) answers
Problem 14.85 "Yes, it is".

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Problem 14.85 (E. I. Timoshenko, V. Shpilrain); resolution: V. Ionin and A. Semidetnov, On some more problems from the Kourovka Notebook, preprint, arXiv:2608.29219 (2026), Section 1, Answer 1.2: every primitive-preserving endomorphism of M_n is an automorphism (the abstract states that the solutions were found with the assistance of large language models and checked by the authors); the Kourovka Notebook (21st issue) marks 14.85 solved (Yes, it is), https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.29219.

articles.title: Primitive-preserving endomorphism problem for free metabelian groups (Kourovka 14.85)
articles.statement:
The statement, posed by E. I. Timoshenko and V. Shpilrain, that for every natural number $n$,
every endomorphism $\varphi$ of the free metabelian group $M_n$ of rank $n$ that maps every
primitive element of $M_n$ to a primitive element is bijective, hence an automorphism.

articles.title: Bogopolski's logarithmic-index separation fails in free groups of rank at least 2
articles.statement:
For every
integer $r \ge 2$ and every real number $C$, there is an element $w$ of the free group $F_r$ of
rank $r$ whose reduced word length $n$ satisfies $n > 1$ and such that every subgroup of finite
index in $F_r$ that does not contain $w$ has index greater than $C \log n$, where $\log$ is the
natural logarithm. That is, the logarithmic-index separation property of Kourovka Problem 15.35
holds for no rank $r \ge 2$.

Bou-Rabee and McReynolds (Theorem 1.4) prove that for every rank $m > 1$ the maximal divisibility
function of $F_m$ on words of length at most $n$ is not $O(\log n)$, which rules out every $C$;
the Kourovka Archive answers 15.35 "No, it is not true".

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Archive of Solved Problems, Problem 15.35 (O. V. Bogopolski); resolution: K. Bou-Rabee and D. B. McReynolds, Asymptotic growth and least common multiples in groups, Bull. London Math. Soc. 43 (2011), 1059-1068, arXiv:0907.3681, Theorem 1.4 (for m > 1, max D_{F_m}(n) is not bounded by O(log n)), https://arxiv.org/abs/0907.3681.

articles.title: Logarithmic-index separation in free groups (Kourovka 15.35)
articles.statement:
The statement, posed by
O. V. Bogopolski, that for some integer $r \ge 2$ there is a real number $C$ such that every
element $w$ of the free group $F_r$ of rank $r$ whose reduced word length $n$ satisfies $n > 1$
lies outside some subgroup of $F_r$ of finite index at most $C \log n$, where $\log$ is the
natural logarithm.

articles.title: Retract of a group
articles.statement:
A subgroup $R$ of a group $F$ is a retract of $F$ when there is an
endomorphism $r \colon F \to F$ whose image is $R$ and which fixes every element of $R$.

articles.title: Negative answer to Bergman's retract intersection question (Kourovka Problem 17.19)
articles.statement:
It is not
the case that for every natural number $n$, every retract $R$ of the free group $F_n$ on $n$
generators and every finitely generated subgroup $H$ of $F_n$, the intersection $H \cap R$ is a
retract of $H$.

Snopce, Tanushevski and Zalesskii (2022) give a free group $F$ of finite rank, a retract $R$ of $F$
and a finitely generated subgroup $H$ of $F$ such that $H \cap R$ is not a retract of $H$; the
Kourovka Archive answers 17.19 "No, it need not".

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Archive of Solved Problems, Problem 17.19 (G. M. Bergman); resolution: I. Snopce, S. Tanushevski and P. Zalesskii, Int. Math. Res. Notices 2022, no. 11 (2022), 8280-8294, Kourovka Archive, Problem 17.19 (No, it need not).

articles.title: Bergman's retract intersection question (Kourovka Problem 17.19)
articles.statement:
The statement that for
every natural number $n$, every retract $R$ of the free group $F_n$ on $n$ generators and every
finitely generated subgroup $H$ of $F_n$, the intersection $H \cap R$ is a retract of $H$.

A subgroup of a free group is finitely generated exactly when it has finite rank.

articles.title: A non-cyclic subgroup of a free group with normal derived subgroup is normal
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a
free group on an arbitrary set of generators, and suppose that $F$ is not cyclic. Then every
subgroup $R$ of $F$ that is not cyclic and whose derived subgroup $[R, R]$ is normal in $F$ is
itself normal in $F$.

Resolved true: Tursunbaev proves that subgroups $H$, $K$ of a free group of arbitrary rank whose
derived subgroups $H' = [H, H]$ and $K' = [K, K]$ are equal and nontrivial coincide; for a
non-cyclic $R$ with $R' = [R, R]$ normal in $F$ and any $f \in F$, the conjugate
$R^f = f^{-1} R f$ satisfies $(R^f)' = (R')^f = R' \ne 1$, so $R^f = R$. The Kourovka Notebook
(21st issue) marks 11.124 solved, "Yes, it is true".

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Problem 11.124 (V. E. Shpilrain); resolution: A. Tursunbaev, Subgroups of free groups with the same derived subgroup, arXiv:2609.06755 (2026), main theorem (subgroups `H`, `K` of a free group of arbitrary rank with `H' = K' ≠ 1` are equal) and its corollary answering 11.124; the Kourovka Notebook (21st issue) marks 11.124 solved, https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.06755.

articles.title: Kourovka Problem 11.124 (free-group subgroups with normal derived subgroup)
articles.statement:
The
statement that for every set $X$ such that the free group $F$ on $X$ is not cyclic, every subgroup
$R$ of $F$ that is not cyclic and whose derived subgroup $[R, R]$ is normal in $F$ is itself
normal in $F$.

articles.title: Free soluble group of rank two
articles.statement:
The free soluble group of rank `2` and derived length `d`: the quotient `F₂ / F₂⁽ᵈ⁾` of the free
group on two generators by the `d`-th term of its derived series.

articles.title: Free soluble groups of rank two have test elements
articles.statement:
Resolved true: the Kourovka Archive answers 14.88 "Yes, it does" (Timoshenko): for every `d > 2` the
free soluble group `F₂/F₂⁽ᵈ⁾` of rank `2` and derived length `d` has a test element. Source: E. I.
Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st
issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Archive of Solved Problems, Problem 14.88 (B. Fine, V. Shpilrain);
resolution: E. I. Timoshenko, Computing test rank for a free solvable group, Algebra and Logic 45
(2006), no. 4, 254-260, main result (the test rank of a non-abelian free solvable group of finite
rank is one less than its rank, so F₂/F₂⁽ᵈ⁾ has test elements for every d > 2), as recorded in V.
Shpilrain's list of open problems in combinatorial group theory, problem (S9); Kourovka Archive,
Problem 14.88 (answer: Yes, it does), https://shpilrain.ccny.cuny.edu/gworld/problems/Back2.html.

articles.title: Kourovka Problem 14.88 (test elements of free soluble groups of rank 2)
articles.statement:
The statement that
for every integer $d > 2$ the free soluble group $F_2 / F_2^{(d)}$ of rank $2$ and derived length
$d$ has a test element, where $F_2$ is the free group on two generators and $F_2^{(d)}$ is the
$d$-th term of its derived series.

Kourovka Notebook Problem 14.88 is due to B. Fine and V. Shpilrain.

articles.title: Test element
articles.statement:
An element $u$ of a group $G$ is a test element of $G$ if every endomorphism
$\varphi$ of $G$ with $\varphi(u) = u$ is bijective, that is, an automorphism of $G$.

articles.title: $\mathrm{SL}_3(\mathbb{Z})$ is not $(2,3)$-generated
articles.statement:
There are no $a, b \in
\mathrm{SL}_3(\mathbb{Z})$ such that $a$ has order $2$, $b$ has order $3$, and $a$ and $b$ generate
$\mathrm{SL}_3(\mathbb{Z})$. Equivalently, $\mathrm{SL}_3(\mathbb{Z})$ is not a quotient of the
modular group $\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{Z}) \cong C_2 \ast C_3$.

This is the negative answer to Kourovka Notebook Problem 14.49 (M. Conder), due to Tamburini and
Zucca, and Nuzhin.

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Archive of Solved Problems, Problem 14.49 (M. Conder); resolution: M. C. Tamburini and P. Zucca, Rend. Lincei Mat. Appl. (9) 11 (2000), no. 1, 5-7; Ya. N. Nuzhin, Math. Notes 70 (2001), no. 1-2, 71-78, Kourovka Archive, Problem 14.49 (answer: No, it is not; SL_d(ℤ) is such a quotient for d ≥ 28).

articles.title: $(2,3)$-generation of $\mathrm{SL}_3(\mathbb{Z})$ (Kourovka 14.49)
articles.statement:
The statement that
there are $a, b \in \mathrm{SL}_3(\mathbb{Z})$ such that $a$ has order $2$, $b$ has order $3$, and
$a$ and $b$ generate $\mathrm{SL}_3(\mathbb{Z})$.

Kourovka Notebook Problem 14.49 (M. Conder) asks whether $\mathrm{SL}_3(\mathbb{Z})$ is a quotient
of the modular group $\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{Z}) \cong C_2 \ast C_3$; since
$\mathrm{SL}_3(\mathbb{Z})$ is not cyclic, this is equivalent to the statement above.

articles.title: Subgroup generated by a symmetric set
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a group and let $X \subseteq G$
satisfy $X^{-1} = X$, where $X^{-1} = \{x^{-1} : x \in X\}$. Then the subgroup of $G$
generated by $X$ equals $\bigcup_{n \in \mathbb{N}} X^n$, where $X^0 = \{1\}$ and
$X^{n+1} = X^n X = \{yx : y \in X^n,\ x \in X\}$.

## Sources

- 2310.10246 D01 (main.tex:146).

articles.title: Lucchini's coprime generation bound fails
articles.statement:
There exist a finite group $G$, subgroups $A$ and
$B$ of $G$ of coprime orders that together generate $G$, and a natural number $d$ such that each
of $A$ and $B$ is generated by at most $d$ elements, but no set of at most $d + 1$ elements
generates $G$. That is, Kourovka Problem 16.53 has a negative answer.

Muliarchyk constructs such groups for every $d \ge 2$, with $A$ and $B$ each needing exactly $d$
generators and $G$ needing exactly $d + 2$; there $A$ and $B$ are metabelian of exponents $6$ and
$55$ and lie inside a finite power of $\mathrm{PSL}_2(11)$.

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Problem 16.53 (A. Lucchini); resolution: K. Muliarchyk, Coprime generation through coset counts: a counterexample to Kourovka Notebook Problem 16.53, preprint (2026), Theorem 1 (for every d ≥ 2 finite groups A_d, B_d ≤ G_d = ⟨A_d, B_d⟩ with coprime orders, d(A_d) = d(B_d) = d and d(G_d) = d + 2); the Kourovka Notebook (21st issue) marks 16.53 solved (No, not always), https://kourovkanotebookorg.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/kourovka_16_53_solution.pdf.

articles.title: Lucchini's coprime generation bound (Kourovka 16.53)
articles.statement:
The statement that for every finite
group $G$, all subgroups $A$ and $B$ of $G$ of coprime orders that together generate $G$, and every
natural number $d$, if each of $A$ and $B$ is generated by at most $d$ elements, then $G$ is
generated by at most $d + 1$ elements.

articles.title: Eulerian polynomial factorization implies $p$-solvability
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group, let $p$
be a prime, and let $\varphi$ be an Eulerian function of $G$, with values in the integer polynomial
ring $\mathbb{Z}[x_0, x_1, \dots]$. If the Eulerian polynomial $\varphi(G)$ is a product $PQ$ of
integer polynomials where $P$ involves no variable other than $x_p$ and $x_p$ does not occur in
$Q$, then $G$ is $p$-solvable.

Resolved true: the Kourovka Archive answers 11.104(b) Yes, citing Damian and Lucchini (2007).

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Archive of Solved Problems, Problem 11.104 (G. E. Wall); resolution: E. Detomi and A. Lucchini, J. London Math. Soc. (2) 70 (2004), 165-181 (a); E. Damian and A. Lucchini, Commun. Algebra 35 (2007), 3451-3472 (b), Kourovka Archive, Problem 11.104 ("Yes, the converses are true").

articles.title: Kourovka Problem 11.104(b) (Eulerian polynomials and $p$-solvability)
articles.statement:
This is the
statement that for every finite group $G$, every prime $p$ and every Eulerian function $\varphi$ of
$G$, with values in the integer polynomial ring $\mathbb{Z}[x_0, x_1, \dots]$: if the Eulerian
polynomial $\varphi(G)$ is a product $PQ$ of integer polynomials where $P$ involves no variable
other than $x_p$ and $x_p$ does not occur in $Q$, then $G$ is $p$-solvable.

articles.title: Solvability from one-variable factorizations of the Eulerian polynomial
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite
group and let $\varphi$ be an Eulerian function of $G$, with values in the integer polynomial ring
$\mathbb{Z}[x_0, x_1, \dots]$. If there are a finite set $S$ of primes and, for each $q \in S$, an
integer polynomial $P_q$ involving no variable other than $x_q$, such that the Eulerian polynomial
$\varphi(G)$ equals $\prod_{q \in S} P_q$, then $G$ is solvable.

Resolved true: the Kourovka Archive answers 11.104(a) Yes, citing Detomi and Lucchini (2004).

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Archive of Solved Problems, Problem 11.104 (G. E. Wall); resolution: E. Detomi and A. Lucchini, J. London Math. Soc. (2) 70 (2004), 165-181 (a); E. Damian and A. Lucchini, Commun. Algebra 35 (2007), 3451-3472 (b), Kourovka Archive, Problem 11.104 ("Yes, the converses are true").

articles.title: Kourovka Problem 11.104(a) (Eulerian polynomials and solvability, G. E. Wall)
articles.statement:
This is the
statement that for every finite group $G$ and every Eulerian function $\varphi$ of $G$, with values
in the integer polynomial ring $\mathbb{Z}[x_0, x_1, \dots]$: if there are a finite set $S$ of
primes and, for each $q \in S$, an integer polynomial $P_q$ involving no variable other than $x_q$,
such that the Eulerian polynomial $\varphi(G)$ equals $\prod_{q \in S} P_q$, then $G$ is
solvable.

articles.title: Eulerian function of a group (G. E. Wall)
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a group and let $f$ be the order
polynomial. A function $\varphi$ from the subgroups of $G$ to the integer polynomial ring
$\mathbb{Z}[x_0, x_1, \dots]$ is an Eulerian function of $G$ if $\sum_{K \le H} \varphi(K) = f(H)$
for every subgroup $H$ of $G$, the sum running over the subgroups $K$ of $H$. The value
$\varphi(G)$ is the Eulerian polynomial of $G$.

For finite $G$ this relation determines $\varphi$ uniquely, by induction on $H$. If infinitely many
subgroups $K \le H$ have $\varphi(K) \ne 0$, the sum is read as $0$.

articles.title: $p$-solvable group
articles.statement:
For a natural number $p$, a group $G$ is $p$-solvable if it has a chain
of subgroups $1 = N_0 \le N_1 \le \dots \le N_n = G$ in which each $N_i$ is normal in $N_{i+1}$ and
each index $[N_{i+1} : N_i]$, taken to be $0$ when it is infinite, is a power $p^k$ with $k \ge 0$
or is coprime to $p$. For finite $G$ and prime $p$ this says that every factor $N_{i+1}/N_i$ is a
$p$-group or has order prime to $p$.

articles.title: Order polynomial of a subgroup
articles.statement:
For a subgroup $H$ of a group, the order polynomial of $H$
is $f(H) = \prod_p x_p^{v_p(|H|)}$ in the integer polynomial ring $\mathbb{Z}[x_0, x_1, \dots]$,
where $p$ runs over the primes, $x_p$ is the variable indexed by $p$, and $v_p(|H|)$ is the
exponent of $p$ in the order $|H|$ of $H$. If $H$ is infinite, $f(H) = 1$.

articles.title: Finite simple groups are generated by two elements of prime-power order
articles.statement:
Every finite simple
group $G$ is generated by two elements $x, y \in G$ whose orders are prime powers, that is, each
of the form $p^k$ with $p$ prime and $k \ge 1$, where the prime and the exponent may differ
between $x$ and $y$. This answers Kourovka Problem 18.52 positively.

The Kourovka Archive answers 18.52 "Yes, it is" (mod CFSG): by C. S. H. King (2017) every finite
(non-abelian) simple group is generated by an involution and an element of prime order; a cyclic
group of prime order is generated by one element of prime order.

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Archive of Solved Problems, Problem 18.52 (J. Krempa); resolution: C. S. H. King, J.
