articles.title: A non-modular complete lattice of formations exists (Kourovka 18.92(b))
articles.statement:
There is a complete
lattice of formations of finite groups that is not modular: a nonempty set $\Theta$ of formations
of finite groups, ordered by inclusion, that contains the intersection of each of its nonempty
subsets and has a largest element, in which the modular law $A \vee (B \wedge C) = (A \vee B)
\wedge C$ for $A \le C$ fails, joins being least upper bounds in $\Theta$ and meets intersections.

The Kourovka Notebook (21st issue) answers 18.92(b) "Yes" (Kinyon-Urban, 2026, confirmed by A. N.
Skiba): writing $\mathfrak{F}_S$ for the finite groups whose order has all prime divisors in $S$,
the formations $\mathfrak{F}_S$ with $S = \emptyset, \{2\}, \{2, 3\}, \{5\}$ and $S$ the set of all
primes are closed under intersections and form the pentagon $N_5$.

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Problem 18.92 (A. N. Skiba); resolution: M. Kinyon and J. Urban, Results on problems from the Kourovka Notebook, preprint, version 4, 19 September 2026, Section 3.29 (Problem 18.92): with F_S the finite groups whose order has all prime divisors in S, {F_S : S finite} ∪ {F_P} is not algebraic and the formations with prime sets ∅, {2}, {2, 3}, {5}, P form a pentagon N_5; an AI solution confirmed by A. N. Skiba, accepted in the Kourovka Notebook (21st issue), https://kourovkanotebookorg.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/kourovka-mathematics.pdf.

articles.title: The non-modular formation lattice problem (Kourovka 18.92(b), A. N. Skiba)
articles.statement:
The proposition
that there is a complete lattice of formations of finite groups that is not modular, joins being
least upper bounds in the lattice and meets being intersections.

articles.title: Residual of a finite group with respect to a class
articles.statement:
For a class $\mathfrak{F}$ of finite
groups and a finite group $G$, the $\mathfrak{F}$-residual $G^{\mathfrak{F}}$ is the intersection
of all normal subgroups $N$ of $G$ with $G/N \in \mathfrak{F}$.

For a formation containing the trivial group it is the smallest such $N$.

articles.title: Isomorphism-closed class of groups
articles.statement:
A class of groups $X$ is a property of groups that is
invariant under isomorphism: if a group $H$ belongs to $X$ and $K$ is a group isomorphic to $H$,
then $K$ belongs to $X$.

Infinite groups may belong to a class; apart from isomorphism invariance, the conditions imposed
on classes below concern only finite groups.

articles.title: Solubly saturated class
articles.statement:
A class of groups $X$ is solubly saturated (a composition class)
if, for every finite group $G$ with soluble radical $R$, whenever the Frattini subgroup $\Phi(R)$
of $R$ is normal in $G$ and $G/\Phi(R)$ belongs to $X$, the group $G$ belongs to $X$.

A formation with this property is a composition (solubly saturated, Baer-local) formation.

articles.title: Formation of finite groups
articles.statement:
A class of groups $X$ is a formation if it contains the trivial
group, for every finite group $G$ in $X$ and every normal subgroup $N$ of $G$ the quotient $G/N$
belongs to $X$, and for every finite group $G$ with normal subgroups $N_1, N_2$ such that
$G/N_1$ and $G/N_2$ belong to $X$, the quotient $G/(N_1 \cap N_2)$ belongs to $X$.

articles.title: Hereditary class of groups
articles.statement:
A class of groups $X$ is hereditary if every subgroup of a
finite group in $X$ belongs to $X$.

articles.title: Radical (Fitting) class
articles.statement:
A class of groups $X$ is radical if, for every finite group $G$,
every normal subgroup of $G$ belongs to $X$ whenever $G$ does, and whenever $N_1, N_2$ are normal
subgroups of $G$ that belong to $X$, their product $N_1 N_2$ belongs to $X$.

articles.title: Soluble radical
articles.statement:
A subgroup $R$ of a group $G$ is the soluble radical of $G$ if $R$ is a
soluble normal subgroup of $G$ that contains every soluble normal subgroup of $G$.

articles.title: Quotient lying in a class
articles.statement:
For a class of groups $X$, a group $G$ and a subgroup $N$ of $G$,
this holds when $N$ is normal in $G$ and the quotient group $G/N$ belongs to $X$.

articles.title: Radical hereditary formations need not be composition formations
articles.statement:
It is not true that every
radical hereditary formation of finite groups is a composition formation: some class of groups
that is a formation, a radical class and a hereditary class is not solubly saturated.

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Archive of Solved Problems, Problem 12.7 (A. F. Vasil'ev); resolution: S. F. Kamornikov, Math. Notes 55 (1994), no. 6, 586-588, Kourovka Archive, Problem 12.7: No, it is not.

articles.title: Kourovka Problem 12.7 (Vasil'ev)
articles.statement:
The statement that every radical hereditary formation of
finite groups is a composition formation: every class of groups that is a formation, a radical
class and a hereditary class is solubly saturated.

articles.title: Classes of finite groups
articles.statement:
A class of finite groups is a predicate on finite groups: it
assigns to every finite group $G$ a proposition, read as "$G$ belongs to the class". The class need
not be closed under isomorphism.

articles.title: The formation generated by a finite group can have infinitely many subformations
articles.statement:
There is
a finite group $G$ such that infinitely many formations are contained in the formation generated
by $G$. That is, the answer to Kourovka Problem 16.31 is negative, even for finite $G$.

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Archive of Solved Problems, Problem 16.31 (V. A. Vedernikov); resolution: V. P. Burichenko, J. Algebra 372 (2012), 428-458, Kourovka Archive, Problem 16.31 (No, not always, even for G finite).

articles.title: Kourovka Problem 16.31 for finite groups
articles.statement:
The statement (V. A. Vedernikov) that for every
finite group $G$ only finitely many formations of finite groups are contained in the formation
generated by $G$. Here formations may be empty, and a formation $\mathfrak{F}$ is contained in the
formation generated by $G$ when every finite group in $\mathfrak{F}$ belongs to the formation
generated by $G$.

articles.title: Formation generated by a finite group
Formations of finite groups, possibly empty
articles.statement:
A class $\mathfrak{F}$ of finite groups is a
formation if it is closed under homomorphic images (whenever $f \colon G \to H$ is a surjective
homomorphism of finite groups and $G \in \mathfrak{F}$, then $H \in \mathfrak{F}$) and under finite
subdirect products (whenever $N_1$ and $N_2$ are normal subgroups of a finite group $G$ with
$G / N_1 \in \mathfrak{F}$ and $G / N_2 \in \mathfrak{F}$, then
$G / (N_1 \cap N_2) \in \mathfrak{F}$). In particular the empty class is a formation.

articles.title: Kourovka Problem 16.82 has a negative answer
articles.statement:
For a class $\mathfrak{X}$ of finite groups,
let $\pi(\mathfrak{X})$ be the set of primes dividing the order of some group in $\mathfrak{X}$,
and for subgroup assignments $\tau_1, \tau_2$ write $\tau_1 \le \tau_2$ on $\mathfrak{X}$ when
$\tau_1(G) \subseteq \tau_2(G)$ for every $G \in \mathfrak{X}$. There is no class $\mathfrak{X}$ of
finite groups that contains at least one group, is closed under homomorphic images, subgroups and
direct products, contains a non-nilpotent group, and has the following property: every set of
closed subgroup functors on $\mathfrak{X}$ in which no two distinct members $\tau_1, \tau_2$
satisfy $\tau_1 \le \tau_2$ on $\mathfrak{X}$ has cardinality at most $|\pi(\mathfrak{X})|$. In
other words, for every such class the lattice $F(\mathfrak{X})$ of closed subgroup functors on
$\mathfrak{X}$ has width greater than $|\pi(\mathfrak{X})|$.

The Kourovka Archive answers 16.82 "No such classes exist", citing Kamornikov (2010).

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Archive of Solved Problems, Problem 16.82 (A. N. Skiba); resolution: S. F. Kamornikov, Siberian Math. J. 51 (2010), no. 5, 824-829, Kourovka Archive, Problem 16.82 (No such classes exist).

articles.title: Kourovka Problem 16.82 (Skiba)
articles.statement:
For a class $\mathfrak{X}$ of finite groups, let
$\pi(\mathfrak{X})$ be the set of primes dividing the order of some group in $\mathfrak{X}$, and
for subgroup assignments $\tau_1, \tau_2$ write $\tau_1 \le \tau_2$ on $\mathfrak{X}$ when
$\tau_1(G) \subseteq \tau_2(G)$ for every $G \in \mathfrak{X}$. There is a class $\mathfrak{X}$ of
finite groups that contains at least one group, is closed under homomorphic images, subgroups and
direct products, and contains a non-nilpotent group, such that the lattice $F(\mathfrak{X})$ of
closed subgroup functors on $\mathfrak{X}$ has width at most $|\pi(\mathfrak{X})|$: every set of
closed subgroup functors on $\mathfrak{X}$ in which no two distinct members $\tau_1, \tau_2$
satisfy $\tau_1 \le \tau_2$ on $\mathfrak{X}$ has cardinality at most $|\pi(\mathfrak{X})|$.

articles.title: Classes of finite groups (Kourovka 16.82 setting)
articles.statement:
A class $\mathfrak{X}$ of finite groups
is a predicate on finite groups $G$ (with carrier in the lowest type universe, together with their
group structure); the groups satisfying it are the members of the class, written
$G \in \mathfrak{X}$.

articles.title: Order on subgroup functors
articles.statement:
Let $\mathfrak{X}$ be a class of finite groups. For subgroup
assignments $\tau_1$ and $\tau_2$, $\tau_1 \le \tau_2$ on $\mathfrak{X}$ when
$\tau_1(G) \subseteq \tau_2(G)$ for every $G \in \mathfrak{X}$. This is the order of the lattice
$F(\mathfrak{X})$ of closed subgroup functors on $\mathfrak{X}$.

articles.title: Closed classes of finite groups
articles.statement:
A class $\mathfrak{X}$ of finite groups is closed when it
contains at least one group and is closed under homomorphic images, subgroups and direct products:
if $G \in \mathfrak{X}$ and $f : G \to H$ is a surjective homomorphism onto a finite group $H$,
then $H \in \mathfrak{X}$; every subgroup of a group in $\mathfrak{X}$ lies in $\mathfrak{X}$; and
if $G, H \in \mathfrak{X}$, then $G \times H \in \mathfrak{X}$.

articles.title: Closed subgroup functors
articles.statement:
Let $\mathfrak{X}$ be a class of finite groups. A subgroup
assignment $\tau$ is a closed subgroup functor on $\mathfrak{X}$ (A. N. Skiba) when the following
three conditions hold. For every $G \in \mathfrak{X}$, $G \in \tau(G)$. For every surjective
homomorphism $\varphi : A \to B$ with $A, B \in \mathfrak{X}$, $\varphi(H) \in \tau(B)$ for every
$H \in \tau(A)$ and $\varphi^{-1}(T) \in \tau(A)$ for every $T \in \tau(B)$. For every
$G \in \mathfrak{X}$, every $H \in \tau(G)$ and every $K \in \tau(H)$, the subgroup $K$, viewed as
a subgroup of $G$, lies in $\tau(G)$; that is, $\tau(H) \subseteq \tau(G)$.

articles.title: Prime divisors of a class of finite groups
articles.statement:
For a class $\mathfrak{X}$ of finite groups,
$\pi(\mathfrak{X})$ is the set of primes $p$ that divide the order of some group in
$\mathfrak{X}$.

articles.title: Subgroup assignments
articles.statement:
A subgroup assignment $\tau$ assigns to every finite group $G$ (with
carrier in the lowest type universe) a set $\tau(G)$ of subgroups of $G$.

articles.title: Kamornikov–Shemetkova theorem (Kourovka Problem 19.38)
articles.statement:
Let $H$ be a subgroup of a
finite soluble group $G$. Suppose that $H$ covers every Frattini chief factor $A/B$ of $G$, that
is, $A \le \langle H, B \rangle$ (which is $HB$, as $B$ is normal), and avoids every complemented
chief factor $A/B$ of $G$, that is, $H \cap A \le B$. Then there are $x, y \in G$ such that
$H \cap H^x \cap H^y = H_G$, where $H^x = xHx^{-1}$ and $H_G$ is the normal core of $H$, the
largest normal subgroup of $G$ contained in $H$.

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Problem 19.38 (S. F. Kamornikov); resolution: S. F. Kamornikov and O. L. Shemetkova, On a question concerning the intersection of Φ-isolators of finite soluble groups, J. Algebra 641 (2024), 1-8, doi:10.1016/j.jalgebra.2023.11.029, the Kourovka Notebook (21st issue) marks 19.38 solved: Yes, it is true, https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v49.

articles.title: Kourovka Problem 19.38
articles.statement:
The statement that for every finite soluble group $G$ and every
subgroup $H$ of $G$ that covers every Frattini chief factor $A/B$ of $G$, that is,
$A \le \langle H, B \rangle$ (which is $HB$, as $B$ is normal), and avoids every complemented
chief factor $A/B$ of $G$, that is, $H \cap A \le B$, there are $x, y \in G$ such that
$H \cap H^x \cap H^y = H_G$, where $H^x = xHx^{-1}$ and $H_G$ is the normal core of $H$, the
largest normal subgroup of $G$ contained in $H$.

articles.title: Complemented chief factor
articles.statement:
For subgroups $A$ and $B$ of a group $G$, $A/B$ is a
complemented chief factor of $G$ when $A/B$ is a chief factor of $G$ and some subgroup $M$ of $G$
satisfies $\langle M, A \rangle = G$ and $M \cap A = B$ (as $A$ is normal, the first condition
says $MA = G$).

articles.title: Frattini chief factor
articles.statement:
For subgroups $A$ and $B$ of a group $G$, $A/B$ is a Frattini chief
factor of $G$ when $A/B$ is a chief factor of $G$ and $A$ is contained in every maximal subgroup
of $G$ that contains $B$; equivalently, $A/B \le \Phi(G/B)$, where $\Phi$ denotes the Frattini
subgroup.

articles.title: Finite groups that are the product of every two non-conjugate maximal subgroups are soluble
articles.statement:
There is no finite group $G$ that is not soluble such that $G = MN$ for every two maximal
subgroups $M$ and $N$ of $G$ that are not conjugate in $G$; here $MN$ is the set of products $mn$
with $m \in M$ and $n \in N$. This answers Kourovka Problem 10.34 in the negative.

Sater (arXiv:2608.02970) and Li and Yang (arXiv:2608.19478) prove that a finite group with this
property is soluble (the almost simple case is due to Tikhonenko and Tyutyanov, 2010). The
Kourovka Notebook (21st issue) marks 10.34 solved, "No, there are no such groups".

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Problem 10.34 (V. S. Monakhov); resolution: R. Sater, Finite groups that are the product of every pair of non-conjugate maximal subgroups are soluble, arXiv:2608.02970 (2026); J. Li and Y. Yang, Products of nonconjugate maximal subgroups, arXiv:2608.19478 (2026), main theorems: a finite group with MN = G for all non-conjugate maximal subgroups M, N is soluble; the Kourovka Notebook (21st issue) marks 10.34 solved, https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.19478.

articles.title: Non-soluble products of non-conjugate maximal subgroups (Kourovka 10.34, Monakhov)
articles.statement:
The
statement that there is a finite group $G$ that is not soluble such that $G = MN$ for every two
maximal subgroups $M$ and $N$ of $G$ that are not conjugate in $G$. Here $MN$ is the set of
products $mn$ with $m \in M$ and $n \in N$.

articles.title: Minimal non-nilpotent subgroup
articles.statement:
A subgroup $M$ of a group $G$ is minimal non-nilpotent if
$M$ is not nilpotent but every proper subgroup of $M$ is nilpotent.

articles.title: $\mathbb{P}$-subnormal subgroup
articles.statement:
A subgroup $H$ of a group $G$ is $\mathbb{P}$-subnormal in
$G$ when $H = G$ or there is a chain of subgroups $H = H_0 < H_1 < \cdots < H_n = G$ in which every
index $|H_i : H_{i-1}|$ is a prime number.

articles.title: Schmidt subgroup
articles.statement:
A subgroup $H$ of a group $G$ is a Schmidt subgroup when $H$ is not
nilpotent but every proper subgroup of $H$ is nilpotent.

Finiteness of $H$ is not part of this definition.

articles.title: Permutability with minimal non-nilpotent subgroups does not force a nilpotent core quotient
articles.statement:
There exist a finite group $G$ and a subgroup $H$ of $G$ with $HM = MH$ (as sets of products) for
every minimal non-nilpotent subgroup $M$ of $G$ such that the quotient $H/H_G$ is not nilpotent,
where the normal core $H_G$ is the largest normal subgroup of $G$ contained in $H$.

This answers Kourovka Problem 17.56 in the negative (Ballester-Bolinches, Esteban-Romero,
Kamornikov and Pérez-Calabuig, 2022).

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Problem 17.56 (V. N. Knyagina, V. S. Monakhov); resolution: A. Ballester-Bolinches, R. Esteban-Romero, S. F. Kamornikov and V. Pérez-Calabuig, J. Algebra 608 (2022), 382-387, the Kourovka Notebook (21st issue) marks 17.56 solved (No, not always).

articles.title: Subgroups permuting with all minimal non-nilpotent subgroups (Kourovka 17.56)
articles.statement:
The
statement that if $H$ is a subgroup of a finite group $G$ with $HM = MH$ (as sets of products) for
every minimal non-nilpotent subgroup $M$ of $G$, then the quotient $H/H_G$ is nilpotent, where the
normal core $H_G$ is the largest normal subgroup of $G$ contained in $H$.

The question is due to V. N. Knyagina and V. S. Monakhov.

articles.title: Finite groups with $\sigma$-subnormal Schmidt subgroups are $\sigma$-nilpotent-by-cyclic
articles.statement:
Let
$\sigma$ be a partition of the set of all primes into nonempty pairwise disjoint blocks, and let $G$
be a finite group in which every Schmidt subgroup is $\sigma$-subnormal. Then $G$ has a normal
$\sigma$-nilpotent subgroup $N$ such that $G / N$ is cyclic: there is $g \in G$ such that every
$x \in G$ satisfies $x g^{-k} \in N$ for some integer $k$. This answers Kourovka Notebook
Problem 19.85 in the affirmative.

Yi and Kamornikov prove that $G / F_\sigma(G)$ is cyclic, where $F_\sigma(G)$ is the largest normal
$\sigma$-nilpotent subgroup of $G$; for nilpotent $G$ one takes $N = G$. The case of the partition
of the primes into single primes was known before.

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Archive of Solved Problems, Problem 19.85 (A. N. Skiba); resolution: X. Yi and S. F. Kamornikov, Finite groups with σ-subnormal Schmidt subgroups, J. Algebra 560 (2020), 181-191, main result, quoted as Lemma 8 (reference [11]) in A. Ballester-Bolinches, S. F. Kamornikov and X. Yi, Finite groups with σ-subnormal Schmidt subgroups, Bull. Malays. Math. Sci. Soc. (2022): if every Schmidt subgroup of a non-nilpotent group G is σ-subnormal, then G / F_σ(G) is cyclic, F_σ(G) the largest normal σ-nilpotent subgroup; Kourovka Archive, Problem 19.85: Yes, it is true, https://doi.org/10.1007/s40840-022-01369-y.

articles.title: Claim of Kourovka Problem 19.85
articles.statement:
The statement that for every partition $\sigma$ of the set
of all primes into nonempty pairwise disjoint blocks and every finite group $G$ in which every
Schmidt subgroup is $\sigma$-subnormal, $G$ has a normal $\sigma$-nilpotent subgroup $N$ such that
$G / N$ is cyclic: there is $g \in G$ such that every $x \in G$ satisfies $x g^{-k} \in N$ for some
integer $k$. The problem is due to A. N. Skiba.

articles.title: Finite groups with $\mathbb{P}$-subnormal Schmidt subgroups are soluble
articles.statement:
Every finite group in
which every Schmidt subgroup is $\mathbb{P}$-subnormal is soluble. This answers Kourovka Notebook
Problem 18.30 in the affirmative.

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Archive of Solved Problems, Problem 18.30 (A. F. Vasil'ev, T. I. Vasil'eva, V. N. Tyutyanov); resolution: V. N. Tyutyanov, Probl. Fiz. Mat. Tekhn. 2015, no. 1 (22), 88-91 (Russian), Kourovka Archive, Problem 18.30: Yes, it must, https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v49.

articles.title: Claim of Kourovka Problem 18.30
articles.statement:
The statement that every finite group in which every
Schmidt subgroup is $\mathbb{P}$-subnormal is soluble. The problem is due to A. F. Vasil'ev,
T. I. Vasil'eva and V. N. Tyutyanov.

articles.title: Groups of Fitting height at most $h$
articles.statement:
For a natural number $h$, a group $G$ has Fitting
height (nilpotent length) at most $h$ if there are normal subgroups
$1 = G_0 \le G_1 \le \cdots \le G_h = G$ of $G$ such that for every $i < h$ some term of the lower
central series of $G_{i+1}$ lies in $G_i$, that is, $G_{i+1} / G_i$ is nilpotent.

articles.title: Chief factors
articles.statement:
For subgroups $A$ and $B$ of a group $G$, $A / B$ is a chief factor of $G$
if $A$ and $B$ are normal in $G$, $B < A$, and every normal subgroup $N$ of $G$ with
$B \le N \le A$ equals $B$ or $A$.

articles.title: Composition factors via subnormal subgroups
articles.statement:
A group $S$ is a composition factor of a group
$K$ if $S$ is simple and some subnormal subgroup $H$ of $K$ has a surjective homomorphism onto $S$.

For finite $K$ this is the same as $S$ occurring as a factor of a composition series of $K$
(refine the subnormal chain through the kernel).

articles.title: Conjugacy separable groups
articles.statement:
A group $G$ is conjugacy separable if any two elements
$x, y \in G$ whose images are conjugate in every quotient $G / N$ by a normal subgroup $N$ of
finite index (that is, $g x g^{-1} y^{-1} \in N$ for some $g \in G$) are conjugate in $G$.

articles.title: Partitions of the primes
articles.statement:
A family $\sigma = (\sigma_i)_{i \in I}$ of sets of natural
numbers is a partition of the primes if every $\sigma_i$ is a nonempty set of primes, $\sigma_i$
and $\sigma_j$ are disjoint whenever $i \ne j$, and every prime lies in some $\sigma_i$.

articles.title: Residually finite $p$-groups
articles.statement:
For a natural number $p$, a group $G$ is residually a finite
$p$-group if every element $g \ne 1$ of $G$ lies outside some normal subgroup of $G$ whose index
is $p^k$ for some $k \ge 0$, where an infinite index counts as $0$.

This notion appears in Kourovka Notebook problems 1.84, 4.52 and 10.30.

articles.title: $\sigma$-nilpotent groups
articles.statement:
For a family $\sigma = (\sigma_i)_{i \in I}$ of sets of natural
numbers, a group $G$ is $\sigma$-nilpotent if it is the internal direct product of finitely many
normal subgroups $H_1, \dots, H_t$ whose orders are $\sigma$-primary (the order of an infinite
subgroup counts as $0$): the $H_k$ generate $G$, and each $H_k$ meets the subgroup generated by
the others trivially.

articles.title: $\sigma$-primary numbers
articles.statement:
For a family $\sigma = (\sigma_i)_{i \in I}$ of sets of natural
numbers, a natural number $n$ is $\sigma$-primary if there is an index $i$ such that every prime
divisor of $n$ lies in $\sigma_i$. For $n = 0$ this means that some $\sigma_i$ contains every
prime.

A finite group is called $\sigma$-primary when its order is.

articles.title: $\sigma$-soluble groups
articles.statement:
For a family $\sigma = (\sigma_i)_{i \in I}$ of sets of natural
numbers, a group $G$ is $\sigma$-soluble if for every chief factor $A / B$ of $G$ the index
$|A : B|$ is $\sigma$-primary (an infinite index counts as $0$).

articles.title: $\sigma$-subnormal subgroups
articles.statement:
For a family $\sigma = (\sigma_i)_{i \in I}$ of sets of
natural numbers, a subgroup $A$ of a group $G$ is $\sigma$-subnormal in $G$ if there is a chain of
subgroups $A = A_0 \le A_1 \le \cdots \le A_n = G$ such that for every $i < n$ either $A_i$ is
normal in $A_{i+1}$, or the index in $A_{i+1}$ of the normal core of $A_i$ in $A_{i+1}$ is
$\sigma$-primary (an infinite index counts as $0$).

articles.title: Restricted wreath product
articles.statement:
For groups $A$ and $B$, let $A \wr_r B = A^B \rtimes B$ be the
regular (unrestricted) wreath product, where $A^B$ is the group of all functions $f : B \to A$ and
$b \in B$ acts on it by $(b \cdot f)(x) = f(b^{-1} x)$. The restricted wreath product $A \wr B$ is
the subgroup of $A \wr_r B$ generated by the elements $(f, b)$ whose function part $f$ has finite
support, that is, $f(x) \ne 1$ for only finitely many $x \in B$.

These elements already form a subgroup, and for finite $B$ it is all of $A \wr_r B$.

articles.title: A counterexample to Skiba's $\sigma$-subnormality question
articles.statement:
The statement of Kourovka
Problem 19.84 is false: there are a partition $\sigma$ of the set of primes, a finite group $G$
and a subgroup $A$ of $G$ such that $A$ is $\sigma$-subnormal in the subgroup
$\langle A, A^x \rangle$ generated by $A$ and $A^x = xAx^{-1}$ for every $x \in G$, but $A$ is
not $\sigma$-subnormal in $G$.

Tyutyanov's example is $G = S_5$, a partition with blocks $\{2, 3\}$ and $\{5\}$, and
$A = \langle (1\,2) \rangle$. Wielandt's theorem gives the affirmative answer for the partition
into single primes.

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Archive of Solved Problems, Problem 19.84 (A. N. Skiba); resolution: V. N. Tyutyanov, letter of 28 August 2019, Kourovka Archive, Problem 19.84: No, not always; in G = S₅ with σ = {2, 3} ∪ {5} the subgroup A = ⟨(12)⟩ is σ-subnormal in ⟨A, A^x⟩ for every x but not σ-subnormal in G, https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v49.

articles.title: Skiba's $\sigma$-subnormality question (Kourovka 19.84)
articles.statement:
The statement that for every
partition $\sigma$ of the set of primes, every finite group $G$ and every subgroup $A$ of $G$, if
$A$ is $\sigma$-subnormal in the subgroup $\langle A, A^x \rangle$ generated by $A$ and
$A^x = xAx^{-1}$ for every $x \in G$, then $A$ is $\sigma$-subnormal in $G$.

articles.title: Supersoluble group (Kourovka 15.81)
articles.statement:
A group $G$ is supersoluble when it has a series
$1 = H_0 \le H_1 \le \cdots \le H_n = G$ of subgroups, each normal in $G$, such that every factor
$H_{i+1}/H_i$ is cyclic.

articles.title: Finite non-supersoluble groups have uncomplemented maximal subgroups of Sylow subgroups
articles.statement:
For
every finite group $G$ that is not supersoluble, there are a prime $p$ and a non-cyclic Sylow
$p$-subgroup $P$ of $G$ with a maximal subgroup $M$ of $P$ that has no proper complement in $G$:
there is no subgroup $K \ne G$ with $MK = G$ and $M \cap K = 1$. This answers Kourovka
Problem 15.81 in the affirmative.

The Kourovka Archive answers 15.81 "Yes, it is" (Wang and Wei).

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Archive of Solved Problems, Problem 15.81 (A. N. Skiba); resolution: Wang Yanming and Wei Huaquan, Sci. China Ser. A 47 (2004), no. 1, 96-103, Kourovka Archive, Problem 15.81 (answer: Yes, it is).

articles.title: Uncomplemented maximal subgroups of Sylow subgroups (Kourovka 15.81, Skiba)
articles.statement:
The statement
that every finite group $G$ that is not supersoluble has, for some prime $p$, a non-cyclic Sylow
$p$-subgroup $P$ with a maximal subgroup $M$ of $P$ that has no proper complement in $G$, that is,
there is no subgroup $K \ne G$ with $MK = G$ and $M \cap K = 1$.

articles.title: Moretó: every non-abelian simple group occurs in Kourovka 19.55(a)
articles.statement:
For every finite
non-abelian simple group $S$ there is a finite group $G$ such that $S$ is a composition factor of
$G$ and every maximal subgroup $M$ of $G$ with $\pi(M) = \pi(G)$ is supersoluble, where $\pi(X)$ is
the set of primes dividing the order of $X$.

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Archive of Solved Problems, Problem 19.55 (V. S. Monakhov); resolution: A. Moretó, Finite groups whose maximal subgroups of order divisible by all the primes are supersolvable, Monatsh. Math. 195 (2021), no. 3, 497-500 (arXiv:2010.04808), Theorem A (every nonabelian simple group occurs as a composition factor), Theorem B (solvable examples of arbitrarily large nilpotency length and rank) and Theorem C (the p-length is 1 for every prime divisor p of |G|); Kourovka Archive, Problem 19.55, https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.04808.

articles.title: Kourovka 19.55(a) (Monakhov): every non-abelian simple group occurs
articles.statement:
The proposition that
for every finite non-abelian simple group $S$ there is a finite group $G$ such that $S$ is a
composition factor of $G$ and every maximal subgroup $M$ of $G$ with $\pi(M) = \pi(G)$ is
supersoluble, where $\pi(X)$ is the set of primes dividing the order of $X$.

articles.title: Moretó: soluble groups in Kourovka 19.55 have unbounded Fitting height
articles.statement:
For every natural
number $h$ there is a finite soluble group $G$ whose Fitting height is greater than $h$ and in
which every maximal subgroup $M$ with $\pi(M) = \pi(G)$ is supersoluble, where $\pi(X)$ is the set
of primes dividing the order of $X$.

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Archive of Solved Problems, Problem 19.55 (V. S. Monakhov); resolution: A. Moretó, Finite groups whose maximal subgroups of order divisible by all the primes are supersolvable, Monatsh. Math. 195 (2021), no. 3, 497-500 (arXiv:2010.04808), Theorem A (every nonabelian simple group occurs as a composition factor), Theorem B (solvable examples of arbitrarily large nilpotency length and rank) and Theorem C (the p-length is 1 for every prime divisor p of |G|); Kourovka Archive, Problem 19.55, https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.04808.

articles.title: Kourovka 19.55(b) (Monakhov): unbounded Fitting height
articles.statement:
The proposition that for every
natural number $h$ there is a finite soluble group $G$ whose Fitting height is greater than $h$ and
in which every maximal subgroup $M$ with $\pi(M) = \pi(G)$ is supersoluble, where $\pi(X)$ is the
set of primes dividing the order of $X$.

articles.title: Chief factor of rank above a bound
articles.statement:
A group $G$ has a chief factor of rank greater than a
natural number $r$ when there are a chief factor $A / B$ of $G$, a prime $p$ and a natural number
$k > r$ such that the index $[A : B]$ equals $p^k$.

A chief factor of a finite soluble group is an elementary abelian $p$-group, of rank $k$ when its
order is $p^k$.

articles.title: Supersoluble group (generator form)
articles.statement:
A group $G$ is supersoluble when there are a natural
number $n$ and elements $g_0, \dots, g_{n-1}$ of $G$ that generate $G$ such that, for every
$i \le n$, the subgroup $G_i = \langle g_j : j < i \rangle$ is normal in $G$.

Then $1 = G_0 \le \dots \le G_n = G$ is a normal series with cyclic factors
$G_{i+1} / G_i = \langle G_i, g_i \rangle / G_i$.

articles.title: Monakhov's condition
articles.statement:
A group $G$ satisfies Monakhov's condition when every maximal
subgroup $M$ of $G$ with $\pi(M) = \pi(G)$ is supersoluble, where $\pi(X)$ is the set of prime
factors of the order of $X$ if $X$ is finite, and is empty if $X$ is infinite.

articles.title: Moretó: soluble groups in Kourovka 19.55 have p-length at most one
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite
soluble group in which every maximal subgroup $H$ with $\pi(H) = \pi(G)$ is supersoluble, where
$\pi(X)$ is the set of primes dividing the order of $X$. Then for every prime $p$ the group $G$ has
$p$-length at most $1$: there are normal subgroups $N \le M$ of $G$ such that $p$ does not divide
$|N|$, the index $[M : N]$ is a power of $p$, and $p$ does not divide $[G : M]$.

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Archive of Solved Problems, Problem 19.55 (V. S. Monakhov); resolution: A. Moretó, Finite groups whose maximal subgroups of order divisible by all the primes are supersolvable, Monatsh. Math. 195 (2021), no. 3, 497-500 (arXiv:2010.04808), Theorem A (every nonabelian simple group occurs as a composition factor), Theorem B (solvable examples of arbitrarily large nilpotency length and rank) and Theorem C (the p-length is 1 for every prime divisor p of |G|); Kourovka Archive, Problem 19.55, https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.04808.

articles.title: Kourovka 19.55(b) (Monakhov): p-length at most one
articles.statement:
The proposition that for every finite
soluble group $G$ in which every maximal subgroup $H$ with $\pi(H) = \pi(G)$ is supersoluble,
where $\pi(X)$ is the set of primes dividing the order of $X$, and for every prime $p$, the group
$G$ has $p$-length at most $1$: there are normal subgroups $N \le M$ of $G$ such that $p$ does not
divide $|N|$, the index $[M : N]$ is a power of $p$, and $p$ does not divide $[G : M]$.

articles.title: Groups of p-length at most one
articles.statement:
For a natural number $p$, a group $G$ has $p$-length at
most $1$ when there are normal subgroups $N \le M$ of $G$ such that $N$ is finite of order not
divisible by $p$, the index $[M : N]$ equals $p^k$ for some natural number $k$ (an infinite index
counting as $0$), and the index $[G : M]$ is finite and not divisible by $p$.

For finite $G$ and prime $p$ this says that $N$ is a $p'$-group, $M / N$ is a $p$-group and $G / M$
is a $p'$-group.

articles.title: Unbounded chief-factor rank under Monakhov's condition
articles.statement:
For every natural number $r$ there is
a finite soluble group $G$ such that every maximal subgroup $M$ of $G$ with $\pi(M) = \pi(G)$ is
supersoluble, where $\pi(X)$ is the set of prime divisors of $|X|$, and $G$ has a chief factor
$A/B$ (normal subgroups $B < A$ of $G$ with no normal subgroup of $G$ strictly between them) of
order $p^k$ for some prime $p$ and some $k > r$.

Moretó's groups $G_n = V_1 \cdots V_n$ (Theorem B and its proof) are such examples: their minimal
normal subgroup $V_n$, an elementary abelian chief factor, has rank tending to infinity; the
Kourovka Archive records "there is not any bound for ... the rank".

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Archive of Solved Problems, Problem 19.55 (V. S. Monakhov); resolution: A. Moretó, Finite groups whose maximal subgroups of order divisible by all the primes are supersolvable, Monatsh. Math. 195 (2021), no. 3, 497-500 (arXiv:2010.04808), Theorem A (every nonabelian simple group occurs as a composition factor), Theorem B (solvable examples of arbitrarily large nilpotency length and rank) and Theorem C (the p-length is 1 for every prime divisor p of |G|); Kourovka Archive, Problem 19.55, https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.04808.

articles.title: Unbounded chief-factor rank under Monakhov's condition (the claim)
articles.statement:
The statement that for
every natural number $r$ there is a finite soluble group $G$ satisfying Monakhov's condition
(every maximal subgroup $M$ of $G$ with $\pi(M) = \pi(G)$ is supersoluble, where $\pi(X)$ is the
set of prime divisors of $|X|$) that has a chief factor $A/B$ of order $p^k$ for some prime $p$
and some $k > r$. This is the answer to Kourovka 19.55(b) for the rank.

articles.title: $p$-soluble groups (series with $p$- and $p'$-factors)
articles.statement:
A group $G$ is $p$-soluble when
it has a chain of subgroups $1 = H_0 \le H_1 \le \cdots \le H_n = G$, each normal in the next,
such that for every $i < n$ the relative index $|H_{i+1} : H_i|$ (taken to be $0$ when it is
infinite) is a power of $p$ or is coprime to $p$. For a finite group this says that every factor
$H_{i+1}/H_i$ is a $p$-group or a $p'$-group.

articles.title: σ-nilpotent supplements to the maximal subgroups of Sylow subgroups (Kourovka 19.88)
articles.statement:
Let
$\sigma$ be a partition of the set of all primes and let $G$ be a finite group. If for every prime
$p$, every Sylow $p$-subgroup $P$ of $G$ and every maximal subgroup $V$ of $P$ there is a
$\sigma$-nilpotent subgroup $T$ of $G$ with $VT = G$, that is, every element of $G$ is a product
$vt$ with $v \in V$ and $t \in T$, then $G$ is $\sigma$-nilpotent. Here a partition of the primes is
a family of nonempty, pairwise disjoint sets of primes whose union is the set of all primes, and a
group is $\sigma$-nilpotent when it is the internal direct product of finitely many normal
subgroups, each of whose order has all its prime divisors in a single block of $\sigma$.

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Archive of Solved Problems, Problem 19.88 (A. N. Skiba); resolution: A.-M. Liu, W. Guo, I. N. Safonova and A. N. Skiba, G-covering subgroup systems for some classes of σ-soluble groups, J. Algebra 585 (2021), 280-293; another solution using CFSG by S. F. Kamornikov and V. N. Tyutyanov, Trudy Inst. Mat. Mekh. UrO RAN 27 (2021), no. 1, 98-102, abstract: a set of subgroups of G containing a supplement to each maximal subgroup of every Sylow subgroup of G is a G-covering subgroup system for the classes of σ-soluble and of σ-nilpotent groups, which answers 19.87 and 19.88; Kourovka Archive, Problem 19.88: Yes, it is true, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jalgebra.2021.06.010.

articles.title: Kourovka Problem 19.88 (statement)
articles.statement:
The statement that for every partition $\sigma$ of the
set of all primes and every finite group $G$: if for every prime $p$, every Sylow $p$-subgroup $P$
of $G$ and every maximal subgroup $V$ of $P$ there is a $\sigma$-nilpotent subgroup $T$ of $G$ with
$VT = G$, that is, every element of $G$ is a product $vt$ with $v \in V$ and $t \in T$, then $G$ is
$\sigma$-nilpotent. Here a partition of the primes is a family of nonempty, pairwise disjoint sets
of primes whose union is the set of all primes, and a group is $\sigma$-nilpotent when it is the
internal direct product of finitely many normal subgroups, each of whose order has all its prime
divisors in a single block of $\sigma$.

articles.title: σ-soluble supplements to the maximal subgroups of Sylow subgroups (Kourovka 19.87)
articles.statement:
Let $\sigma$
be a partition of the set of all primes and let $G$ be a finite group. If for every prime $p$, every
Sylow $p$-subgroup $P$ of $G$ and every maximal subgroup $V$ of $P$ there is a $\sigma$-soluble
subgroup $T$ of $G$ with $VT = G$, that is, every element of $G$ is a product $vt$ with $v \in V$
and $t \in T$, then $G$ is $\sigma$-soluble. Here a partition of the primes is a family of nonempty,
pairwise disjoint sets of primes whose union is the set of all primes, and a group is
$\sigma$-soluble when for every chief factor $A/B$ of it (normal subgroups $B < A$ with no normal
subgroup strictly between them) all prime divisors of the index $|A : B|$ lie in a single block of
$\sigma$.

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Archive of Solved Problems, Problem 19.87 (A. N. Skiba); resolution: A.-M. Liu, W. Guo, I. N. Safonova and A. N. Skiba, G-covering subgroup systems for some classes of σ-soluble groups, J. Algebra 585 (2021), 280-293; another solution using CFSG by S. F. Kamornikov and V. N. Tyutyanov, Trudy Inst. Mat. Mekh. UrO RAN 27 (2021), no. 1, 98-102, abstract: a set of subgroups of G containing a supplement to each maximal subgroup of every Sylow subgroup of G is a G-covering subgroup system for the classes of σ-soluble and of σ-nilpotent groups, which answers 19.87 and 19.88; Kourovka Archive, Problem 19.87: Yes, it is true, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jalgebra.2021.06.010.

articles.title: Kourovka Problem 19.87 (statement)
articles.statement:
The statement that for every partition $\sigma$ of the
set of all primes and every finite group $G$: if for every prime $p$, every Sylow $p$-subgroup $P$
of $G$ and every maximal subgroup $V$ of $P$ there is a $\sigma$-soluble subgroup $T$ of $G$ with
$VT = G$, that is, every element of $G$ is a product $vt$ with $v \in V$ and $t \in T$, then $G$ is
$\sigma$-soluble. Here a partition of the primes is a family of nonempty, pairwise disjoint sets of
primes whose union is the set of all primes, and a group is $\sigma$-soluble when for every chief
factor $A/B$ of it (normal subgroups $B < A$ with no normal subgroup strictly between them) all
prime divisors of the index $|A : B|$ lie in a single block of $\sigma$.

articles.title: $p$-soluble supplements of maximal subgroups of a Sylow subgroup force $p$-solubility
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime, $G$ a finite group whose order is divisible by $p$, and $P$ a Sylow
$p$-subgroup of $G$. If every maximal subgroup $M$ of $P$ has a $p$-soluble supplement in $G$,
that is, a $p$-soluble subgroup $K$ of $G$ with $MK = G$, then $G$ is $p$-soluble.

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Archive of Solved Problems, Problem 17.111 (A. N. Skiba); resolution: GuoHua Qian, Science China Math. 56 (2013), 1015-1018, Kourovka Archive, Problem 17.111 (Yes, it must).

articles.title: Kourovka Problem 17.111 (supplements of maximal subgroups of Sylow subgroups)
articles.statement:
The
statement, asked by A. N. Skiba, that for every prime $p$, every finite group $G$ whose order is
divisible by $p$ and every Sylow $p$-subgroup $P$ of $G$, if every maximal subgroup $M$ of $P$ has
a $p$-soluble supplement in $G$, that is, a $p$-soluble subgroup $K$ of $G$ with $MK = G$, then
$G$ is $p$-soluble.

articles.title: Smirnov's negative answer to Kourovka Problem 11.93
articles.statement:
The block lattices of finite groups do
not generate the variety of all lattices: there are lattice terms $p$ and $q$ such that $p$ and $q$
take the same value in the block lattice of every finite group $G$ under every assignment of blocks
of $G$ to the variables, but take different values in some lattice $L$ under some assignment of
elements of $L$ to the variables. Here the blocks of $G$ are the cosets of normal subgroups of $G$
and the empty set, and the block lattice of $G$ is the set of blocks ordered by inclusion.

Smirnov shows that the variety generated by the block lattices of groups does not contain all
finite lattices: for each element $g$ of a group $G$, the filter of blocks containing $g$ is a
modular, even arguesian, lattice.

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Archive of Solved Problems, Problem 11.93 (D. M. Smirnov); resolution: D. M. Smirnov, Siberian Math. J. 33, no. 4 (1992), 663-668, Kourovka Archive, Problem 11.93: "No, it is not"; Archive 9.62: the variety generated by the block lattices of groups does not contain all finite lattices, https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v49.

articles.title: Kourovka Problem 11.93: do block lattices generate all lattices?
articles.statement:
**Kourovka Problem 11.93: do block lattices generate all lattices?** The proposition, asked by
D. M. Smirnov, that the block lattices of finite groups generate the variety of all lattices. Here
the blocks of a group $G$ are the cosets of normal subgroups of $G$ and the empty set; ordered by
inclusion they form the block lattice of $G$, whose meet is intersection and whose join of two
blocks is the intersection of all blocks containing their union. Formally, the proposition states:
for all lattice terms $p$ and $q$, if $p$ and $q$ take the same value in the block lattice of every
finite group $G$ under every assignment of blocks of $G$ to the variables, then $p$ and $q$ take
the same value in every lattice $L$ under every assignment of elements of $L$ to the variables.

By Birkhoff's theorem this is equivalent to the variety generated by these block lattices being
the variety of all lattices.

articles.title: Join in the block lattice
articles.statement:
For subsets $X$ and $Y$ of a group $G$, their block join is the
intersection of all blocks of $G$ that contain $X \cup Y$. Since blocks are closed under
intersections and $G$ itself is a block, this is the smallest block containing $X \cup Y$; for
blocks $X$ and $Y$ it is their join in the block lattice of $G$.

articles.title: Evaluation of lattice terms in the block lattice
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a group and $v$ an assignment
of a subset $v(n)$ of $G$ to each variable $x_n$. The value of a lattice term under $v$ is defined
by recursion on the term: the variable $x_n$ has value $v(n)$, a meet $s \wedge t$ has as value
the intersection of the values of $s$ and $t$, and a join $s \vee t$ has as value the block join of
the values of $s$ and $t$, the intersection of all blocks of $G$ containing their union. When
every $v(n)$ is a block, this is the value of the term in the block lattice of $G$.

articles.title: Evaluation of lattice terms
articles.statement:
Let $L$ be a lattice and $v$ an assignment of an element
$v(n)$ of $L$ to each variable $x_n$. The value of a lattice term under $v$ is defined by
recursion on the term: the variable $x_n$ has value $v(n)$, and a join $s \vee t$ or meet
$s \wedge t$ has as value the join or meet in $L$ of the values of $s$ and $t$.

articles.title: Blocks of a group
articles.statement:
A subset $X$ of a group $G$ is a block if it is empty or a coset $gN$
of a normal subgroup $N$ of $G$ (Kourovka Notebook, Archive 9.62). Ordered by inclusion, the
blocks of $G$ form the block lattice $C(G)$.

articles.title: Lattice terms
articles.statement:
Lattice terms in the variables $x_0, x_1, x_2, \dots$ are built
inductively: each variable $x_n$ is a term, and for terms $s$ and $t$ their join $s \vee t$ and
their meet $s \wedge t$ are terms.

articles.title: Isomorphic simple maximal subgroups need not be conjugate under automorphisms
articles.statement:
There are a
finite simple group $G$ and isomorphic maximal subgroups $X$ and $Y$ of $G$, both simple groups,
such that no automorphism $\varphi$ of $G$ satisfies $\varphi(X) = Y$. That is, the answer to
Kourovka Problem 18.115 is negative.

The Kourovka Archive answers 18.115 "No, not always": there are two $\operatorname{Aut} G$-classes
of $M_{12}$ in $E_6(5)$ (Kleidman–Wilson, 1990), and Craven (2023) found two classes of
$\mathrm{PSL}_2(11)$ and two of $\mathrm{PSL}_2(19)$ in $E_6(q)$ for certain $q$.

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Archive of Solved Problems, Problem 18.115 (P. Schmid); resolution: P. B. Kleidman and R. A. Wilson, J. London Math. Soc. (2) 42 (1990), 555-561; D. A. Craven, Invent. Math. 234 (2023), no. 2, 637-719, Kourovka Archive, Problem 18.115: No, not always; two Aut G-classes of M_12 in E_6(5) (Kleidman-Wilson), and two classes of PSL_2(11) and of PSL_2(19) in E_6(q) for certain q (Craven), https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v49.

articles.title: Schmid's question on isomorphic simple maximal subgroups (Kourovka 18.115)
articles.statement:
The statement
that in every finite simple group $G$, any two isomorphic maximal subgroups $X$ and $Y$ that are
themselves simple groups are conjugate in $\operatorname{Aut} G$, that is, $\varphi(X) = Y$ for
some automorphism $\varphi$ of $G$.

articles.title: Fully invariant subgroups of every order do not force cyclicity
articles.statement:
Not every finite group $G$
having, for every divisor $d$ of $|G|$, a fully invariant subgroup of order $d$ (a subgroup $H$
with $\varphi(H) \le H$ for every endomorphism $\varphi$ of $G$) is cyclic.

The Kourovka Archive answers 16.61 "No" (Abdollahi): take $G = C_p \times C_{p^2}$, where $C_p$
and $C_{p^2}$ are cyclic $p$-groups of orders $p$ and $p^2$.

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Archive of Solved Problems, Problem 16.61 (D. MacHale); resolution: A. Abdollahi, letter of 4 March 2009, as recorded in the Kourovka Archive, Kourovka Archive, Problem 16.61 (No: G = C_p × C_{p²}).

articles.title: MacHale's question on fully invariant subgroups (Kourovka 16.61)
articles.statement:
The statement that every
finite group $G$ having, for every divisor $d$ of $|G|$, a fully invariant subgroup of order $d$
(a subgroup $H$ with $\varphi(H) \le H$ for every endomorphism $\varphi$ of $G$) is cyclic.

articles.title: A group isomorphic to its nontrivial normal subgroups need not be free of infinite rank, simple or infinite cyclic
articles.statement:
**A group isomorphic to its nontrivial normal subgroups need not be free of infinite rank, simple
or infinite cyclic.** There is a nontrivial group $G$ that is isomorphic to each of its nontrivial
normal subgroups and is neither free of infinite rank (isomorphic to the free group on an infinite
set), nor simple, nor infinite cyclic. That is, the answer to Kourovka Problem 12.45 is negative
(V. N. Obraztsov, 1997).

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Archive of Solved Problems, Problem 12.45 (P. Hall; J. C. Lennox); resolution: V. N. Obraztsov, Proc. London Math. Soc. (3) 75 (1997), 79-98, Kourovka Archive, Problem 12.45: No.

articles.title: Hall's question on groups isomorphic to their nontrivial normal subgroups (Kourovka 12.45)
articles.statement:
The statement that every nontrivial group that is isomorphic to each of its nontrivial normal
subgroups is free of infinite rank (isomorphic to the free group on an infinite set), simple, or
infinite cyclic.

articles.title: Normal subgroups of $K$-groups need not be $K$-groups
articles.statement:
There is a group $G$ whose subgroup
lattice is complemented (a $K$-group) with a normal subgroup $N$ whose own subgroup lattice is not
complemented; so Kourovka Problem 11.128 has a negative answer.

The Kourovka Archive answers 11.128 "No, it is not" (Obraztsov).

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Archive of Solved Problems, Problem 11.128 (M. Emaldi); resolution: V. N. Obraztsov, J. Austral. Math. Soc. (Ser. A) 61, no. 2 (1996), 267-288, Kourovka Archive, Problem 11.128: "No, it is not", https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v49.

articles.title: Kourovka Problem 11.128 on normal subgroups of $K$-groups
articles.statement:
Call a group $G$ a $K$-group
when its subgroup lattice is complemented: every subgroup $A$ of $G$ has a subgroup $B$ with
$A \cap B = 1$ and $\langle A, B \rangle = G$. This is the assertion (M. Emaldi) that every normal
subgroup of a $K$-group, viewed as a group in its own right, is again a $K$-group.

articles.title: Not every finitely generated group with three maximal subgroups is finite
articles.statement:
There is a
finitely generated infinite group with exactly three maximal subgroups; that is, it is false that
every finitely generated group with exactly three maximal subgroups is finite.

This answers Kourovka Problem 17.17 (G. M. Bergman) in the negative: the Kourovka Archive cites a
2-generated group constructed in Section 7 of Ershov and Jaikin-Zapirain (2013), which is infinite
and has exactly three maximal subgroups, each of index 2.

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Archive of Solved Problems, Problem 17.17 (G. M. Bergman); resolution: M. Ershov and A. Jaikin-Zapirain, J. Reine Angew. Math. 677 (2013), 71-134, Kourovka Archive, Problem 17.17 (No, it need not: a 2-generated 2-LERF group in Section 7 of Ershov-Jaikin-Zapirain is an infinite group with 3 maximal subgroups, all of index 2).

articles.title: Bergman's question for three maximal subgroups
articles.statement:
Kourovka 17.17 (G. M. Bergman) asks
whether a finitely generated group with only finitely many maximal subgroups must be finite. This
is the case of three maximal subgroups, which the problem singles out: every finitely generated
group with exactly three maximal subgroups is finite.

articles.title: Fitting subgroup
articles.statement:
The Fitting subgroup `F(G)`: the join of the nilpotent normal subgroups of `G` (for finite `G`
the largest nilpotent normal subgroup).

articles.title: Subgroup generated by the inclusion-minimal triple intersections
articles.statement:
For subgroups $A$, $B$,
$C$ of a group $G$, the subgroup $\mathrm{Min}_G(A, B, C)$ is the subgroup of $G$ generated by
those intersections $A \cap xBx^{-1} \cap yCy^{-1}$ ($x, y \in G$) that are minimal by inclusion
among all such intersections, that is, that contain no other intersection of this form.

articles.title: Inclusion-minimal triple intersections need not lie in the Fitting subgroup
articles.statement:
It is not true
that for every finite soluble group $G$ and all nilpotent subgroups $A$, $B$, $C$ of $G$, the
subgroup $\mathrm{Min}_G(A, B, C)$ generated by those intersections
$A \cap xBx^{-1} \cap yCy^{-1}$ ($x, y \in G$) that are minimal by inclusion among all such
intersections is contained in the Fitting subgroup $F(G)$, the join of all nilpotent normal
subgroups of $G$.

Kinyon and Urban (Section 3.38) give a soluble group $G$ of order $36864$ with nilpotent subgroups
$A$ of order $16$ and $B = C$ of order $2048$ such that $\mathrm{Min}_G(A, B, B) = A$ while $F(G)$
does not contain $A$. Since this group is soluble, it answers part (c), and hence part (b), in the
negative.

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Problem 20.122 (V. I. Zenkov); resolution: M. Kinyon and J. Urban, Results on problems from the Kourovka Notebook, preprint, version 4, 19 September 2026, Kinyon-Urban, Section 3.38 (Problem 20.122(a)-(c)): G = E ⋊ Q soluble of order 512 · 72 = 36864, A = Z × H of order 16 and B = C the stabilizer of order 2048 are nilpotent, min_G(A, B, B) = Min_G(A, B, B) = A and F(G) = E does not contain A; the Kourovka Notebook (21st issue) marks 20.122 solved, "No, it is not always true in all three cases" (AI solution confirmed by V. I. Zenkov), https://kourovkanotebookorg.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/kourovka-mathematics.pdf.

articles.title: Inclusion-minimal triple intersections and the Fitting subgroup (Kourovka 20.122(b), (c))
articles.statement:
The statement that for every finite soluble group $G$ and all nilpotent subgroups $A$, $B$, $C$ of
$G$, the subgroup $\mathrm{Min}_G(A, B, C)$ generated by those intersections
$A \cap xBx^{-1} \cap yCy^{-1}$ ($x, y \in G$) that are minimal by inclusion among all such
intersections is contained in the Fitting subgroup $F(G)$, the join of all nilpotent normal
subgroups of $G$.

articles.title: Nilpotent injector
articles.statement:
A subgroup $H$ of a group $G$ is a nilpotent injector when, for every
subnormal subgroup $K$ of $G$, the intersection $H \cap K$ is nilpotent and is a maximal nilpotent
subgroup of $K$: every nilpotent subgroup $L$ of $G$ with $H \cap K \le L \le K$ equals
$H \cap K$.

articles.title: Subgroup generated by the triple intersections of least order
articles.statement:
For subgroups $A$, $B$, $C$
of a group $G$, the subgroup $\min_G(A, B, C)$ is the subgroup of $G$ generated by those
intersections $A \cap xBx^{-1} \cap yCy^{-1}$ ($x, y \in G$) whose order is at most the order of
every such intersection.

Orders are taken as natural numbers, so an infinite subgroup counts as having order $0$; the
notion is intended for finite $G$.

articles.title: Minimal-order triple intersections need not lie in the Fitting subgroup
articles.statement:
It is not true that
for every finite soluble group $G$ and all nilpotent subgroups $A$, $B$, $C$ of $G$, the subgroup
$\min_G(A, B, C)$ generated by the intersections $A \cap xBx^{-1} \cap yCy^{-1}$ ($x, y \in G$)
of least order is contained in the Fitting subgroup $F(G)$, the join of all nilpotent normal
subgroups of $G$.

Kinyon and Urban (Section 3.38) give a soluble group $G$ of order $36864$ with nilpotent subgroups
$A$ of order $16$ and $B = C$ of order $2048$ such that $\min_G(A, B, B) = A$ while $F(G)$ does not
contain $A$. Since this group is soluble, it answers part (c), and hence part (a), in the negative.

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Problem 20.122 (V. I. Zenkov); resolution: M. Kinyon and J. Urban, Results on problems from the Kourovka Notebook, preprint, version 4, 19 September 2026, Kinyon-Urban, Section 3.38 (Problem 20.122(a)-(c)): G = E ⋊ Q soluble of order 512 · 72 = 36864, A = Z × H of order 16 and B = C the stabilizer of order 2048 are nilpotent, min_G(A, B, B) = Min_G(A, B, B) = A and F(G) = E does not contain A; the Kourovka Notebook (21st issue) marks 20.122 solved, "No, it is not always true in all three cases" (AI solution confirmed by V. I. Zenkov), https://kourovkanotebookorg.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/kourovka-mathematics.pdf.

articles.title: Minimal-order triple intersections and the Fitting subgroup (Kourovka 20.122(a), (c))
articles.statement:
The
statement that for every finite soluble group $G$ and all nilpotent subgroups $A$, $B$, $C$ of $G$,
the subgroup $\min_G(A, B, C)$ generated by the intersections $A \cap xBx^{-1} \cap yCy^{-1}$
($x, y \in G$) of least order is contained in the Fitting subgroup $F(G)$, the join of all
nilpotent normal subgroups of $G$.

The question is due to V. I. Zenkov.

articles.title: Boundedly many conjugates of a nilpotent injector meet in the Fitting subgroup
articles.statement:
There is a
natural number $k$ such that for every finite group $G$ and every nilpotent injector $H$ of $G$
there are elements $g_1, \dots, g_k \in G$, not necessarily distinct, with
$g_1 H g_1^{-1} \cap \dots \cap g_k H g_k^{-1} = F(G)$, where $F(G)$ is the Fitting subgroup of
$G$.

Zenkov proved, using the classification of finite simple groups, that $k = 3$ works, which answers
Kourovka Problem 19.37(a) positively.

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Archive of Solved Problems, Problem 19.37 (S. F. Kamornikov); resolution: V. I. Zenkov, Intersections of three nilpotent subgroups in a finite group, Siberian Math. J. 62 (2021), no. 4, 621-637, doi:10.1134/S0037446621040066, Kourovka Archive, Problem 19.37: Yes, one can choose k = 3 as such a constant, mod CFSG, https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v49.

articles.title: Kourovka Problem 19.37(a)
articles.statement:
The assertion that there is a natural number $k$ such that for
every finite group $G$ and every nilpotent injector $H$ of $G$ there are elements
$g_1, \dots, g_k \in G$, not necessarily distinct, with
$g_1 H g_1^{-1} \cap \dots \cap g_k H g_k^{-1} = F(G)$, where $F(G)$ is the Fitting subgroup of
$G$.

articles.title: Three conjugates of a nilpotent injector meet in the Fitting subgroup
articles.statement:
For every finite group
$G$ and every nilpotent injector $H$ of $G$ there are elements $g_1, g_2, g_3 \in G$, not
necessarily distinct, with $g_1 H g_1^{-1} \cap g_2 H g_2^{-1} \cap g_3 H g_3^{-1} = F(G)$, where
$F(G)$ is the Fitting subgroup of $G$.

This answers Kourovka Problem 19.37(b) positively; it is due to Zenkov and uses the classification
of finite simple groups, the soluble case being due to Passman and Mann.

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Archive of Solved Problems, Problem 19.37 (S. F. Kamornikov); resolution: V. I. Zenkov, Intersections of three nilpotent subgroups in a finite group, Siberian Math. J. 62 (2021), no. 4, 621-637, doi:10.1134/S0037446621040066, Kourovka Archive, Problem 19.37: Yes, one can choose k = 3 as such a constant, mod CFSG, https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v49.

articles.title: Kourovka Problem 19.37(b)
articles.statement:
The assertion that for every finite group $G$ and every
nilpotent injector $H$ of $G$ there are elements $g_1, g_2, g_3 \in G$, not necessarily distinct,
with $g_1 H g_1^{-1} \cap g_2 H g_2^{-1} \cap g_3 H g_3^{-1} = F(G)$, where $F(G)$ is the Fitting
subgroup of $G$.

articles.title: Nilpotent subgroups of a finite simple group have conjugates meeting trivially
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a
finite non-abelian simple group and let $A$ and $B$ be nilpotent subgroups of $G$. Then there is
$x \in G$ with $A \cap x B x^{-1} = 1$.

Burness and Huang proved this (for alternating groups using work of Kurmazov and Zenkov); the case
$A = B$ answers Kourovka Problem 15.40 positively.

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Problem 15.40 (E. P. Vdovin); resolution: T. C. Burness and H. Y. Huang, On the intersections of nilpotent subgroups in simple groups, arXiv:2508.03479 (2025), abstract (Vdovin's conjecture and its stronger form: A ∩ B^x = 1 for nilpotent subgroups A, B of a simple group, combined with work of Kurmazov and Zenkov on alternating groups); the Kourovka Notebook (21st issue) marks 15.40 solved, https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.03479.

articles.title: Kourovka Problem 15.40
articles.statement:
The assertion, in the two-subgroup form of its resolution, that for
every finite non-abelian simple group $G$ and all nilpotent subgroups $A$ and $B$ of $G$ there is
$x \in G$ with $A \cap x B x^{-1} = 1$.

The case $A = B$ is the problem as posed.

articles.title: Three conjugates of a nilpotent subgroup meet inside the Fitting subgroup
articles.statement:
For every finite
group $G$ and every nilpotent subgroup $N$ of $G$ there are $x, y \in G$ with
$N \cap x N x^{-1} \cap y N y^{-1} \le F(G)$, where $F(G)$ is the Fitting subgroup of $G$.

This answers Kourovka Problem 17.40 positively; it is due to Zenkov (2021) and uses the
classification of finite simple groups.

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Archive of Solved Problems, Problem 17.40 (E. P. Vdovin); resolution: V. I. Zenkov, Siberian Math. J. 62 (2021), 621-637, Kourovka Archive, Problem 17.40 (Yes, such elements always exist, mod CFSG).

articles.title: Kourovka Problem 17.40
articles.statement:
The assertion that for every finite group $G$ and every nilpotent
subgroup $N$ of $G$ there are $x, y \in G$ with $N \cap x N x^{-1} \cap y N y^{-1} \le F(G)$, where
$F(G)$ is the Fitting subgroup of $G$.

articles.title: Triple intersections with conjugates
articles.statement:
For subgroups $A$, $B$, $C$ of a group $G$, this is
the set of all subgroups of $G$ of the form $A \cap xBx^{-1} \cap yCy^{-1}$ with $x, y \in G$,
that is, the intersections of $A$ with a conjugate of $B$ and a conjugate of $C$.

articles.title: Lattices of centralizers need not be modular (Kourovka 11.4)
articles.statement:
Call a subgroup of a group
$G$ a centralizer if it equals $C_G(X)$ for some subset $X \subseteq G$. Modularity of centralizer
sublattices fails: there is a group $G$ in which the join (in the subgroup lattice) of any two
centralizers is again a centralizer, but which has centralizers $A$, $B$, $C$ with $A \le C$ and
$(A \sqcup B) \sqcap C \ne A \sqcup (B \sqcap C)$, where $\sqcup$ and $\sqcap$ are the join and meet
in the subgroup lattice of $G$.

The Kourovka Archive answers 11.4 "No, not always" (Obraztsov); for finite groups the answer is
yes.

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Archive of Solved Problems, Problem 11.4 (V. A. Antonov); resolution: V. N. Obraztsov, J. Algebra 199, no. 1 (1998), 337-343, Kourovka Archive, Problem 11.4: "No, not always", https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v49.

articles.title: Modularity of centralizer sublattices (Kourovka 11.4)
articles.statement:
Call a subgroup of a group $G$ a
centralizer if it equals $C_G(X)$ for some subset $X \subseteq G$. This is the proposition that for
every group $G$ in which the join (in the subgroup lattice) of any two centralizers is again a
centralizer, any three centralizers $A$, $B$, $C$ of $G$ with $A \le C$ satisfy the modular law
$(A \sqcup B) \sqcap C = A \sqcup (B \sqcap C)$, where $\sqcup$ and $\sqcap$ are the join and meet
in the subgroup lattice of $G$.

Centralizers are always closed under intersection, so the hypothesis says that they form a
sublattice of the subgroup lattice. The question is due to V. A. Antonov.

articles.title: Centralizer subgroups
articles.statement:
A subgroup $H$ of a group $G$ is a centralizer if $H = C_G(X)$ for
some subset $X \subseteq G$, where $C_G(X)$ is the subgroup of elements of $G$ that commute with
every element of $X$.

articles.title: Zenkov–Monakhov–Revin theorem (Kourovka 14.62)
articles.statement:
For every finite group $G$ and every
non-soluble normal subgroup $H$ of $G$ there is a maximal soluble subgroup $S$ of $H$ (a soluble
subgroup $S \le H$ contained in no strictly larger soluble subgroup of $H$) such that
$G = H\,N_G(S)$, where $N_G(S)$ is the normalizer of $S$ in $G$; since $H$ is normal, this says
that $H$ and $N_G(S)$ generate $G$.

Zenkov, Monakhov and Revin proved this using the classification of finite simple groups, so the
Kourovka Archive answers 14.62 "Yes, it always exists".

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Archive of Solved Problems, Problem 14.62 (V. S. Monakhov); resolution: V. I. Zenkov, V. S. Monakhov and D. O. Revin, Algebra and Logic 43 (2004), no. 2, 102-108 (using the classification of finite simple groups), Kourovka Archive, Problem 14.62 (answer: Yes, it always exists mod CFSG).

articles.title: Kourovka 14.62: a maximal soluble subgroup whose normalizer supplements
articles.statement:
The proposition
that for every finite group $G$ and every non-soluble normal subgroup $H$ of $G$ there is
a maximal soluble subgroup $S$ of $H$ (a soluble subgroup $S \le H$ contained in no strictly
larger soluble subgroup of $H$) such that $G = H\,N_G(S)$, where $N_G(S)$ is the normalizer of $S$
in $G$; since $H$ is normal, this says that $H$ and $N_G(S)$ generate $G$.

articles.title: Permutable subgroups of large alternating groups are trivial or the whole group
articles.statement:
There is a
natural number $n$ such that for every $m > n$, every $A_m$-permutable subgroup of the alternating
group $A_m$ is either the trivial subgroup or $A_m$ itself. Here a subgroup $A$ of a group $G$ is
$G$-permutable when for every subgroup $B$ of $G$ there is $x \in G$ with $A B^x = B^x A$, where
$B^x = x B x^{-1}$.

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Problem 17.37 (A. F. Vasil'ev, A. N. Skiba); resolution: N. Yang and A. Galt, Bull. Malays. Math. Sci. Soc. (2) 46 (2023), no. 5, Paper no. 177, as stated in S. Zhang, Ordinary G-permutable subgroups of finite simple groups, preprint, arXiv:2610.12329 (2026), Zhang, Introduction (Yang and Galt proved that there is N ≥ 7 such that no A_n with n ≥ N has a proper nontrivial A_n-permutable subgroup, with A_n-permutable as in Problem 17.112); the Kourovka Notebook (21st issue) marks 17.37 solved (Yes, there is), https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12329.

articles.title: Kourovka Problem 17.37 on permutable subgroups of alternating groups
articles.statement:
This proposition
asserts that there is a natural number $n$ such that for every $m > n$, every $A_m$-permutable
subgroup of the alternating group $A_m$ is either the trivial subgroup or $A_m$ itself. Here a
subgroup $A$ of a group $G$ is $G$-permutable when for every subgroup $B$ of $G$ there is $x \in G$
with $A B^x = B^x A$, where $B^x = x B x^{-1}$ is the conjugate of $B$ by $x$ and products of
subgroups are products of subsets of $G$.

The trivial subgroup and $A_m$ itself are always $A_m$-permutable.

articles.title: $G$-permutable subgroups
articles.statement:
A subgroup $A$ of a group $G$ is $G$-permutable when for every
subgroup $B$ of $G$ there is $x \in G$ such that $A B^x = B^x A$, where $B^x = x B x^{-1}$ is the
conjugate of $B$ by $x$ and the products are products of subsets of $G$.

articles.title: Conjugate subgroup
articles.statement:
For a subgroup $A$ of a group $G$ and an element $x \in G$, the
conjugate subgroup is $A^x = x^{-1} A x = \{x^{-1} a x : a \in A\}$.

articles.title: Paranormal subgroup
articles.statement:
A subgroup $A$ of a group $G$ is paranormal (Z. I. Borevich) when,
for every $x \in G$, the conjugate $A^x = x^{-1} A x$ is contained in the subgroup generated by
the conjugates $A^u$ with $u$ in the subgroup $\langle A, A^x \rangle$ generated by $A$ and
$A^x$.

articles.title: Polynormal subgroup
articles.statement:
A subgroup $A$ of a group $G$ is polynormal (Z. I. Borevich) when,
for every $x \in G$, the conjugate $A^x = x^{-1} A x$ is contained in the subgroup generated by
the conjugates $A^u$ with $u \in A^{\langle x \rangle}$, where $A^{\langle x \rangle}$ is the
subgroup generated by the conjugates $A^{x^n}$ with $n \in \mathbb{Z}$.

articles.title: A polynormal subgroup that is not paranormal (Kourovka 14.50 refuted)
articles.statement:
There is a finite
group $G$ with a subgroup $A$ that is polynormal but not paranormal. So the conjecture of
Kourovka Problem 14.50 is false.

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Archive of Solved Problems, Problem 14.50 (Z. I. Borevich; A. S. Kondratiev); resolution: V. I. Mysovskikh, Dokl. Math. 60 (1999), 71-72, Kourovka Archive, Problem 14.50 (answer: Not always).

articles.title: Polynormal subgroups of finite groups are paranormal
articles.statement:
Kourovka 14.50 (Z. I. Borevich; A. S. Kondratiev): every polynormal subgroup of a finite group
is paranormal.

articles.title: An infinite group without nontrivial proper pronormal subgroups exists
articles.statement:
There is an infinite
group $G$ in which every pronormal subgroup is trivial or equal to $G$. Here a subgroup $H$ of $G$
is pronormal when, for every $g \in G$, the subgroups $H$ and $H^g = gHg^{-1}$ are conjugate by an
element of $\langle H, H^g \rangle$. This answers Kourovka Problem 19.74 in the affirmative.

Corson constructs an infinite simple group with no proper abnormal subgroup, which the problem
states is equivalent (the normalizer of a pronormal subgroup is abnormal); the 21st issue of the
Kourovka Notebook marks 19.74 solved ("Yes, it does").

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Problem 19.74 (D. O. Revin); resolution: S. M. Corson, Infinite simple groups with no proper abnormal subgroups, Monatsh. Math. (2025), doi:10.1007/s00605-025-02116-8 (arXiv:2505.07330), Theorem 1: there is an infinite group that is simple, torsion-free, has no maximal subgroup and has no proper abnormal subgroup, answering Revin's problem; the Kourovka Notebook (21st issue) marks 19.74 solved: Yes, it does (the problem states the equivalent form: an infinite simple group without proper abnormal subgroups), https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.07330.

articles.title: Infinite groups without nontrivial proper pronormal subgroups (Kourovka 19.74, Revin)
articles.statement:
The statement that there is an infinite group $G$ in which every pronormal subgroup is trivial or
equal to $G$. Here a subgroup $H$ of $G$ is pronormal when, for every $g \in G$, the subgroups $H$
and $H^g = gHg^{-1}$ are conjugate by an element of $\langle H, H^g \rangle$.

articles.title: Propermutable subgroups
articles.statement:
A subgroup $H$ of a group $G$ is propermutable in $G$ when there
is a subgroup $B$ of $G$ with $G = N_G(H)B$ (every element of $G$ is a product $nb$ with $n$ in
the normalizer $N_G(H)$ of $H$ and $b \in B$) such that $H$ permutes with every subgroup $X$ of
$B$, that is, $HX = XH$.

articles.title: 2-nilpotent groups
articles.statement:
A group $G$ is $2$-nilpotent when it has a normal subgroup $N$ of
finite odd order whose index in $G$ is $2^k$ for some natural number $k$.

articles.title: Permuting subgroups
articles.statement:
Let $H$ and $X$ be subgroups of a group $G$. Then $H$ permutes
with $X$ when $HX = XH$ as subsets of $G$, where $HX = \{hx : h \in H, x \in X\}$ and
$XH = \{xh : x \in X, h \in H\}$.

articles.title: Propermutability is not inherited by intermediate subgroups
articles.statement:
There exist a finite group $G$
and subgroups $A \le B \le G$ such that $A$ is propermutable in $G$ but $A$, regarded as a
subgroup of $B$, is not propermutable in $B$. This is the positive answer to
Kourovka Problem 18.91(a).

The Kourovka Archive answers 18.91(a) "Yes, there is" (A. A. Pypka and D. Yu. Storozhenko, 2017).

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Archive of Solved Problems, Problem 18.91 (A. N. Skiba); resolution: (a) A. A. Pypka and D. Yu. Storozhenko, Dopov. Nac. Akad. Nauk Ukrain. 2017, no. 7, 18-20 (Ukrainian); (b) Kh. A. Al-Sharo, Finite groups with given systems of weakly S-propermutable subgroups, J. Group Theory 19 (2016), no. 5, 871-887, Kourovka Archive, Problem 18.91: a) Yes, there is; b) Yes, it is. Al-Sharo, Corollary 1.3: if X ⊴ G, P ∈ Syl_p(X), (p - 1, |X|) = 1, and for some 1 < D < P every subgroup of P of order |D| (and, when P is non-abelian and |D| = 2, every cyclic subgroup of order 4) is S-propermutable in G, then X is p-nilpotent, https://doi.org/10.1515/jgth-2016-0017.

articles.title: Kourovka Problem 18.91(a) (statement)
articles.statement:
The statement of Kourovka Problem 18.91(a)
(A. N. Skiba): there exist a finite group $G$ and subgroups $A \le B \le G$ such that $A$ is
propermutable in $G$ but $A$, regarded as a subgroup of $B$, is not propermutable in $B$.

articles.title: Propermutable subgroups of a non-abelian Sylow 2-subgroup force 2-nilpotency
articles.statement:
Let $G$
be a finite group and $P$ a non-abelian Sylow $2$-subgroup of $G$, with $|P| = 2^n$, and let $k$
be a natural number with $1 \le k < n$. If every subgroup of $P$ of order $2^k$ is propermutable
in $G$, and, when $k = 1$, every cyclic subgroup of $P$ of order $4$ is propermutable in $G$, then
$G$ is $2$-nilpotent. This is the positive answer to Kourovka Problem 18.91(b).

The Kourovka Archive answers 18.91(b) "Yes, it is" (Kh. A. Al-Sharo, 2016). Al-Sharo's
Corollary 1.3 (quoted below), applied to the normal subgroup $X = G$ with $p = 2$ (where
$(p - 1, |G|) = 1$ holds), gives 2-nilpotency already when the subgroups in question are only
$S$-propermutable, a weaker condition than propermutability: a subgroup $H$ of $G$ is
$S$-propermutable in $G$ when there is a subgroup $B$ of $G$ with $G = N_G(H)B$ such that $H$
permutes with every Sylow subgroup of $B$.

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Archive of Solved Problems, Problem 18.91 (A. N. Skiba); resolution: (a) A. A. Pypka and D. Yu. Storozhenko, Dopov. Nac. Akad. Nauk Ukrain. 2017, no. 7, 18-20 (Ukrainian); (b) Kh. A. Al-Sharo, Finite groups with given systems of weakly S-propermutable subgroups, J. Group Theory 19 (2016), no. 5, 871-887, Kourovka Archive, Problem 18.91: a) Yes, there is; b) Yes, it is. Al-Sharo, Corollary 1.3: if X ⊴ G, P ∈ Syl_p(X), (p - 1, |X|) = 1, and for some 1 < D < P every subgroup of P of order |D| (and, when P is non-abelian and |D| = 2, every cyclic subgroup of order 4) is S-propermutable in G, then X is p-nilpotent, https://doi.org/10.1515/jgth-2016-0017.

articles.title: Kourovka Problem 18.91(b) (statement)
articles.statement:
The statement of Kourovka Problem 18.91(b)
(A. N. Skiba), with the range $1 \le k < n$: let $G$ be a finite group and $P$ a non-abelian
Sylow $2$-subgroup of $G$, with $|P| = 2^n$, and let $k$ be a natural number with $1 \le k < n$.
If every subgroup of $P$ of order $2^k$ is propermutable in $G$, and, when $k = 1$, every cyclic
subgroup of $P$ of order $4$ is propermutable in $G$, then $G$ is $2$-nilpotent.

The printed problem has $1 < k < n$, which contradicts its clause for $k = 1$; the range
$1 \le k < n$ is the one of Al-Sharo's Corollary 1.3.

articles.title: Subgroup lattices of Chernikov groups without a quasicyclic square have finite dimension
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a Chernikov group, that is, a group with a normal subgroup of finite index isomorphic to
a direct product of finitely many quasicyclic groups (infinite abelian groups all of whose proper
subgroups are finite). Suppose that $G$ does not contain a direct product of two quasicyclic groups
over the same prime: there is no quasicyclic group $Q$ with an injective homomorphism
$Q \times Q \to G$. Then the lattice of subgroups of $G$ has finite order dimension: the inclusion
order on the subgroups of $G$ is the intersection of finitely many linear orders on that set.

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Problem 11.116 (L. N. Shevrin); resolution: M. Kinyon and J. Urban (with Codex gpt-6-astra), Results on problems from the Kourovka Notebook, preprint, version 4 (19 September 2026), Section 3.9: if `D ⊴ G` has index `m` and `D = C_{p₁^∞} × ⋯ × C_{p_r^∞}` with distinct primes, the subgroup lattice of `G` embeds in a product of `2rm` chains, so its order dimension is at most `2rm`; the Kourovka Notebook (21st issue) marks 11.116 solved (AI solution confirmed by P. Shumyatsky), https://kourovkanotebookorg.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/kourovka-mathematics.pdf.

articles.title: Shevrin's problem on the dimension of subgroup lattices of Chernikov groups
articles.statement:
The
proposition that for every Chernikov group $G$ that does not contain a direct product of two
quasicyclic groups over the same prime (that is, there is no quasicyclic group $Q$ with an
injective homomorphism $Q \times Q \to G$), the lattice of subgroups of $G$ has finite order
dimension: the inclusion order on the subgroups of $G$ is the intersection of finitely many linear
orders on that set. This is Kourovka Problem 11.116 (L. N. Shevrin).

articles.title: Groups containing the square of a quasicyclic group
articles.statement:
A group $G$ contains a direct product
of two quasicyclic groups over the same prime when there are a quasicyclic group $Q$ and an
injective group homomorphism $Q \times Q \to G$ (quasicyclic groups over the same prime are
isomorphic).

articles.title: Poset of finite order dimension
articles.statement:
A partially ordered set has finite (order) dimension: its order relation is the intersection
of finitely many linear orders on the same set.

articles.title: Chernikov group
articles.statement:
